Loop is now 5-for-6 on field-goal attempts and 11-for-11 on extra-point tries in 2026. The Ravens are fifth in scoring at 30.7 points per game, so he should continue earning plenty of opportunities for one of the best offenses in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Loop and the Ravens pay a visit to the surging Falcons for a Week 5 interconference clash on Sunday Night Football. The second-year kicker went 1-for-2 on field-goal attempts and connected on all three PATs during Baltimore's 24-18 win in Week 4. Loop missed his second field goal of the season but set a new career high with his make from 64 yards out, and he's now 6-for-8 on field goals and a perfect 14-for-14 on extra points. Atlanta has scored the most points in the league over its last two games (80), meaning Loop and the Ravens will have to keep up in a potential high-scoring game.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tyler Loop and the Ravens travel to square off against the division-rival Browns in Week 6. He made all three of his field-goal attempts and his lone PAT during Baltimore's 30-23 overtime victory in Week 5. Two of Loop's makes came from 50-plus yards, and he's now 5-for-5 on kicks from that distance this season and 9-for-11 on field goals overall. He's turning into a very reliable fantasy asset for a Ravens team that scores 29.2 points per game, making him a strong play against Cleveland.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tyler Loop and the Ravens host the division-rival Bengals for a Week 7 showdown. He finished 1-for-2 on field-goal attempts and converted his lone PAT during Baltimore's 13-10 loss in Week 6. Through six contests this season, Loop is 10-for-13 (76.9%) on field goals and a perfect 16-for-16 on extra-point tries. He has three outings with 100% accuracy and three with 50% accuracy, making him an inconsistent fantasy option despite kicking for a Ravens offense that scores 26.0 points per game, which ranks seventh so far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tyler Loop and the Ravens visit the 5-1 Bills in Week 8. He connected on both of his field-goal attempts and his lone PAT during Baltimore's 35-13 loss in Week 7. Following a 30-point outing in an overtime victory in Week 5, the Ravens' offense has struggled mightily over the last two games, combining for just 23 points over that stretch. However, with Lamar Jackson (ankle) progressing toward a return from a three-game absence, Loop could have more opportunities to score versus a Bills defense allowing 28.5 points per contest, the third-most in the NFL.

outlooksByWeek.2: Deebo Samuel will look to build upon a strong season-opening performance when the 49ers face Miami in Week 2. In Samuel's return to San Francisco following a one-year hiatus, he caught six of seven targets for 48 yards and a touchdown in last Thursday's win over the Rams. Samuel and Mike Evans finished with nearly identical receiving lines, suggesting that both veteran wideouts can thrive with QB Brock Purdy. The Dolphins were beat handily by the Raiders in Week 1 while giving up three TDs through the air (though two were to RB Ashton Jeanty).
outlooksByWeek.3: Deebo Samuel is coming off a quiet game heading into San Francisco's Week 3 matchup against the Cardinals. Samuel caught three passes for 31 yards and rushed once for four yards in Sunday's rout of Miami. However, fellow wideouts Demarcus Robinson (ankle) and Mike Evans (hip) both exited that contest due to injury, and though early reports suggest Evans should be fine for Week 3, Samuel could see more looks come his way given his comparatively good health. Arizona has given up the sixth-most fantasy points per game to wideouts so far this year and was just torched by Seattle's Jaxon Smith-Njigba (9-155-3 receiving line) on Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.4: Deebo Samuel could take on the 49ers' No. 1 WR role in Week 4 against Denver if Mike Evans (ribs/oblique) is unable to play. Though Evans left in the second quarter in this past Sunday's win over Arizona, Samuel ended the contest without seeing a target. However, he still had a good fantasy line thanks to an 80-yard TD on a hook-and-ladder play, and Samuel also gained 14 yards on two carries. Should Evans be unable to suit up against Denver, Samuel could face the daunting task of trying to beat star cornerback Patrick Surtain.
outlooksByWeek.5: Deebo Samuel has been a versatile cog for the 49ers heading into a Week 5 matchup against Seattle. Samuel has scored three receiving TDs though four games, and he's also racked up 185 receiving yards, 74 rushing yads and 231 kick-return yards. The veteran wideout has drawn a modest 17 targets so far, but he's been very efficient in hauling in 14 of them. San Francisco may look to use Samuel creatively against a Seahawks defense that is allowing just 246.8 yards per game this season, fewest in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Deebo Samuel is dealing with a hamstring injury and may not be able to play in San Francisco's Week 6 matchup against Washington. Samuel was hurt in the third quarter of this past Sunday's win over Seattle and was quickly ruled out. The veteran receiver is slated for imaging, which should provide clarity about the extent of the injury and a potential return timeline. If Samuel can't play in Week 6, he'll miss the opportunity to feast on a Commanders defense that has struggled mightily against the pass this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Deebo Samuel and the 49ers travel to face the Falcons in Week 7. The veteran receiver missed San Francisco's 23-17 victory in Week 6 with a hamstring injury he suffered in Week 5. Head coach Kyle Shanahan stated they would "hold off" on placing him on injured reserve with the Week 8 bye approaching, so it sounds like Samuel is in jeopardy of missing the road tilt against Atlanta. Expect him to work towards a Week 9 return, as long as he doesn't suffer any sort of setback.

player.seasonOutlook: Samuel reunited with the 49ers in July after solid yet unspectacular lone season in Washington. The former second-round pick cleared 85 touches and 800 scrimmage yards for the fifth consecutive season and finished 25th among receivers in fantasy points -- his third-career top-30 fantasy campaign. Samuel's role as a short-area target and occasional rusher gets the ball in his hands plenty (he's ranked in the top 15 among WRs in touches and RAC five years in a row), but it doesn't allow him much scoring upside (10 TDs over the last two years, and he's never cleared five end zone targets in one season). Now 30 years old, Samuel figures to resume his role as a short-area playmaker in Kyle Shanahan's highly-efficient offense. He's a fine late-round flier with WR3/flex upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Matthew Golden should remain a top look in Green Bay's passing offense in Week 2 against the Jets. Golden led the Packers in routes (40) and targets (12) in Week 1 against Minnesota, and he converted six catches for 95 yards. He already looks to have a big enough role for a second-year jump, and the pass-heavy nature of Green Bay's offense helps his case even more. He'll face a Jets secondary that allowed a middle-of-the-pack 26.4 PPR points to wide receivers in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Matthew Golden will remain a top option for Jordan Love as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Golden led Green Bay in receiving yards against the Jets in Week 2, catching four of six targets for 58 yards. The second-year wide receiver is also now set to take on a larger role, at least in the short term, with Jayden Reed looking to miss some time with a neck injury.  Golden will look to expand on his 10-153-0 receiving line against an Atlanta defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 30.3 PPR points per game to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Matthew Golden will aim to keep it rolling as the Packers play the Buccaneers in Week 4. Golden led Green Bay in receiving yards and targets in Week 3 against the Falcons, catching five of 12 targets for 100 yards and a touchdown. The second-year wide receiver is in the middle of a breakout season, outpacing more than half of his 2025 output in just the first three games of this year. He'll take on a Tampa Bay defense that's allowed a top-ten 25.4 fantasy points per game to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Matthew Golden will look to do more as the Packers play the Bears in Week 5. Golden finished Week 4 against the Buccaneers with a season-low three catches for 21 yards, but he was able to salvage his performance with a touchdown. The second-year pass catcher remains a top option for quarterback Jordan Love, and he has an 18-274-2 receiving line through four games. Golden will be a major factor in Green Bay's success against their big rival, but he will face a Chicago defense that's ranked top five in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.6: Matthew Golden will aim to stay hot as the Packers play the Cowboys in Week 6. Golden finished Week 5 versus the Bears with the highest yardage total of his career, reeling in six catches for 123 yards. The second-year pass catcher has continued to squash bust projections every week this season, with 24 catches for 297 yards and two touchdowns across five outings. He'll face a Dallas defense that's fared even worse against wide receivers, ranking 21st in fantasy points allowed to the position so far.
outlooksByWeek.7: Matthew Golden will look to build off another statement performance as the Packers play the Lions in Week 7. Golden brought in six of 13 targets for 104 yards and a touchdown in a Week 6 win over the Cowboys, which could have been more if not for a pair of dropped touchdowns. The second-year wideout has now recorded a 30-501-3 receiving line off a team-high 57 targets, and he's already outpaced all of his 2025 output in just six games this season. He'll take on a Detroit defense that's ranked 30th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Matthew Golden will look to bounce back as the Packers play the Panthers in Week 8. Golden wasn't abysmal in a Week 7 loss to the Lions, but he logged a season-low 39 yards on six catches. The second-year pass catcher has still totaled 36 grabs for 540 yards and three touchdowns across the seven games of the season, completely obliterating his 39-361-0 receiving line from the 2025 season across 14 games. He'll face a Carolina defense that's ranked a tough fifth in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.

player.seasonOutlook: Golden is eyeing a Year 2 leap following a disappointing rookie season in which he was limited to 39 touches and failed to find the end zone in 14 regular-season games. Golden was limited to 53% of the snaps and never cleared six targets in a single outing. Some optimism was generated from Golden's 4-84-1 receiving line in the playoff loss to Chicago, but even with Romeo Doubs and Dontayvion Wicks gone, it's unclear if he will actually see a big boost in usage in Matt LaFleur's offense considering that no Green Bay receiver has cleared a 21% target share since Davante Adams' departure prior to 2022. The speedy Golden, who also contributes as a rusher, is a recent first-round pick entering his second season. He's worth a speculative middle-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: J.K. Dobbins wasn't a big part of the Broncos' game plan in their season-opening loss to Kansas City, as the veteran running back had only eight carries for 36 yards. RJ Harvey's volume was similar, with seven touches to Dobbins' eight, but turnovers and game flow played a part in limiting their opportunities. Dobbins averaged over 80 scrimmage yards last season in the 10 regular-season games he was healthy, so better days should be ahead for Denver's lead back, although they may not come right away. In Week 2, he'll face a Jaguars defense that ranked third in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: J.K. Dobbins' workload has been limited to begin the season, with just 18 carries for 72 yards through the Broncos' first two games. The veteran back also has yet to see a target, as RJ Harvey and rookie Jonah Coleman have been prioritized as pass-catchers. Dobbins picked up a minor hamstring injury in Week 2's win over the Jaguars, but the issue isn't expected to keep him out of the lineup in Week 3. The same can't be said for Harvey, however, who didn't play at all in Week 2 due to his own hamstring strain. Dobbins could split touches with Coleman again in Week 3 against a Rams defense that just saw the return of Aaron Donald in Week 2 and has yet to allow a rushing TD this year.
outlooksByWeek.4: J.K. Dobbins is coming off his largest workload of the season in the Broncos' Week 3 win over the Rams. He had 17 carries and 18 total touches but turned them into just 53 scrimmage yards. Dobbins has struggled out of the gate, averaging just 3.5 yards per carry, but he should continue to handle the majority of the early-down work while rookie Jonah Coleman is on IR. RJ Harvey, who compiled 47 scrimmage yards on just eight touches against the Rams, remains the primary passing-down back. Dobbins will look for his first touchdown of 2026 in Week 4 against a 49ers defense that ranks 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: J.K. Dobbins continues to struggle as the primary early-down back for the Broncos. In a Week 4 loss to the 49ers, he managed just 40 rushing yards on 11 carries. This marks the fourth straight game to begin the season he's failed to reach 50 rushing yards or get into the end zone. Dobbins' 3.5 yards per carry would be a career low; he's never had a mark below 4.6 in any year he's played at least eight games. The veteran RB has at least stayed healthy, but that hasn't led to much production. He'll try to get going in Week 5 against a Chargers defense that ranks 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: J.K. Dobbins scored his first touchdown of the season in the Broncos' Week 5 win over the Chargers, while also producing season highs in touches (20) and rushing yards (68). The veteran running back was one of the few players to clearly benefit from Sean Payton's return to play-calling duties, but Dobbins still managed fairly modest numbers. He's been able to stay healthy so far in 2026, but through five games he's averaged just 3.6 yards per carry, a mark that would be a career low if it doesn't improve. Dobbins will take on a Seahawks defense in Week 6 that's tied for 16th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs, but which has yet to allow any back to reach 70 rushing yards in a game.
outlooksByWeek.7: J.K. Dobbins scored a rushing touchdown for a second straight game in the Broncos' overtime win over the Seahawks in Week 6. The veteran running back hasn't found much success overall in a struggling offense, averaging just 3.3 yards per carry with zero gains of 20-plus yards through six games, but his role as the goal-line back provides him with a consistent path to production. Dobbins is also more involved as a pass catcher in recent weeks, producing an 8-27-0 line while logging multiple targets in four straight weeks. He'll look to break out in Week 7 against a Cardinals defense that ranks 28th in rushing yards per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: J.K. Dobbins may be in danger of losing his spot in the Broncos' offense. During a Week 7 win over the Cardinals, rookie Jonah Coleman led the backfield with nine carries compared to Dobbins' six, and Coleman's 11 touches were also more than RJ Harvey's five. Both Dobbins and Harvey got into the end zone while Coleman didn't, suggesting that this could be turning into a full-blown committee. Dobbins doesn't contribute as a pass catcher the way Harvey does, so if he gets supplanted on early downs by Coleman, he may fade out of the game plan entirely. Dobbins will have trouble producing on limited volume in Week 8 versus a Kansas City defense that ranks seventh in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Dobbins re-signed with Denver and will attempt to fend off sophomore RJ Harvey for the team's lead-back job. With both active during Weeks 1-10 last season (10 games), Dobbins handled 153 carries (60% team share) and 15 targets (4%), compared to 50 carries (20%) and 29 targets (9%) for Harvey. Dobbins ran well (5.05 yards per carry) when healthy, but he was limited to four touchdowns and was a nonfactor as a receiver (37 yards on 15 targets) en route to averaging 11.6 fantasy points (27th). Dobbins enters his age-27 campaign having yet to play a full season in his career (seven-plus missed games in four of the past five years) and without much value even when active (he has never produced a top-20 fantasy campaign). Dobbins is an underwhelming flex option with added value in non-PPR formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Xavier Worthy captured three of his six Week 1 targets for only 18 yards. The workload was low, but Kansas City QB Patrick Mahomes completed only five passes to wideouts in the Monday night opener. The third-year pro has the speed to stretch the field, but he's generally used more underneath, along with occasionally carrying the ball. Worthy is a Week 2 flex option when the Chiefs host the Colts. Indianapolis was one of five defenses to allow over 300 yards passing in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Xavier Worthy scored his first touchdown of the season in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, snagging a one-yard toss from Patrick Mahomes in the second quarter. Worthy has notched steady target volume early in the season, with 13 total looks, but that has resulted in just an 8-43-1 line, and he has yet to get a carry. With Mahomes spreading the ball around and the offense prioritizing Kenneth Walker and the run game, Worthy will need some big plays to make a real fantasy contribution. The third-year speedster will face a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's given up five passing TDs through two games, but only one to a wide receiver.
outlooksByWeek.4: Xavier Worthy has struggled to break free for a big gain for Kansas City this season. The third-year speedster has managed just a 10-63-1 line on 15 targets, and surprisingly, he has yet to get a carry, perhaps to keep him healthy. Patrick Mahomes has also spread the ball around effectively, as Worthy, Travis Kelce, Rashee Rice, and Kenneth Walker all have between 15 and 18 targets, so a big volume increase isn't likely. Worthy faces a tough matchup in Week 4 against a Raiders secondary that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs and has yet to allow a TD to the position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Xavier Worthy comes out of Kansas City's Week 5 bye still looking to establish himself as a consistent part of the passing attack. With both Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton getting hurt during a Week 4 win over the Raiders, Worthy caught four of seven targets for a season-high 70 yards. Rice appears to be on track to return quickly, but Thornton is likely to miss the rest of the year, which could open up some downfield routes for Worthy. The third-year speedster will face a Chargers secondary in Week 6 that ranks 16th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Xavier Worthy is coming off his most productive game of the season, catching all seven of his targets for 73 yards in Kansas City's Week 6 win over the Chargers. With Rashee Rice sidelined, Worthy's volume has ticked up, but he hasn't been targeted more than seven times in a game this season. The third-year speedster also hasn't been able to break many big gains, with only one of his 21 catches going for 20-plus yards after nine of his 42 receptions in 2025 went for 20-plus. Worthy isn't likely to produce a ceiling game in Week 7 against a Seahawks secondary that ranks third in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Xavier Worthy struggled in Week 7 while filling in as Kansas City's No. 1 wide receiver, catching just three of six targets for 11 yards in a loss to the Seahawks. The third-year speedster has yet to reach 80 receiving yards this season, and it's looking increasingly like he won't live up to the billing of being the 28th overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft. Once Rashee Rice is cleared to return from a hamstring strain, Worthy might benefit from returning to a more comfortable supporting role. He'll try to bounce back in Week 8 against a Broncos secondary that could again be without Pat Surtain, but still ranks sixth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: After impressing as a rookie with 101 touches and 12 touchdowns in 20 games (including the playoffs), Worthy had the look of an emerging star. Things didn't go as planned in Year 2, though, as the 2024 first-round pick was injured on his third snap of the season and wasn't productive or utilized as much as expected upon his return. Worthy was limited to one touchdown (Week 6) and reached 12 fantasy points once in 14 games (Week 4). The speedy Worthy is still only 23 years old, so a Year 3 breakout is certainly possible, especially with Rashee Rice and 36-year-old Travis Kelce as his only legit target competition. He's worth a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Emeka Egbuka is expected to operate as Tampa Bay's top receiver in the Week 2 matchup against the Browns, whose defense struggled against wideouts in Week 1. Despite logging just six targets last week, Egbuka led the Buccaneers in receiving yards, solidifying himself as the team's top WR. Additionally, Egbuka had been nursing a toe injury leading up to the Week 1 loss, so he should only become more explosive as the season progresses. He's in for an incredible Week 2 matchup, as Cleveland's secondary allowed 50.6 PPR fantasy points to wideouts last week, the third-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Emeka Egbuka is expected to remain the Buccaneers' top receiving option in the Week 3 matchup against the Vikings, whose defense has given up 38.9 PPR fantasy points to WRs this season. Egbuka had a rough Week 2 outing, finishing third on Tampa Bay in receptions (three) and targets (five) while slotting in at fifth in yards (16). However, he did score a touchdown and was on the field for 85 percent of the Buccaneers' offensive snaps, suggesting he'll remain the team's WR1. He's set for a tough Week 3 matchup against a Minnesota defense that gave up just three points and 163 passing yards to the Bears in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.4: Emeka Egbuka will remain the Buccaneers' top wideout in the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. Despite another relatively underwhelming Week 3 performance (5-62-0), Egbuka clearly remains atop Tampa Bay's receiving corps, leading the team in targets, receptions, and receiving yards. Baker Mayfield (thumb) will be sidelined in Week 4, which suggests Egbuka will likely see less opportunities. Regardless of who starts at quarterback, Egbuka is in for a favorable matchup against a Green Bay defense that's allowed 34.7 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Emeka Egbuka will look to bounce back from a poor performance in the Buccaneers' Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. Egbuka was targeted just four times during the Week 4 loss to the Packers, his lowest mark of the season. While Baker Mayfield (thumb) remains sidelined and Jalon Daniels acts as the Buccaneers' signal caller, Egbuka may continue receiving less opportunities. However, he's in for a great Week 5 matchup against a Dallas defense that's given up 36.9 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Emeka Egbuka is expected to remain the Buccaneers' top wideout in the Week 6 matchup against the Steelers. Egbuka had a good bounce-back performance in the Week 5 win over the Cowboys, catching six of nine targets for 38 yards while adding 14 yards and a touchdown on the ground. Despite a relatively underwhelming start to the season, Egbuka still leads Tampa Bay in yards (192), targets (33) and receptions (21) through five games. He could struggle in Week 6 against a Pittsburgh secondary that's allowed just 27.7 fantasy points per game to opposing WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Emeka Egbuka is expected to remain the Buccaneers' top wideout in the Week 7 matchup against the Panthers. Egbuka had his most promising game of the 2026 season in the overtime loss to the Steelers, turning a whopping 16 targets into seven receptions for 48 yards and a score. Tampa Bay's offense has struggled without Baker Mayfield (thumb), averaging just 167 passing yards per game since his injury. Despite this, Egbuka has remained productive and could benefit from the potential return of Mayfield in Week 7. Regardless of who starts at quarterback, Egbuka could struggle against a Panthers defense that's allowed just 29.6 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this year.
outlooksByWeek.8: Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) is expected to operate as the Buccaneers' top wideout if active for the Week 8 matchup against the Falcons. Egbuka was sidelined for the Week 7 win over the Panthers but still leads Tampa Bay in targets (49), receptions (28) and receiving touchdowns (two) this season. With Baker Mayfield at quarterback this year, Egbuka has averaged 4.3 receptions, 47 yards and 0.3 touchdowns per game. He could find success against a Falcons defense that's given up 34.4 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Egbuka is a fascinating evaluation following a rookie season that couldn't have started much better (five TDs and 20.5 fantasy PPG during his first five games), but that fell apart from there (one TD and 7.8 PPG during his final 12 games). By season's end, Egbuka sat in the top 10 in targets and air yards, but a horrific 49% catch rate led to a 34th-place finish in fantasy PPG. The good news is that, with Mike Evans out of the picture and Chris Godwin now 30 years old, Egbuka has a shot to emerge as Baker Mayfield's No. 1 target. The 2025 first-round pick is a strong bet for a leap forward and should be viewed as a WR2 with the potential for a full-on breakout.

outlooksByWeek.2: DeVonta Smith was fairly quiet in the season opener for the Eagles. Smith finished with three catches for 53 yards in the 24-22 win over Washington. On the plus side, Smith led the team in targets for the game with six. The absence of A. J. Brown should pay dividends for Smith, perhaps as early as Week 2 versus the Titans. Tennessee allowed 215 passing yards and zero touchdowns through the air in its season opener, though the opposing quarterback was Geno Smith of the New York Jets. Expect Smith to become more involved against a suspect defense.
outlooksByWeek.3: DeVonta Smith broke loose last game for the Eagles, snagging 10 passes for 117 yards and a touchdown in a win over the Titans. Smith saw a team-best 13 targets for the game, a pace which should continue in the absence of A.J. Brown. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL. The Eagles could also rely even more on the passing game if Saquon Barkley is sidelined due to injury.
outlooksByWeek.4: DeVonta Smith unsurprisingly led the Eagles in targets, receptions and receiving yardage last game. Unfortunately, the output was rather pedestrian, as Smith managed six catches and 65 yards on eight targets in the ugly 27-7 loss to the Bears. Smith has been held under 70 yards receiving in two of his three games this season. In Week 4, he will face a rather stingy Rams pass defense allowing just 171.3 yards per game through the air, which is fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: DeVonta Smith missed last game for the Eagles with a hamstring issue, and his status is very much up in the air for Week 5 versus the Jags. Philadelphia's passing offense struggled mightily without Smith and tight end Dallas Goedert, and the early departure of Saquon Barkley due to an injury of his own did not help matters. If Smith misses additional time, Dontayvion Wicks, Darius Cooper and rookie Makai Lemon will have some big shoes to fill. An intriguing matchup lurks in Week 5 versus the Jags. Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: DeVonta Smith has missed two-straight games for the Eagles. Smith has been nursing a hamstring ailment, and his status for Week 6 versus the Panthers remains up in the air. The Eagles offense has struggled mightily without Smith and running back Saquon Barkley. If Smith can return to the lineup, he would provide a major boost against a Carolina defense allowing 230.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 22nd in the league. If Smith cannot suit up, Dontayvion Wicks, Makai Lemon and Darius Cooper would see added work.
outlooksByWeek.7: DeVonta Smith returned to the Eagles lineup with a bang. Smith snagged seven passes for 75 yards and a touchdown following a two-game absence from a hamstring issue. Even with backup quarterback Tanner McKee under center, Smith was targeted a staggering 14 times. As a result, even with McKee at quarterback for the foreseeable future, Smith should have more than ample opportunities. In Week 7, the Eagles will face a Dallas defense that has struggled to defend the pass in 2026. The Cowboys are allowing 232.7 passing yards per game, which is 23rd in the NFL. In addition, Dallas has surrendered 11 passing touchdowns, which is tied for 24th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: DeVonta Smith missed Philadelphia's last game after aggravating a hamstring injury. Smith has played in just four games this season due to the nagging issue, which could also leave him sidelined in Week 8 versus the Commanders. If he is able to suit up, Smith could have a tasty matchup, even with backup quarterback Tanner McKee under center. Washington is allowing 254 passing yards per game, which is 28th in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders have surrendered 15 passing scores, which is tied for 28th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: It's generally tough for a former Heisman Trophy winner and first-round draft pick to fly under the radar, but that has been the case for Smith in recent years. With all eyes on A.J. Brown, Smith has finished no lower than 30th among receivers in fantasy PPG in each of his five seasons (top 30 in PPG each of the last four). The "slim reaper" saw a big dip in touchdowns last season (four, after at least seven the prior three seasons), but remained very efficient (career 9.1 yards per target and 2.1 yards per route run). Smith has handled roughly one-quarter of the Eagles' targets throughout his career, and that may rise slightly after Brown was traded to New England. Smith, 27, is the Eagles' No. 1 receiver for the first time as a non-rookie and is well positioned for a strong WR2 campaign.

The June trade of Myles Garrett quashed much of the enthusiasm surrounding the Browns' D/ST, though the team still has a trio of strong front-line defenders in Mason Graham, Jared Verse (the big return in the Garrett deal) and Carson Schwesinger and finished fourth at the position in fantasy points in 2025. Don't underestimate this unit, which has one of the softer early-season schedules, especially over the first five weeks (@JAX, @TB, CAR, PIT, @NYJ).

outlooksByWeek.2: Makai Lemon was listed as the No. 3 wideout for the Eagles heading into their Week 1 clash with Washington. Unfortunately, Lemon lost five yards on three catches in his NFL debut.  On the bright side, he was targeted four times and was one of only three Eagles receivers to record a catch. Better outputs lie ahead, perhaps as early as Week 2 versus Tennessee.  The Titans surrendered 215 yards passing to Geno Smith of the Jets in their opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Makai Lemon had just one catch in Philadelphia's win over Tennessee. Lemon is battling with Darius Cooper for the No. 3 wideout spot, as Dontayvion Wicks has all but claimed No. 2 for his own. Lemon had just one target last game, while Cooper had three and Wicks managed six. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Makai Lemon is coming off his best game as a member of the Eagles.  Unfortunately, the output was rather pedestrian, as Lemon managed three catches and 29 yards on four targets in the ugly 27-7 loss to the Bears. Lemon has yet to find the end zone as a rookie. In Week 4, he will face a rather stingy Rams pass defense allowing just 171.3 yards per game through the air, which is fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Makai Lemon saw a career-high six targets last game for the Eagles. With DeVonta Smith shelved due to a hamstring ailment, Lemon finished with the second-most targets on the team behind Darius Cooper.  However, the Philadelphia passing game struggled mightily overall, with no wideout gaining more than 33 yards through the air. While Smith should remain sidelined for Week 5, it remains to be seen how the targets will be divided between Lemon, Cooper and Dontayvion Wicks. Nevertheless, an intriguing matchup lurks in Week 5 against the Jags. Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Makai Lemon set career highs across the board last game for the Eagles. Lemon was targeted seven times en route to five catches for 43 yards in the 19-17 loss to the Jags. Lemon has 13 targets in his last two outings. The continued absence of DeVonta Smith with a hamstring injury has boosted the opportunities for Lemon, a trend that could continue in Week 6 versus Carolina. In addition, the Panthers are allowing 230.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 22nd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Makai Lemon caught three passes for 19 yards last game for the Eagles. Lemon was third on the team in targets with six, though the return of DeVonta Smith to the lineup may have limited his production overall. Tanner McKee should start at quarterback for the foreseeable future, which could cap Lemon's upside as well.  In Week 7, the Eagles will face a Dallas defense that has struggled to defend the pass in 2026. The Cowboys are allowing 232.7 passing yards per game, which is 23rd in the NFL. In addition, Dallas has surrendered 11 passing touchdowns, which is tied for 24th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Makai Lemon set career highs across the board last game for the Eagles. With both DeVonta Smith as well as Dontayvion Wicks sidelined due to injury, Lemon snagged seven passes for 67 yards and his first NFL touchdown. He was targeted eight times in the contest. If Smith and/or Wicks are unable to suit up in Week 8 versus the Commanders, Lemon could have a delicious matchup, even with backup quarterback Tanner McKee under center. Washington is allowing 254 passing yards per game, which is 28th in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders have surrendered 15 passing scores, which is tied for 28th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Lemon was selected by the Eagles with the 20th overall pick of April's draft. Lemon is on the small side (5-foot-11, 192 pounds), but he posted a 3.04 YPRR (best in this rookie class) during his collegiate career, dropping only three of 190 career targets (his 1.6% drop rate also paced this class). Lemon, who aligned in the slot on 74% of his collegiate routes, posted a dominant 79-1,156-11 receiving line in 2025, while also contributing as a rusher (two TDs) and returner. With A.J. Brown now in New England, Lemon will battle Dontayvion Wicks for No. 2 work opposite DeVonta Smith. Lemon's skill set provides him with upside, but with plenty of mouths to feed in Philly's low-volume pass offense, he's best valued as a flex option in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jadarian Price is set for his second NFL start when Seattle travels to Arizona in Week 2. Price was efficient in his professional debut last Wednesday versus New England, rushing 10 times for 52 yards while catching both of his targets for six yards. George Holani was given eight carries in the win, which helped limit Price's workload. The split between the two going forward remains to be seen, but there's certainly a chance that Price's touches will increase as the season progresses. The Cardinals' run defense looked good against the Chargers in Week 1, holding Omarion Hampton to 43 yards on 12 carries.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jadarian Price injured his shoulder in the Seahawks' Week 2 win over Arizona, and it's unclear if he'll be able to play in Week 3 against Washington. The rookie RB was injured in the fourth quarter versus the Cardinals and finished the game with 13 carries for 52 yards and one catch for eight yards. Should Price not be able to play in Week 3, Emanuel Wilson would be he lead candidate to take over as the Seahawks starting RB. The Commanders have been awful against the pass but decent against the run this season and are yielding just 3.79 YPC against running backs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jadarian Price heads into Seattle's Week 4 matchup against the Chargers with potentially a lot on the line. After fumbling early in Sunday's Week 3 win over the Commanders, the rookie ended up logging just five totes for 15 yards while adding one catch for seven yards. Meanwhile, Emanuel Wilson (nine carries) and George Holani (three carries and five catches) each out-touched Price, casting uncertainty about the Seahawks' backfield plans moving forward. Price would benefit from a productive (and fumble-free) performance against the Chargers, who rank 19th in the league in giving up 17.2 fantasy points per game through three weeks.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jadarian Price (chest) is eligible to return from IR for Seattle's Week 8 matchup against Chicago. Price hasn't played since Week 3, but he's expected to be designated to return this week. It remains to be seen if the rookie will be able to suit up against the Bears, and even if he does play, he may be part of a backfield committee that also includes Emanuel Wilson and the potentially returning Zach Charbonnet (knee). With that said, Seattle's backfield could find success against a Chicago defense that has given up 4.33 yards per carry to running backs, 25th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Price was selected by the Seahawks with the No. 32 overall pick of April's draft. Price managed only 280 career carries while stuck behind Jeremiyah Love at Notre Dame, but he showed well, posting a 4.13 YAC (second best in this rookie class) and 3.6 forced missed tackle rate (third best). He wasn't a factor as a receiver, however, totaling 15 receptions in 41 games. Price has a path to an immediate feature role in Seattle's run-first offense, though he may eventually defer substantial work to Zach Charbonnet (ACL recovery). Value Price as a flex, though he should land on the weekly RB2 radar while Charbonnet is sidelined.

outlooksByWeek.2: Caleb Williams will look to build off a monster performance as the Bears take on the Vikings at home in Week 2. Williams delivered for Chicago in the highest-scoring Week 1 game in NFL history. The third-year quarterback completed 21 of 29 passes for 269 yards and two touchdowns while carrying the ball 10 times for 65 yards and two more TDs. Williams will have more of a challenge this upcoming Sunday, given that the Vikings allowed the fewest fantasy points per game (14.3) to quarterbacks in the 2025 season. Still, Minnesota's secondary is susceptible, as they ceded 387 passing yards, two touchdowns and one interception to Jordan Love this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.3: Caleb Williams is not expected to play in Week 3 as the Bears take on the Eagles. Williams went down with what looked like a freak injury against the Vikings in Week 2, but he now sits week-to-week with a hamstring ailment. Tyson Bagent is slated to get the start versus an Eagles defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 20.6 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks across two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Caleb Williams is unlikely to play in Week 4 as the Bears take on the Jets. Williams went down with what looked like a freak injury against the Vikings in Week 2, but he now sits week-to-week with a hamstring ailment. Case Keenum is slated to get the start again versus a Jets defense that gave up 269 passing yards and two touchdowns to Jared Goff in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Caleb Williams is set to miss another game as the Bears travel to Green Bay in Week 5. Williams went down with what looked like a freak injury against the Vikings in Week 2, but he now sits week-to-week with a hamstring ailment. Tyson Bagent is set to get the start again versus a Packers defense that gave up 148 passing yards, one touchdown and two interceptions to Buccaneers rookie Jalon Daniels in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.6: Caleb Williams' status is up in the air ahead of Chicago's Week 6 matchup at Atlanta. Williams has been sidelined since he injured his hamstring against Minnesota in Week 2, but he could be ready to return if he has a favorable practice week. If he plays, the starting quarterback will face a Falcons defense that's ranked 21st in fantasy points allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Caleb Williams will aim to build on a stellar return as the Bears play the Patriots in Week 7. Williams had no struggles in Week 6 against the Falcons in his first game since Week 2, completing 83 percent of passes for 305 yards and one touchdown. The third-year quarterback has now surpassed 250 passing yards in both games that he's played through this season, and the sky's the limit now. He'll face a New England defense that's ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Caleb Williams will aim to stay hot as the Bears play the Seahawks in Week 8. Williams impressed in his second game back from a hamstring injury in Week 7, completing 67 percent of passes for 308 yards and two touchdowns over the Patriots. The third-year quarterback has now passed for 300-plus yards in back-to-back weeks, and he hasn't committed a turnover in that stretch. He'll take on a Seattle defense that's been tougher on QBs, ranking second in fantasy points allowed to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams enters his third NFL season after a solid rookie campaign in 2024 followed by a big leap forward in 2025. Williams finished last season no lower than 11th among QBs in pass attempts, completions, pass yards, passing TDs, carries, rush yards, rush TDs and fantasy points per game. While Williams' completion percentage was one of the worst in the league (58%), his dual-threat ability and turnover avoidance (seven INTs both seasons) has led to solid fantasy output. The 2024 No. 1 draft pick has a good supporting cast in playcaller Ben Johnson and a trio of young pass catchers in Rome Odunze, Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland. Williams is a fringe QB1 with upside for another leap.

outlooksByWeek.2: Isaiah Likely scored twice in his debut for the Giants in Week 1, leading a stunning victory over the Cowboys. Likely caught all eight of his targets for 78 yards and the two scores to lead the Giants in receiving. Especially in the red zone and on third down, quarterback Jaxson Dart leaned heavily on his new tight end, something that should continue in Week 2 versus the Rams. Los Angeles allowed 205 passing yards and three touchdowns in its dismal season-opening loss to the 49ers, while also losing star acquisition Myles Garrett to a knee injury. Aaron Donald will make his return from retirement to help out the defensive line, though.
outlooksByWeek.3: Isaiah Likely led the Giants in both receptions and targets last game. Despite seeing 10 opportunities, though, Likely caught five passes for just 33 yards in the dismal loss to the Rams. The bigger news may be that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, Likely will likely see his stock take a hit. However, in Week 3, the Giants will face a lackluster Titans defense allowing 233.5 passing yards per clash, which is 20th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Isaiah Likely's breakout season likely came to a crashing halt with the injury to Jaxson Dart. Likely managed just two catches for 13 yards in the win over the Titans last game. Jameis Winston has been uninspiring to say the least at quarterback, which has limited the opportunities for Likely.  Winston should remain under center in Week 4 versus a vulnerable Cardinals defense. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Isaiah Likely led the Giants in targets last game. Likely saw a staggering 12 balls thrown his way en route to seven catches for 66 yards in the win over Arizona. However, fellow tight end Theo Johnson stole a touchdown from him. Still, Likely's renewed usage with quarterback Jameis Winston under center was a pleasant surprise, as Likely only had five targets in the prior game versus Tennessee. A tasty matchup lurks in Week 5 versus Washington. The Commanders defense has struggled to defend the pass in 2026. Washington has allowed 11 passing scores, which is tied for last in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders are yielding 242.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Isaiah Likely exploded for 11 receptions and two touchdowns last game for the Giants. The 11 receptions set a career high, and Likely scored twice for the second time in five contests. Likely has a staggering 25 targets over the last two outings alone. In Week 6, the Giants host the Saints. New Orleans has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, allowing just 212.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the league. However, New Orleans has also given up eight passing scores already, which is tied for 20th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Isaiah Likely has remained extremely busy for the Giants, regardless of who lines up at quarterback. Likely has received double-digit targets in four of the last five games for the G-Men. Likely has scored three times in the last two contests, and five times on the season overall. Likely leads all NFL tight ends in receiving yards and touchdowns, and is second in receptions to Trey McBride. Likely should be primed for another big outing in Week 7 versus the Texans. Houston is allowing 246 passing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Likely signed with the Giants after four years of backing up Mark Andrews in Baltimore. Likely is reuniting with coach John Harbaugh and is finally expected to play a consistent offensive role. During his time in Baltimore, Likely was limited to 50% of the team's offensive snaps and never finished a season better than 20th among tight ends in snaps, routes, targets, catches, yards or fantasy PPG. His only extensive stretch with Andrews sidelined came back in 2023. During the seven-game span, Likely posted a 23-356-6 receiving line on a 16% target share and averaged a solid 13.5 fantasy PPG. The 26-year-old is obviously unproven, but his receiving skills in New York's ascending offense are enough to put him on the TE2 radar.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cam Little got off to an accurate start by converting both of his field-goal attempts and all four extra points in Jacksonville's Week 1 win. He made an NFL-record 68-yard field goal last season, so there are no concerns about his leg strength. Getting into scoring range will be tougher than usual for the Jaguars in Week 2 against a Broncos defense that allowed the third-fewest points in the league last season, though 70 yards could be within Little's realistic range in the thin Denver air. Little's upside is high enough to maintain fantasy starter status, even given the tricky Week 2 matchup for Jacksonville's offense.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cam Little had a rare miss in Week 2 but has been one of the NFL's best kickers since entering the league in 2024. Through 36 games with the Jaguars, he has converted 61 of 68 field-goal attempts, including an NFL-record 68-yard field goal. He's a little riskier than usual in Week 3 against a Patriots defense that's allowing just 8.0 points per game, but Little is probably too good to bench regardless of the opponent.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cam Little narrowly missed setting an NFL record in Jacksonville's Week 3 win over the Patriots, as his 70-yard field-goal attempt squeaked just wide right. Little already holds the record for the longest made field goal in a regular-season game with a 68-yarder last season, but the powerful kicker has converted just 4-of-6 field-goal attempts in 2026 while having hit all 10 of his PAT tries. Despite Little's pedestrian start, his impressive range coupled with Jacksonville's ability to move the ball effectively give Little starter-level upside each game, and a Week 4 road matchup against a Bengals team that's allowing 21.0 points per game is no exception.
outlooksByWeek.5: Cam Little made all three of his field-goal attempts in Jacksonville's Week 4 win over the Bengals. The big-legged kicker has yet to miss from inside 50 yards and has tremendous range, as Little made an NFL-record 68-yard field goal last season and narrowly missed a 70-yard attempt this season. Little remains a viable fantasy starter as usual in Week 5 against an Eagles team that's allowing 23.3 points per game but has given up only six successful field goals through four games. This game will be played at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London, where Spencer Shrader and Drew Stevens combined to make all five of their field-goal attempts in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.6: Cam Little made both of his field-goal attempts in Jacksonville's 19-17 Week 5 win over the Eagles in London, including the game-winning 57-yarder on the game's final play. He also missed a PAT, with a bad snap contributing after the Jaguars lost long snapper Ross Matiscik to a shoulder injury in the first quarter. Snaps could again be an issue on Jacksonville's kicking attempts in Week 6, but the big-legged Little has too much upside to bench as the Jaguars play their second consecutive game in London, this time taking on a Texans team that has allowed 12 made field goals (tied for third-most in the league), and 22.0 points per game.
outlooksByWeek.8: Cam Little has started 10-for-12 on field-goal attempts with a long of 60 across Jacksonville's first six games. The big-legged kicker could be in for a busy afternoon in Week 8 at home against the Colts, who are giving up 25.7 points per game and have allowed a league-high 21 field-goal attempts, 18 of which have been successful. Little is worth snagging off waivers if he was dropped during Jacksonville's Week 7 bye, as he profiles as a top-10 kicker for Week 8 and beyond.

outlooksByWeek.2: Romeo Doubs will seek a larger role in the Patriots' passing game in Week 2 against the Steelers. Doubs failed to record a catch on three targets in his team debut, playing only 56% of the snaps despite New England losing A.J. Brown to a high-ankle sprain. With Brown set to miss significant time, Doubs should garner more opportunities, but it looks as though he's still developing chemistry with Drake Maye. Questions remain regarding the Steelers' secondary, which is likely to remain without Joey Porter Jr. They weren't tested last week, but counting on a breakthrough from Doubs is risky.
outlooksByWeek.3: Romeo Doubs will look to build on Week 2's uptick in workload in the Patriots offense when they face the Jaguars in Week 3. After not catching a pass in his Week 1 debut, Doubs snagged three of four targets for a team-high 96 yards in Week 2. New England's passing game is sputtering, and despite A.J. Brown missing the last game and a half, Doubs has not logged heavy volume. Jacksonville's secondary was just beaten for 138 yards by Jaylen Waddle, but otherwise, has held up with only one touchdown to opposing wideouts. Until his opportunities increase, Doubs presents a risky profile.
outlooksByWeek.4: Romeo Doubs' workload remains minimal for the Patriots ahead of their Week 4 matchup with the Bills. Despite A.J. Brown's absence (ankle), Doubs has just 11 targets through three weeks. He's averaging a robust 24.2 yards per reception, and the Bills are allowing a big 9.3 yards per target to opposing wideouts. With Drake Maye struggling, gambling on a few Week 4 chunk plays is risky.
outlooksByWeek.5: Romeo Doubs has an ascending role in the Patriots' passing game ahead of a Week 5 matchup with the Raiders. He collected a season-high nine targets in Week 4, and while it resulted in just six catches and 58 yards, he found the end zone twice. Las Vegas will rush the passer, which has troubled Drake Maye. The secondary is allowing 8.2 yards per target to wideouts, so Doubs can capitalize on whatever volume he receives.
outlooksByWeek.6: Romeo Doubs' opportunities have been limited through five games, with the Patriots hosting the Jets in Week 6. After recording nine targets in Week 4, Doubs hauled in just one of three looks in Week 5, giving him three or four targets in four of the first five games with his new team. Though the Jets have been statistically stout against the pass, allowing just 195.4 yards per game, they've allowed five opposing wide receivers to post at least 58 yards in as many games. With Drake Maye spreading targets around, Doubs' ceiling is low, making him a fringe flex option.
outlooksByWeek.7: Romeo Doubs was placed on the injured list after injuring his shoulder while making a diving touchdown catch in Week 6. The Patriots expect him to return following their Week 11 bye. While Doubs is out, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism, and Kyle Williams should log more targets.

player.seasonOutlook: Doubs signed with the Patriots during free agency after spending his first four NFL seasons with the Packers. He was a serviceable player during his Green Bay tenure, but he never finished a season in the top 30 among receivers in targets, catches, yards or fantasy points. Consistently mediocre, Doubs has averaged either 10.2 or 10.3 fantasy PPG each of the last three seasons. In New England, Doubs is likely to settle in as Drake Maye's No. 2 target behind A.J. Brown, though his target ceiling figures to be capped with the likes of DeMario Douglas, Mack Hollins and Kyle Williams also in the mix at receiver. Doubs, 26, is a fine addition to your bench, but his upside is limited.

outlooksByWeek.2: Nico Collins is in danger of sitting out against the Bengals in Week 2 due to a hamstring injury. He paced Houston's passing attack with a 7-75-1 line on 10 targets in the season opener, so he would work as the team's WR1 again in Week 2 against the Bengals if given the green light to suit up. Cincinnati didn't allow a passing TD to the Buccaneers in Week 1 but had one of the league's worst all-around defenses last season, when the Bengals gave up the second-most yards and third-most points in the NFL. Collins remains a set-and-forget fantasy WR1 as he chases his fourth consecutive 1,000-yard receiving season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Nico Collins (hamstring) didn't suit up for the Texans in Week 2 and may not be ready to return against the Colts in Week 3. If Collins recovers, he'll jump back in as the top option in Houston's passing game and a fantasy WR2 at worst. Should Collins sit again, TE Dalton Schultz could continue to work as the primary pass catcher for C.J. Stroud, while the Texans get by with Kayshon Boutte, Xavier Hutchinson, Jaylin Noel and Jared Wayne at WR.
outlooksByWeek.4: Nico Collins (hamstring) could return from a two-week absence in Week 4 against the Cowboys. Houston's No. 1 WR will immediately jump back into the fantasy WR1 range if he plays against a Dallas defense that's giving up 27.3 points per game. The Cowboys have allowed seven touchdowns through the air, though only three of those went to WRs. Houston hasn't garnered much production out of its wide receiver room in Collins' absence. If Collins remains unavailable, TE Dalton Schultz would likely remain the de facto top target for QB C.J. Stroud.
outlooksByWeek.5: Nico Collins returned from a two-game absence due to a hamstring injury in Week 5 and reclaimed his customary spot as Houston's top receiver and a fantasy WR1. He scored twice against the Cowboys and has compiled 14 catches for 194 yards and three TDs in two appearances this season. Collins can be started with confidence in Week 5 against the Titans, who are allowing 167 receiving yards per game to wideouts. DeVonta Smith and Zay Flowers each compiled at least 117 yards and a TD against Tennessee's secondary.
outlooksByWeek.6: Nico Collins is averaging 83 receiving yards and one touchdown per game as the clear No. 1 option in Houston's passing game. His role isn't expected to change in Week 6 against the Jaguars, even with the Texans having traded for 2024 fourth overall pick Marvin Harrison from the Cardinals. Jacksonville boasts the league's best run defense but has a vulnerable secondary, as the Jaguars are the only team to have allowed over 1,000 yards to wide receivers this season. Collins is a top-five fantasy WR for Week 6.
outlooksByWeek.7: Nico Collins has posted at least 79 scrimmage yards in three of his four appearances this season for the Texans ahead of a Week 7 home game against the Giants. The star wideout can be deployed in his usual spot as a fantasy WR1 for Week 7 while facing a Giants secondary that has done a decent job of suppressing yards from WRs but is tied for the fourth-most TDs allowed to the position with seven. Collins has 24 touchdown receptions in 46 games since the start of the 2023 campaign, including three scores in four games this season as the top target for resurgent QB C.J. Stroud.

player.seasonOutlook: Collins heads into his sixth NFL campaign yet to play a full 17-game season, but having been very productive when on the field. The 2021 third-round pick has cleared 1,000 yards and scored either seven or eight touchdowns each of the past three seasons, finishing in the top 10 in fantasy PPG and top 12 in yards per route run in all three. A force near the goal line, Collins ranked fourth among receivers with 13 end zone targets in 2025. The 27-year-old's target share doesn't stack up with other top receivers (he has never cleared 24.4%), but his high-end efficiency is just enough to keep him in the back-end WR1 mix.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaylen Waddle did not contribute much in his Broncos' debut, catching just one of three targets for a meager two yards in the Week 1 loss to Kansas City. Steve Spagnuolo's rebuilt secondary prioritized taking Waddle out of the picture, and the former Dolphin wideout hasn't yet established enough chemistry with QB Bo Nix to overcome consistent double teams. Waddle will look to bounce back in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that was tied for 17th last season in points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaylen Waddle broke out in the Broncos' Week 2 win over the Jaguars, erupting for an 8-138-0 line on 10 targets as he began to get on the same page as quarterback Bo Nix. Waddle logged plenty of downfield targets but also had a red zone look, usage that promises plenty more big performances. The former Dolphin hasn't had a 1,000-yard season since 2023, but the early returns in Denver suggest he'll have little trouble returning to that level in 2026. He'll face a Rams secondary in Week 3 that's allowed just 19 receptions to WRs through two weeks, tied for seventh in the NFL, but three of those have gone for touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaylen Waddle is struggling to adjust to his new offense with the Broncos. The former Dolphins wide receiver caught only two of his seven targets in a Week 3 win over the Rams for 10 yards, while adding a 14-yard run. Waddle leads Denver with 20 targets through three games, but he's turned them into just 11 catches for 150 yards, and he's still looking for his first TD of the season. He'll face a 49ers secondary in Week 4 that ranks ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jaylen Waddle scored his first touchdown with the Broncos in a Week 4 loss to the 49ers, but it was overall another disappointing performance from the former Dolphin. Waddle has recorded double-digit targets only once in four games to begin the season, leading to a modest 16-185-1 line on 26 looks from Bo Nix. That's still better numbers than Courtland Sutton, and the issue seems to be the overall struggles of the offense under first-time play caller Davis Webb. How long Sean Payton lets that situation last before reclaiming those duties is an open question for Denver. Waddle will try to hit paydirt again in Week 5 against a Chargers secondary that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jaylen Waddle continues to struggle in his first season with the Broncos. He's been held to 35 receiving yards or fewer in four of five games, including a 2-19-0 line on five targets in a Week 5 win over the Chargers. Having Sean Payton reclaim play-calling duties should help the offense in the long run, but Waddle will be tough to trust until he begins to display consistent chemistry with Bo Nix. Waddle will face a Seahawks secondary in Week 6 that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jaylen Waddle remains stuck in neutral as part of a sluggish Broncos passing game. The former Dolphin has gone four straight games without reaching 40 receiving yards, managing just a 13-88-1 line on 25 targets over that stretch while quarterback Bo Nix tries to find a rhythm. Waddle showed his upside back in Week 2 with an 8-138-0 line, but until the Denver offense begins clicking, his production will remain erratic. He could break out in Week 7 against a Cardinals secondary that's given up 10 touchdowns to wide receivers this season, 31st in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jaylen Waddle left the Broncos' Week 7 win over the Cardinals in the fourth quarter with a chest injury after producing a modest 4-48-0 line on seven targets. The former Miami wideout hasn't been able to get comfortable in his new environment; he has been held under 50 receiving yards in six of his first seven games for Denver. The severity of Waddle's injury isn't clear, but the team had little incentive to get him back on the field with a big lead. Assuming he is cleared to play in Week 8, he'll have a tough time producing a ceiling game against a Kansas City secondary that ranks third in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Waddle was traded to Denver after spending his first five seasons in Miami. The 2021 first-round pick was solid during his Dolphins tenure, finishing in the top 30 among receivers in fantasy PPG four times, though never reaching the top 10 while often playing second fiddle to Tyreek Hill. Although he has been a reliable target and has missed only seven games in five years, Waddle hasn't finished a season higher than 20th in targets or catches since 2021. In Denver, the 27-year-old Waddle will compete with Courtland Sutton for the team lead in targets in a scheme that likes to spread the ball around. Not utilized near the goal line much at 5-foot-10 and 180 pounds (he's yet to clear seven end zone targets in a season), Waddle is likely to max out as a back-end WR2 in Denver.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cam Skattebo showed no ill effects from last season's injury in Week 1 for the New York Giants. Skattebo rushed 18 times for 81 yards and a touchdown in he stunning 28-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys. With the Giants poised to possess the ball and feed the running game under new coach John Harbaugh, Skattebo should continue to be in line for a heavy workload. In Week 2, the Giants will face a Rams defense that was surprisingly suspect against the run in their first game of the season.  The Rams allowed 174 yards on the ground, which currently ranks them 30th in the league. However, Aaron Donald will return to the fold out of retirement versus the G-Men.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cam Skattebo managed just 55 yards from scrimmage last game for the Giants. The bigger news may be that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, teams will likely gameplan to stop the run, which starts with Skattebo. That could mean tough sledding for the running game for the G-Men overall. However, in Week 3, the Giants will face a mediocre Titans run defense that has given up 120.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is 21st in the NFL. In addition, the Titans have already surrendered three rushing scores in the first two games of the season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cam Skattebo racked up 100 yards from scrimmage in the 12-7 win for the Giants over the Titans. Skattebo took 20 carries for 60 yards while also catching three passes for 40 yards out of the backfield. With Jameis Winston under center, the Giants should continue to rely on the running game led by Skattebo in Week 4 versus Arizona. The Cardinals have been suspect against the run in 2026, allowing 127.7 yards per clash on the ground, which is 26th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Cam Skattebo has struggled to find room to roam for the Giants thus far this season. Skattebo rushed 18 times for 58 yards in the 36-24 win over the Cardinals last game. He is averaging just 3.5 yards per carry as teams dare the Giants to throw with backup quarterback Jameis Winston. In Week 5, Skattebo will face a rather stingy Washington run defense as well. The Commanders are allowing just 93.5 yards per tilt on the ground, which is sixth in the league. However, Washington did allow three rushing touchdowns last game versus the Colts.
outlooksByWeek.6: Cam Skattebo was mostly a non-factor last game against the Commanders, at least until the end of a wild contest which resulted in a tie. Skattebo managed 40 of his 71 scrimmage yards in overtime, though coughed up the ball as the Giants were in field goal range to potentially win the game. Skattebo would have truly been the goat for this contest had Washington not botched the final seconds of overtime. Skattebo has had 60 rushing yards or less in four-straight games, and has failed to score since the opener. However, in Week 6, the Giants will face a Saints defense that has been gutted on the ground thus far in 2026. New Orleans is allowing148.8 rushing yards per clash, which is 30th in the league. In addition, New Orleans has allowed the most rushing touchdowns in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Cam Skattebo had zero touches last game for the Giants. One week after losing a key fumble, Skattebo was removed from his starting job as the Giants backfield devolved into a four-man committee. Tyrone Tracy was the team's most productive back, scoring one rushing and one receiving touchdown, but managed just 45 scrimmage yards on eight touches. Devin Singletary had 33 yards on five touches and Najee Harris eked out just two rushing yards on four carries. Skattebo could return to a more significant role in Week 7 against the Texans, but it will be hard to trust any New York running back until one emerges from the pack. Houston is also allowing just 83 rushing yards per contest, which is third in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Skattebo is a Year 2 breakout candidate following an impressive but injury-shortened rookie season. The fourth-round pick first played a significant offensive role in Week 2 and went on to average 16.0 carries, 4.7 targets and 96.3 yards while scoring six TDs during his six full games. His 19.1 fantasy points per game during the span would've ranked sixth over the full season. The 24-year-old enters 2026 with a new coach (John Harbaugh) and playcaller (Matt Nagy), but his competition for touches are Najee Harris and the same guys he beat out for work in 2025 (Tyrone Tracy Jr., Devin Singletary). Assuming his ankle heals up as expected, Skattebo will be on the RB2 radar with upside for more.

outlooksByWeek.2: D'Andre Swift will aim to replicate a huge game as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Swift was dominant against the Panthers in Week 1, carrying the ball 18 times for 124 yards and three touchdowns. The veteran ball carrier topped any of his games in the 2025 season, showcasing that he should also benefit from a higher-scoring Chicago offense this year. He'll play a Minnesota defense that shelled Green Bay on the ground in their opener, but he has established himself more than the Packers' current RB room.
outlooksByWeek.3: D'Andre Swift will be a top option in Chicago's offense in Week 3 against the Eagles. Swift cooled down in Week 2 after a monster opener, logging 16 rushes for 45 yards on the ground. The veteran RB did see success in the passing game, logging five catches for 54 yards. With Tyson Bagent expected to start at quarterback for the Bears, Swift could be utilized more heavily on the ground. Philadelphia has also allowed 216 rushing yards to running backs this season, a bottom-10 mark in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: D'Andre Swift should remain Chicago's top option in the rushing game against the Jets in Week 4. Swift saw a season-high 20 carries in Week 3 versus Philly , taking them for 84 yards and adding on two catches for four yards. The veteran ball carrier eclipsed 80 rushing yards in two of the first three games of the campaign, but he's seen his only end zone appearances come from Week 1. He'll now turn his attention to a Jets defense that ceded 99 rushing yards and two touchdowns off 20 carries to Jahmyr Gibbs in their most recent outing.
outlooksByWeek.5: D'Andre Swift will seek to get back on track as the Bears travel to Green Bay in Week 5. Swift rushed the ball 15 times for 58 yards and caught two targets for 16 yards against the Jets in Week 4, but he also lost a fumble and was stopped at the goal line twice. The veteran was outplayed by his younger counterpart, Kyle Monangai, who posted a 30-146-2 rushing line. Either way, Swift should still get plenty of usage against a Packers defense that's ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to running backs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.6: D'Andre Swift could be in line for a featured role once again as the Bears play the Falcons in Week 6. Swift should have benefited hugely from Kyle Monangai being out with a toe injury in Week 5, but he rushed nine times for 43 yards and a touchdown and caught four passes for 30 yards in a blowout loss. The status of Monangai remains up in the air ahead of Chicago's away bout, and Swift's value is very much contingent on his position mate's status. Atlanta has ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy RBs so far.
outlooksByWeek.7: D'Andre Swift could see his workload take a hit as the Bears play the Patriots in Week 7. Swift was inefficient on the ground in Week 6 with 16 carries for 44 yards, but he was able to salvage his outing with two rushing touchdowns and four catches for 26 yards. The veteran has benefited from Kyle Monangai being out the last two weeks with turf toe, especially given that three of his six touchdowns this season have come in that stretch. Whether Monangai plays or not, Swift will face a New England front that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy RBs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: D'Andre Swift's role will be up in the air heading into Week 8 as the Bears travel to Seattle. Swift produced once again in Week 7, tallying 22 rushes for 78 yards and a touchdown, along with catching four passes for 12 yards. The veteran has benefited from a workhorse role with Kyle Monangai (toe/thumb) out the last three weeks, finding the end zone four times and averaging over 19 touches per game in that stretch. Monangai could be in line to return this week, but the pair of running backs have proven to both hold value even when both active. Either way, Swift will face a Seahawks defense that's ranked top 10 in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs (15.4).

player.seasonOutlook: Swift is entering his seventh NFL season and third with Chicago. The veteran back was busy as both a rusher and receiver en route to clearing 1,300 scrimmage yards in each of his first two seasons with the Bears. Though he found the end zone 10 times and finished 17th among backs in fantasy points per game last season, Swift deferred substantial work to Kyle Monangai and is likely to be in even more of a timeshare in 2026. Still in his prime at age 27, Swift continues to play at a high level (4.87 yards per carry last season), but his role in the Chicago offense figures to limit him to low-ceiling RB2/flex production.

outlooksByWeek.2: Bryce Young will look to stay hot in the Panthers' Week 2 matchup against the Falcons, whose defense allowed just 14.8 fantasy points to quarterbacks in Week 1. Despite Carolina's defensive struggles, Young threw for 361 yards, the third-most in the NFL during Week 1, and led the offense to 37 points. Additionally, he added a touchdown on the ground as the Panthers offense looked more aggressive than in 2025. Young is also in for a favorable matchup, as he threw for 569 yards and accounted for four total touchdowns in two games versus the Falcons in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bryce Young will look to stay hot in the Panthers' Week 3 matchup against the Browns, whose defense has surrendered 22.1 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks this season. Young has been one of the most productive QBs in the NFL through two weeks, as he's tied for the most touchdown passes in the league (six) while ranking second in passing yards (648). He's also threatened defenses with his legs, adding 16 yards and a score on the ground. Young could very well finish as one of fantasy's top quarterbacks again in Week 3 while playing a Browns defense that's allowed five touchdown passes this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Bryce Young is expected to lead the Panthers' offense into a Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Despite a Week 3 loss, Young remained productive, throwing for 291 yards, one touchdown and an interception. Through three weeks, the Alabama product has accounted for eight total touchdowns and two turnovers while leading Carolina's offense to 29.7 points per game. He's dealing with injuries to Jalen Coker (quad) and Xavier Legette (knee), which could result in the Panthers leaning more on the ground game in Week 4. Regardless, Young should be in for a favorable matchup against a Lions defense that's given up the most fantasy points per game to opposing QBs (35.3) this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Bryce Young is expected to continue leading Carolina's offense in the Week 6 matchup against the Eagles. Young has performed very well to start the season, leading the NFL in passing yards per game (317) while accounting for 10 total touchdowns. In his most recent performance, a Week 4 win over the Lions, Young threw for a whopping 329 yards and two touchdowns. He's expected to remain one of fantasy's top quarterbacks while facing an Eagles defense that's allowed 22.4 fantasy points per game to opposing QBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Bryce Young is expected to remain productive in the Panthers' Week 7 matchup against the Buccaneers. Through five games this season, Young has thrown for 1,549 yards and accounted for 12 touchdowns with just two interceptions, leading the league with 309.8 passing yards per game. He's emerged as one of fantasy's top quarterbacks while leading the Panthers' offense to 29.2 points per game, the fourth-best mark in the NFL. Expect Young to remain productive in Week 7 against a Buccaneers defense that's given up just 18.7 fantasy points per game to opposing QBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Bryce Young will look to bounce back from a poor performance in the Panthers' Week 8 matchup against the Packers. Young underwhelmed for the first time all season in the Week 7 loss to the Buccaneers, completing 14 of 27 passes for 163 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. Despite this, Young has been one of the league's most productive quarterbacks this season, throwing for an average of 285.3 yards and 2.0 touchdowns per game. He'll look to rebound in Week 8 against a strong Packers defense that's given up just 17.8 fantasy points per game to opposing QBs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Young has yet to find his way to any sort of fantasy relevance during his first three NFL seasons. The 2023 No. 1 draft pick has yet to finish a season better than 20th in passing yards, 10th in rushing yards or 24th in fantasy points per game. Efficiency has been a problem, as last season's career-high 6.3 yards per attempt was barely up from 2024 and still among the worst in the NFL. Young's 47.6 QBR last season ranked 22nd among 28 qualified quarterbacks. Perhaps the 25-year-old will make a leap in top target Tetairoa McMillan's second season and Brad Idzik's debut as the offensive playcaller, but it will be asking a lot to expect QB1 production. Young is best viewed as a fringe QB2 in 12-team leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mike Evans had a strong 49ers debut last Thursday versus the Rams and will next face Miami in Week 2. Evans caught six passes for 49 yards and a touchdown in the season opener, with his score coming on a two-yard connection with quarterback Brock Purdy. The veteran wideout tied with Deebo Samuel for the most targets among SF wideouts, so he looks to have already established a good rapport with Purdy. Evans could be in for another strong performance Sunday against a Titans defense that allowed three passing touchdowns in a Week 1 loss to Las Vegas.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mike Evans picked up a hip injury in San Francisco's win over Miami on Sunday, but early indications suggest he'll be fine for a Week 3 matchup versus the Cardinals. Evans has established a nice rapport with QB Brock Purdy so far this season, as the veteran wideout has caught nine of 10 targets for 103 yards and a touchdown. San Francisco's WR corps has been thinned by the season-ending injury to rookie De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle) and Demarcus Robinson's more recent ankle injury, which will likely sideline him for Week 3, so Evans' availability as a reliable target for Purdy has taken on increased importance. Arizona was crushed by star wideout Jaxon Smith-Njigba (9-155-3 receiving line) in Week 2 and has given up four total receiving TDs to wideouts through two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Mike Evans' status for San Francisco's Week 4 game against Denver is cloudy due to injuries to his ribs and oblique. Evans was injured in the second quarter of Sunday's win over Arizona and wasn't able to return to the contest. He had gotten off to a strong start prior to the injury, catching three passes for 34 yards and a touchdown. If he's able to suit up against Denver, he'll face a tough challenge against star cornerback Patrick Surtain and a defense that has allowed the NFL's second-lowest catch rate (50.9%) to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Mike Evans seems likely to continue playing through an injury to his ribs for San Francisco's Week 5 matchup against the Seahawks. The veteran wideout toughed out the injury in Week 4 and posted a 5-76-0 receiving line against a tough Broncos secondary. That receiving yardage was a season-high mark for Evans, as were his eight targets. Seattle could pose a significant challenge to the 49ers' receiving corps, however, as the Seahawks have yielded just 12.8 fantasy points per game to wideouts this season -- third-fewest in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Mike Evans is coming off his best game as a member of the 49ers heading into a Week 6 tilt against Washington. Evans posted a 7-113-1 receiving line and added a two-point conversion in a tight win over the division-rival Seahawks this past Sunday.
