Fellow wideout Deebo Samuel injured his hamstring in the victory, and if he's unable to return for Week 6, Evans' importance in the passing game could be elevated even higher. The Commanders may be ripe for the picking, as they've given up the seventh-most fantasy points per game (25.0) to wideouts on the campaign.
outlooksByWeek.7: Mike Evans and the 49ers are in Atlanta for a Week 7 road tilt. Unfortunately for him, he'll likely be spending it, and possibly more, on the sidelines after aggravating his Achilles injury in San Francisco's Week 6 win. Evans is expected to sit out the contest against the Falcons with a Week 8 bye on the horizon, giving him extra time and recovery for a chance to suit up in Week 9.

player.seasonOutlook: Evans signed with the 49ers after spending his first 12 NFL seasons with the Buccaneers. The future Hall of Famer famously opened his career with 11 consecutive 1,000-yard seasons, but that streak ended when he missed nine games due to injury last season. Even when active, Evans wasn't his usual, productive self, delivering only one weekly fantasy finish better than 23rd and none better than 11th. Now 33 years old, Evans is past his prime, but he's in line for a decent chunk of the targets, especially near the goal line, in Kyle Shanahan's high-scoring offense. Evans is best valued as a touchdown-dependent WR3/flex with more value in non-PPR formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers travel in Week 2 to face the Patriots, who have the ninth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (15.0) to RBs. He rushed 10 times for 46 yards and caught five of six targets for 27 yards in Pittsburgh's 20-13 win against Atlanta. Warren lost a fumble, but he still out-touched fellow RB Rico Dowdle 15-10 and had much better results from those opportunities. If the Steelers continue to favor the passing game against New England, or if they're forced into it via game flow, Warren would carry a bit more value in what looks to be a true timeshare.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers welcome the Bengals to town for a Week 3 AFC North matchup. He rushed 11 times for 43 yards and brought in two of four targets for 34 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss to New England. Warren handled 11 of 20 carries from backs in this one, but the Steelers weren't able to get much going on offense. It looks like he's the 1A out of the backfield, and although it's not by a substantial amount, Rico Dowdle is considered questionable to suit up on Sunday with a toe injury. Warren faces a 14th-ranked Cincinnati defense in fantasy points allowed (19.0) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers travel to take on the Browns for an AFC North clash in Week 4. He rushed 17 times for 127 yards and caught three of four targets for 49 yards during Pittsburgh's thrilling 30-27 victory in Week 3. Warren handled a workhorse role with Rico Dowdle (toe) out, and it looks like that could again be the case with a short turnaround for Week 4's Thursday Night Football showcase in Cleveland. He'll face a tough matchup as the Browns rank sixth in fantasy points allowed (17.1) to RBs and are one of seven teams yet to surrender a TD to the position.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers welcome the Colts to town in Week 5. He tallied 17 carries for 93 yards while catching three of six targets for 33 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss. Warren handled a massive workload for the second straight week with Rico Dowdle (toe) on the sidelines. There's a chance Dowdle remains out against Indianapolis, leaving Warren as the unquestioned lead back versus the Colts' 23rd-ranked defense, which has allowed 24.2 fantasy points per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers travel to face the Buccaneers in Week 6. He rushed 15 times for 101 yards and a touchdown and caught all six of his targets for 87 yards, including an 80-yard TD reception, during Pittsburgh's Week 5 win. Warren continued to handle a workhorse role with Rico Dowdle (toe) out for the third straight contest. He compiled 490 scrimmage yards and two TDs on 61 touches over that stretch, and head coach Mike McCarthy stated Monday that Warren is viewed as "our featured player right now." Even if Dowdle can suit up versus Tampa Bay's sixth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (17.4) in Week 6, Warren is likely to keep working as the lead back for a Steelers offense averaging 29.3 points through their last three outings.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers face off against the Saints in Paris in Week 7. He had 14 carries for 50 yards and caught two of four targets for 28 yards during Pittsburgh's overtime victory in Week 6. With Rico Dowdle (toe) back on the field, Warren's opportunities dipped noticeably despite out-touching Dowdle 16-10. He should still handle a larger volume than Dowdle going forward, but managers should certainly temper expectations as long as both backs are healthy. Warren draws a very favorable matchup against a New Orleans defense that ranks dead last in fantasy points allowed per game (30.7) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers host the Browns for a Week 8 divisional clash. He had 18 carries for 101 yards and corralled three of four targets for 36 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 7 victory in Paris. Fellow running back Rico Dowdle amassed 86 scrimmage yards on 15 touches, and it appears he's rounding into form after missing nearly a month with a toe injury. Warren remains atop the backfield hierarchy, but he'll face a tough test against Cleveland's eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (19.7) to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Warren reached career-high marks in touches (251), yardage (1,291) and touchdowns (eight) last season, his fourth in the league. The former undrafted free agent put up 13.6 fantasy points per game (19th among backs) and PFF tracked him with 56 forced missed tackles (seventh). Pittsburgh swapped out Kenneth Gainwell for Rico Dowdle as Warren's running mate, and the two are expected to split work in a Mike McCarthy offense that rarely deploys its backs in the passing game. Warren is capable and effective as a rusher and receiver, but his ceiling figures to be limited in this committee. He's likely to cap out as a flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: DeMario Douglas will seek more production in Week 2 when the Patriots face the Steelers. He logged a reasonable seven targets to open the season but turned that into just 20 yards on five grabs. Douglas has a rapport with QB Drake Maye as a safety valve, and while snaps seem safe with A.J. Brown (ankle) sidelined for the foreseeable future, Douglas topped 40 yards just four times last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: DeMario Douglas' role in New England's struggling passing offense is questionable ahead of a Week 3 game at Jacksonville. In Week 2, Douglas logged just two targets in his first full game without A.J. Brown after a seven-target opener, and he's averaging just 4.8 yards per reception to start the season. Jacksonville is allowing a hefty 10.3 yards per target to opposing wideouts, but Douglas' inability to stretch the field would require uncharacteristic heavy volume to provide a modest fantasy return.
outlooksByWeek.4: DeMario Douglas hasn't been consistently targeted in the Patriots struggling passing attack ahead of a Week 4 matchup with the Bills. Douglas has just one catch in each of his last two games, and while last week's popped for 38 yards, he's averaging just 9.4 yards on his seven snags to date. Buffalo's defense has been friendly to opposing wideouts, allowing 9.3 ypt with six receivers going for 40+ yards, but with limited volume, Douglas doesn't seem destined to exploit that.
outlooksByWeek.5: DeMario Douglas hasn't emerged in the Patriots' receiving corps ahead of a Week 5 matchup against the Raiders. Despite A.J. Brown's continued absence, Douglas has just four total catches over the last three weeks, tallying 62 yards. An uptick in volume appears unlikely against an exploitable secondary that allows 8.2 yards per target, leaving Douglas as a dart throw as opposed to a reliable lineup option.
outlooksByWeek.6: DeMario Douglas faces an uphill battle to match Week 5's success when the Patriots face the Jets in Week 6. Douglas shined with two touchdowns and a season-high 65 yards against the Raiders, but he's still hauled in no more than two balls in three of five outings while being held to 38 yards or fewer in his first four games. New England is spreading the ball around in its surging passing attack, so Douglas seems unlikely to retain heavy volume. The Jets have allowed four opposing receivers to register 63 yards or more in the last two weeks, giving Douglas a shot at some upside.
outlooksByWeek.7: DeMario Douglas is emerging as a viable option for the Patriots ahead of a Week 7 matchup with the Bears. Over the past two weeks, Douglas has garnered 13 targets, turning them into 11 catches and three touchdowns. Though A.J. Brown is back from an ankle injury, New England could be without Romeo Doubs due to a shoulder ailment, suggesting Douglas' place in the receiving pecking order may be unchanged, giving him a chance to post solid numbers against a secondary that's allowed nine opposing receivers to gain at least 55 yards.
outlooksByWeek.8: DeMario Douglas will seek a rebound in Week 8 when New England travels to Miami. He was on a two-game heater entering Week 7, but finished with just three catches for 23 yards and has been held to 38 yards or fewer in five of seven outings. Miami is allowing an attractive 8.8 yards per target, the eighth-highest total league-wide, but because of vulnerabilities to tight ends and running backs in the passing game, opposing wideouts have the second-fewest yards, suggesting it may be better to look elsewhere for meaningful production.

player.seasonOutlook: The Chiefs have fielded a middling fantasy D/ST the past two seasons, scoring in double-digits only seven times  but finishing with zero or negative fantasy points only five times . Top draftee Mansoor Delane replaces CB Trent McDuffie, who was traded to the Rams, but the team otherwise returns largely the same starting lineup. An opening-week matchup against the Broncos should be avoided, but there are pockets of the schedule where the Chiefs would be great for streaming: Weeks 3-4 (@MIA, @LV) and Weeks 9-11 (NYJ, @ATL, ARI) especially.

outlooksByWeek.2: Khalil Shakir will look to remain Josh Allen's security blanket in Week 2 when the Bills host the Lions. Shakir managed four grabs on six targets to open the season, finishing with 50 yards. He operated underneath while newly acquired DJ Moore stretched the field. The Lions' vulnerable secondary gave up 410 yards passing in Week 1, but Shakir will likely be limited by shorter routes, creating a safe but uninspiring fantasy option.
outlooksByWeek.3: Khalil Shakir remains a steady, stable cog in Buffalo's passing game entering a Week 3 matchup with the Chargers. Shakir logged six targets in each of the Bills' first two games but hasn't topped 50 yards or scored. Shakir didn't take on an elevated role in Week 2 following DJ Moore's (shoulder) early exit, but he faces a secondary that allowed 75 yards to Kendrick Bourne and 119 yards to Tre Tucker, and both operate in a similar slot role to Shakir.
outlooksByWeek.4: Khalil Shakir seeks more opportunities in Week 4 when the Bills face the Patriots. Despite a season-high 71% snap share in Week 3, Shakir had his lowest output of 2026, catching just a six-yard pass on three targets in a game where Josh Allen struggled. Shakir could benefit from additional looks in Week 4 if DJ Moore is matched up consistently with CB Christian Gonzalez. Operating primarily out of the slot tempers high yardage totals.
outlooksByWeek.5: Khalil Shakir maintains a steady role out of the slot for Buffalo as they prepare to face the Rams in Week 5. Shakir is coming off a season-high 82 yards in Week 4, his third game with at least six targets. His workload is independent of DJ Moore's shoulder status. Shakir will either garner more targets if Moore is out, or benefit from the attention Moore usually draws. However, the Rams defense hasn't allowed an opposing receiver to top 50 yards, suggesting Shakir is a risky floor and limited ceiling option.
outlooksByWeek.6: Khalil Shakir continues to play a minimal role in the Bills' passing game as they enter a Week 6 matchup with the Raiders. Shakir had just three targets in Week 5, the second time he's experienced that limited volume in three weeks despite the continued absence of DJ Moore (shoulder). Shakir is averaging a career-best 14.2 yards per catch and with Las Vegas proving vulnerable over the middle (nine catches, 122 yards, two touchdowns last week to DeMario Douglas and Efton Chism), Shakir could exploit a favorable matchup despite a lack of heavy volume.
outlooksByWeek.8: Khalil Shakir will reprise his slot role in Week 8 when the Bills host the Ravens. Shakir hasn't directly benefited from DJ Moore's (shoulder) absence, with a largely unchanged role prior to Buffalo's Week 7 bye, logging six or more targets in four of six contests. While he's topped four catches just once, he's averaging 13.2 yards per catch, his highest mark since 2023. Baltimore's secondary has been more vulnerable to larger, outside X receivers, with Drake London, Tee Higgins, and Carnell Tate all topping 100 yards against them. Shakir will need to continue to take advantage of his opportunities to be a viable fantasy option.

player.seasonOutlook: Shakir has settled in as a reliable, short-range target for Josh Allen, though the role hasn't led to much fantasy success. The 2022 fifth-round pick has cleared a 20% target share and 70 catches in consecutive seasons, ranking top five among receivers in catch rate and RAC both years. A nonfactor near the goal line, however, Shakir totaled eight TDs and five end zone targets during the span. Shakir finished the two seasons just outside of the top 35 fantasy receivers and will now have to compete with DJ Moore for the team lead in targets. Shakir was already barely worth flex consideration, so the potential for a slight decrease in target volume suggests the 26-year-old is no more than a low-ceiling bench option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Hunter Henry will look for more opportunities in Week 2 when New England hosts Pittsburgh. Henry caught all three of his targets to open 2026, and with the Patriots losing A.J. Brown (ankle) for the foreseeable future, additional targets could come Henry's way. Pittsburgh didn't allow a catch to tight ends last week, but that was a product of poor opponent quarterback play. Henry can be considered a back-end option at the position with the potential for far more against a defense he posted two touchdowns and 90 yards against a season ago.
outlooksByWeek.3: Hunter Henry will look to keep expanding his role for the Patriots in Week 3 against the Jaguars. In their first full game without A.J. Brown in Week 2, Henry logged a 92% snap share but drew only five targets, turning them into three catches for 40 yards. Drake Maye has struggled to open the season, posting a 1:4 TD:INT ratio, and while someone has to catch the limited passes, Henry faces a challenging matchup against a defense that hasn't allowed an opposing tight end to top 32 yards against them so far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Hunter Henry is laboring for opportunity in a sputtering Patriots passing offense ahead of a Week 4 game against the Bills. Henry caught just one of two targets in Week 3, finishing with five yards, and has yet to score or top 40 yards. There are likely better Week 4 options with Henry facing a defense that's allowed one opposing tight end to top 35 yards.
outlooksByWeek.5: Hunter Henry could have an expanded role in Week 5 when the Patriots face the Raiders with Eli Raridon (ankle) uncertain. Henry was already playing at least 70% of the snaps, and he posted a season-high five catches for 62 yards in Week 4, collecting five targets for the second time this season. Las Vegas has allowed five touchdown catches to opposing tight ends, but also just 6.1 yards per target through four games, suggesting Henry may need to find the end zone for the first time in 2026 to be a fantasy asset.
outlooksByWeek.6: Hunter Henry has been steady in the Patriots passing game ahead of a potentially difficult Week 6 matchup with the Jets. He has three catches in four of the Patriots' first five games, three times recording at least 40 yards, and he posted 45 and 49 yards in two matchups last season against this divisional opponent. However, the Jets have been stingy against tight ends, allowing just 191 yards (6.0 yards per target) and zero touchdowns through five games.
outlooksByWeek.7: Hunter Henry brings a two-game scoring streak into the Patriots' Week 7 matchup with the Bears. With Drake Maye clicking on all cylinders over the last three weeks (10 touchdown passes), Henry has posted at least three catches and 44 yards during that stretch. Chicago has defended tight ends well for most of the season, but over the last two weeks, an opposing tight end has gone for 60 or more yards, and they've surrendered their first two touchdowns of the year to the position. Henry's volume is steady, giving him a bit more of a reliable floor than high potential.
outlooksByWeek.8: Hunter Henry is poised to build on a season-high performance in Week 7 when the Patriots face the Dolphins in Week 8. While he failed to reach the end zone for the first time in three games, Henry hauled in all seven of his targets for 71 yards, all season bests. Miami has been exploited by opposing tight ends with six touchdown receptions in six games and 9.3 yards per target, the second highest mark in the league. New England continues to spread targets around, but it seems wise to scheme into this vulnerability, making Henry a preferred Week 8 option.

player.seasonOutlook: Henry has settled in as one of Drake Maye's top targets, having reached 85 targets, 60 catches and 650 yards each of the past two seasons (each ranked in the top 10 among tight ends). A threat downfield and near the goal line, Henry has finished in the top 15 in aDOT each of the past seven seasons and 12th or better in end zone targets in seven of his nine campaigns. Despite the solid usage, Henry hasn't sported much fantasy upside, as he has failed to finish in the top 12 in fantasy PPG since 2020 (he has never finished better than eighth). The 31-year-old has added target competition this season (Romeo Doubs and A.J. Brown), so he's no more than a fringe TE2.

outlooksByWeek.2: KC Concepcion and the Browns are on the road in Week 2 to face the Buccaneers and their eighth-ranked defense in receiving yards allowed to WRs (101). The rookie looked hungry and fought for more on every play, catching four of five targets for 43 yards and rushing three times for 15 yards while losing a fumble. Concepcion's blunder came on a play from behind as he tried to gain extra yardage, but it was still a promising debut for the 24th overall pick in the 2026 draft, as he led the team in receptions and targets. Still, it's difficult to trust anyone on the Browns' offense, especially against a Tampa Bay defense that held Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins to 71 combined yards.
outlooksByWeek.3: KC Concepcion and the Browns return home in Week 3 to host the Panthers and their 18th-ranked passing defense. He finished Cleveland's upset win over the Buccaneers in Week 2 with six catches on six targets for 28 yards and had one rush for minus-6 yards. Concepcion led the team in receptions but was last in average yards per touch at just 4.7. His general involvement on offense is a great sign, but it appears fellow rookie Denzel Boston is the Browns receiver to roster thanks to his big-play ability.
outlooksByWeek.4: KC Concepcion and the Browns welcome Pittsburgh to town for an AFC North clash in Week 4. He caught just two of nine targets for nine yards during Cleveland's upset victory in Week 3. Concepcion wasn't able to contribute much despite tying for the team lead in targets with Harold Fannin Jr., but it's still a positive sign that the Browns are looking to get the ball in his hands. He'll get his first chance to face the division-rival Steelers and their 14th-ranked defense in receiving yards allowed (403) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: KC Concepcion and the Browns visit the Jets for a Week 5 showdown. The rookie receiver finished second on the team in receptions (5) and yardage (64), while his eight targets led the way in Cleveland's Week 4 victory. Concepcion also returned two punts for 10 yards, as it remains clear the Browns want the ball in his hands in a variety of ways for him to shine as a playmaker. However, he'll face a talented Jets secondary that allows 28.5 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks ninth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: KC Concepcion and the Browns welcome the division-rival Ravens to town in Week 6. He caught his lone target for five yards before leaving Cleveland's 17-12 loss in Week 5 with a head injury after a hard hit. Concepcion has entered the league's five-step concussion protocol and will have to be cleared by an independent neurologist before returning to the field. The promising rookie's status should be monitored leading up to a Week 6 showdown against Baltimore's 23rd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per contest (36.2) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: KC Concepcion and the Browns visit the Titans in Week 7. He hauled in four of six targets for 37 yards and rushed twice for two yards during Cleveland's 13-10 comeback win in Week 6. The rookie first-round pick led the team in targets, tied for first in receptions, and was second in yardage behind veteran Jerry Jeudy (69). Concepcion will look to deliver more, along with the entire Browns' offense, versus Tennessee's 24th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (35.9) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: KC Concepcion and the Browns travel to Pittsburgh for a Week 8 divisional clash. He caught eight of 10 targets for 129 yards and had three carries for another 23 yards during Cleveland's comeback victory in Week 7. The rookie broke out with season highs in receptions, yardage and targets while leading the Browns in every category. Concepcion will aim to score his first touchdown of his career versus the Steelers 14th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (30.5) to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Concepcion was selected by the Browns in the first round of April's draft. He is a quick and explosive short-to-intermediate receiver whose career 27.2% target share topped this entire rookie class. Primarily a slot receiver during his first two seasons at NC State, Concepcion played more on the outside in 2025 at Texas A&M, but he figures to primarily work inside in the pros (career 72% slot rate), while also helping as a rusher and returner. Concepcion will need to fend off the likes of Jerry Jeudy, Harold Fannin Jr. and fellow rookie Denzel Boston for targets in an offense with quarterback issues, so while he has upside, he's best valued as a flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jahmyr Gibbs will look to keep it rolling in Detroit's Week 2 matchup at Buffalo. Gibbs was the bell cow managers hoped for in Week 1 against the Saints, logging 29 rushes for 156 yards, two touchdowns and catching all five of his targets for 30 yards. He'll also face a Bills defense that fared badly against the ground game in their season opener, allowing Gibbs' former teammate David Montgomery to total 79 yards and three touchdowns off 23 touches.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jahmyr Gibbs will aim to keep things rolling as the Lions take on the Jets in Week 3. Gibbs finished with huge numbers once again in Week 2, but most of his output came from six catches for 61 yards and a touchdown. The superstar running back has seen high volume so far, with 56 touches for 299 scrimmage yards and three touchdowns to his name this season. He'll face a Jets defense that's been tough against the run in its first two games, but New York hasn't faced anyone of Gibbs' caliber.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jahmyr Gibbs will look to keep his touchdown tear alive as the Lions travel to Carolina in Week 4. Gibbs was a beast once again in Week 3 against the Jets, turning 20 carries into 99 yards and two touchdowns, as well as catching the ball six times for 65 yards and another touchdown. The fourth-year star has now found the end zone six times across three games, and he's totaled 463 yards from scrimmage. He'll face a Panthers defense that's allowed the third-most fantasy points per game (30.5) to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jahmyr Gibbs will aim to return to dominance as the Lions play the Cardinals in Week 5. Gibbs produced for fantasy managers in Week 4, but he still rushed 15 times for a season-low 46 yards with a touchdown, tacking on four catches for 31 yards. Either way, the superstar running back has found the end zone in every game this season, and he's surpassed 100 total yards in three of four games. He'll face an Arizona defense that's ranked top five against fantasy RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jahmyr Gibbs will look to come out of the bye week with a bang as the Lions play the Packers in Week 7. Gibbs was a monster in Week 5 against the Cardinals, rushing 25 times for 151 yards and two touchdowns, with five catches for 56 yards as well. The premier running back has now surpassed 100 scrimmage yards in all but one game this season, and he's found the end zone nine times across five games. He'll face a Green Bay front that's ranked 29th in fantasy points allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jahmyr Gibbs will look to get back in the end zone as the Lions play the Vikings in Week 8. Gibbs hit the century mark on the ground for the third time this season in Week 7 versus Green Bay, rushing the ball 29 times for 116 yards and adding five catches for 27 yards. The superstar unfortunately was held to zero touchdowns for the first time this season, with nine to his name across the first five games. He'll change focus now to a Minnesota defense that's ranked third in fantasy points allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Gibbs has finished in the top 10 among running backs in yards per carry, routes, targets, receptions, touchdowns and fantasy points in each of his first three campaigns. In fact, his 38 touchdowns over the past two seasons are four more than any other player. Though Gibbs has finished as a top-three fantasy back in each of the past two years, he has yet to finish a season higher than seventh in touches. That very well could change this season with David Montgomery no longer in the mix. The 24-year-old Gibbs is one of the NFL's top playmakers in one of its best offenses. He's a strong option with the first pick of fantasy drafts.

outlooksByWeek.2: Colston Loveland will look to get more involved as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Loveland disappointed in Week 1 against the Panthers, failing to bring in either of his two targets, even though it was the highest-scoring Week 1 game in NFL history. The second-year tight end's output was hopefully a fluke, especially as he was still on the field for 86 percent of Chicago's offensive snaps. Loveland will also face a Minnesota defense that allowed five catches for 115 yards to Green Bay's tight ends in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Colston Loveland will look to turn things around as the Bears play the Eagles in Week 3. Loveland disappointed again in Week 2, catching just one of three targets for three yards against the Vikings. The second-year tight end now has just one catch on the year, which is nowhere near the breakout season managers were projecting. He'll likely be thrown to by Tyson Bagent against Philly defense that's allowed the fewest PPR fantasy points per game to tight ends this season (5.1).
outlooksByWeek.4: Colston Loveland will look to improve his role even more as the Bears play the Jets in Week 4. Loveland finally saw more than a chalked role against the Eagles in Week 3, reeling in all four of his targets for 31 yards. This output is far from what was expected of the second-year tight end heading into the season, but it's still optimistic for the future. He'll face a New York defense that's ceded a top-ten 8.0 fantasy points per game to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Colston Loveland will look to build off a season-best performance as the Bears travel to Green Bay in Week 5. Loveland commanded nine targets in Week 4 against the Jets, which allowed him to finish with six catches for 57 yards. The second-year tight end has now increased his yardage from zero to three to 31 to 57 in the first four games of the year. He'll aim to find the end zone for the first time of the campaign against a Packers defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against TEs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Colston Loveland will look to do more as the Bears play the Falcons in Week 6. Loveland wasn't able to build on a solid six catches for 57 yards in Week 4, reeling in just two of five targets for 19 yards versus the Packers in Week 5. The second-year pass catcher has been thrown to by three quarterbacks of varying skill so far this year, which could add to the struggles of his output. He'll take on an Atalnta defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy TEs this year.
outlooksByWeek.7: Colston Loveland will look to build off a season-best outing as the Bears play the Patriots in Week 6. Loveland caught six of seven targets for 65 yards and a touchdown in Caleb Williams' return to the field. The second-year tight has now caught six passes in two of his last three games, and he sits in a favorable spot after a rough start to the year. He'll face a New England defense that's ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to TEs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.8: Colston Loveland will aim to continue producing as the Bears play the Seahawks in Week 8. Loveland stayed hot in a Week 7 win over New England, finishing with season highs in catches (7), targets (12), yards (69) and tacking on a touchdown. The second-year tight end has had a promising turnaround to the season, with 50 or more yards in three of his last four games and back-to-back outings with a score. He'll face a Seattle defense that's ranked fourth in fantasy points allowed to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: After averaging 4.1 targets and 8.5 fantasy PPG during his first 14 NFL games, Loveland leaped to 12.0 targets (10-plus in each) and 20.0 fantasy PPG during his final four games of 2025 (including the playoffs). For perspective, there have been only 12 instances of a tight end seeing at least 10 targets in four consecutive regular-season games in NFL history (and only one was a rookie). Loveland's overall efficiency was terrific, as he ranked eighth or better among tight ends in YPR, YPT and YPRR. With DJ Moore gone, the 2025 first-round pick enters his age-22 season all but locked into a massive workload alongside Rome Odunze and Luther Burden III. Loveland's ceiling is lofty, and midrange fantasy TE1 should be his floor.

outlooksByWeek.3: Josh Jacobs is unlikely to play in the Packers' Week 3 matchup against the Falcons. Jacobs remains on the Commissioner's Exempt List at this point in the season, with no current indications of when he'll be back in action. A committee of MarShawn Lloyd, Chris Brooks and Kaleb Johnson will continue to provide Green Bay's rushing attack while the veteran is absent.
outlooksByWeek.8: Josh Jacobs will look to ramp it up even more as the Packers play the Panthers in Week 8. Jacobs carved out a solid performance in his return to the field against the Lions in Week 7, rushing the ball for 36 yards off 11 carries but catching five passes for 55 yards and a touchdown. While the rushing efficiency wasn't there, the usage definitely was, which bodes well for the veteran ball carrier. He could also be in store for a better outing on the ground, as Carolina has ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to RBs this campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: Jacobs' 2025 season can be split in two parts: pre-injury and post-injury. While healthy during his first nine games, Jacobs picked up where he left off from a terrific 2024 debut season with Green Bay, averaging 21.1 touches and 19.6 fantasy points while scoring 11 TDs. After missing all but 11 snaps during Weeks 11 and 12, Jacobs returned and wasn't quite the same, averaging 14.6 touches and 11.3 points while totaling three touchdowns in his final five games. But Jacobs, 28, was still effective overall (PFF's fourth-highest-graded back) and has a clear grasp on lead-back duties in a good Green Bay offense that has afforded him 30 touchdowns (fifth most in the NFL) in 32 games. He's a fine back-end RB1 when active, but a likely suspension makes him less valuable on draft day.He's worth a mid-round flier until the dust settles.

outlooksByWeek.2: Patrick Mahomes proved he was fully recovered from last year's ACL injury in Kansas City's season-opening win over the Broncos, scoring a 15-yard rushing TD in addition to completing 15 of 27 passes for 184 yards and two touchdowns with one interception. The offense flowed through new lead back Kenneth Walker and benefited from some short fields, but Mahomes still took advantage of his opportunities. The star QB could be headed for better individual numbers in Week 2 against a Colts defense that looked awful in its opener and which ranked 31st in passing yards allowed in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Patrick Mahomes has Kansas City's offense humming, and through two games, he's produced 566 passing yards and a 5:1 TD:INT while adding a touchdown on the ground. The superstar QB has spread the ball around effectively, as five different targets have been on the end of those TDs, and a revitalized running game with Kenneth Walker has prevented defenses from laying back and clogging the passing lanes. Mahomes could be headed for big numbers in Week 3 against a Dolphins defense that has yet to record a sack in 2026 and which sits 32nd in completion rate against at a stunning 78.8%.
outlooksByWeek.4: Patrick Mahomes continued his strong start to the season in Kansas City's Week 3 win over the Dolphins, producing multiple touchdowns for a third straight game. The two-time MVP has a 7:2 TD-to-INT ratio in those three contests while adding another score on the ground, and his 8.3 yards per attempt would be his highest mark since 2019. He's done it without the benefit of a single dominant receiver, as Travis Kelce, Kenneth Walker, Rashee Rice, and Xavier Worthy have all logged between 15 and 18 targets. Mahomes will look to keep rolling in Week 4 against a Raiders defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Patrick Mahomes comes out of Kansas City's bye with a strong 9:2 TD:INT and 8.1 yards per attempt through four games. The presence of Kenneth Walker in the backfield has opened things up for the team's passing game, but Mahomes did lose Week 4 breakout Tyquan Thornton to a dislocated ankle that could potentially sideline the speedy wideout for the rest of the season. Rashee Rice also picked up a minor hamstring strain prior to the bye, which could leave Mahomes working with a very inexperienced group of WRs, although he still has Travis Kelce to fall back on. Mahomes will be facing a Chargers defense in Week 6 that is tied for 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Patrick Mahomes didn't have much to do in Kansas City's Week 6 easy win over the Chargers. With Kenneth Walker and the defense doing most of the work in a 22-6 victory, Mahomes failed to throw a touchdown pass for the first time this season, although he did rack up 272 passing yards and 9.1 yards per attempt. His 8.3 mark on the year is his best since 2019, and through five games he's produced 10 TDs-nine passing and one rushing-against three turnovers. Mahomes faces a much tougher test in Week 7 against a Seahawks defense that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Patrick Mahomes is coming off one of the worst performances of his career in Kansas City's Week 7 loss to the Seahawks. The two-time MVP threw for a season-low 165 yards with zero touchdowns and failed to get his team into the red zone for the first time in 153 career starts, including regular season and playoffs. With his wide receiver room thinned by injuries, Mahomes is again having a tough time stretching the field or taking advantage of a defense's focus on Kenneth Walker. He'll try to bounce back in Week 8 against a Broncos defense playing below expectations, which sits tied for 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Mahomes is a bit of a wild card as he embarks on his 10th season. The two-time NFL MVP followed up a pair of disappointing fantasy seasons (2023-24) with an elite start to 2025 (24.5 points per game during Weeks 1-8) and a disappointing finish that included 15.0 points per game during his final six games and a torn ACL in Week 15. Mahomes' efficiency has dipped the past three seasons, and while he made up ground as a rusher in 2025 (fifth among QBs in rushing yards and TDs despite three missed games), he might not be able to run as often this season as he recovers fully from the knee injury. Mahomes will be ready to play in Week 1, but he hasn't been a consistent fantasy QB1 since 2022. He's a risky mid-round flier in drafts.

outlooksByWeek.2: Michael Wilson will look to break through against a tough Seattle secondary for Arizona in Week 2. Wilson performed well in a season-opening win over the Chargers, catching five of seven targets for 56 yards. He outproduced presumed No. 1 wideout Marvin Harrison, though newcomer Kendrick Bourne led the WR corps with an 8-75-0 line. All three figure to be challenged by a Seahawks defense that ranked 10th in passing yards allowed last year.
outlooksByWeek.3: Michael Wilson faces a tough challenge in Arizona's Week 3 matchup in San Francisco. Wilson was quiet against Seattle this past Sunday, catching just two of seven targets for 18 yards. However, he was still the Cardinals' second-leading receiver in a game during which QB Jacoby Brissett threw for just 95 yards. The 49ers have surrendered only 15.6 fantasy points per game to wideouts, the ninth-best mark in the league threw two weeks.
outlooksByWeek.4: Michael Wilson appears to be Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett's favorite wideout target heading into a Week 4 matchup against the Giants. Wilson got a whopping 17 targets this past Sunday in a loss to San Francisco, recording 11 catches for 89 yards and a touchdown. Meanwhile, Marvin Harrison posted a quiet 3-40-0 line on five targets. Of course, star TE Trey McBride will consistently draw plenty of Brissett's attention, but it looks like Wilson is in line for lots of looks in the team's offense. He could thrive against a Giants defense that is giving up 23.6 fantasy points per game to WRs, ninth-most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Michael Wilson has settled in atop Arizona's WR depth chart heading into a Week 5 tilt against the Lions. Wilson caught seven passes on 13 targets for 95 yards against the Giants in Week 4, leading or co-leading the Cardinals in all three categories. He's drawn a whopping 30 targets over his past two contests, making it clear that QB Jacoby Brissett sees him as the top option among the team's wideouts. Wilson could be in store for a big game against a Detroit defense that has yielded 28.3 fantasy points per game to wide receivers, third-most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Michael Wilson is set to lead Arizona's wideout corps versus the Rams in Week 6. After Marvin Harrison was made inactive this past Sunday due to a pending trade, Wilson functioned as the no-doubt No. 1 WR for the Cardinals but managed just four catches for 30 yards against Detroit. He was outproduced by fellow wideout Kendrick Bourne, who posted a 5-70-0 line, but Wilson should have plenty of chances to thrive with Harrison officially off to Houston. The Rams have given up the fewest receiving yards per game to wideouts this season, but they've also surrendered seven receiving TDs to the position, tied for third-most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Michael Wilson has emerged as Arizona's leading wide receiver following Marvin Harrison Jr.'s departure, recording 33 receptions for 320 yards and a touchdown through six games. Wilson has averaged 9.7 yards per reception, and his established role as the team's new WR1 should keep him among Jacoby Brissett's preferred targets alongside star tight end Trey McBride. However, the Cardinals' passing attack has struggled to generate explosive plays, limiting Wilson's weekly ceiling. To make things even more complicated, the Week 7 matchup against the Broncos is far from easy, as Denver has allowed the seventh-fewest fantasy points per game to wideouts in 2026. That, coupled with Brissett's inconsistent play under center, limits Wilson's fantasy appeal considerably in most formats.
outlooksByWeek.8: Michael Wilson will look to get back his early-season mojo with a juicy matchup when Arizona faces the Cowboys in Week 8. After hauling in 18 passes on 30 targets for 184  yards across Weeks 3 and 4, Wilson has compiled just 12 receptions on 22 targets for 117 yards over his past three games. The downturn has some in spite of the Cardinals trading away Marvin Harrison to make Wilson the team's clear-cut No. 1 wide receiver, though tight end Trey McBride has continued to feature as QB Jacoby Brissett's top target. Harrison will have a chance to put up big numbers versus a Dallas defense that ranks 27th in the NFL with 23.9 fantasy points per game allowed to wideouts.

player.seasonOutlook: After averaging 4.3 targets and 7.6 fantasy points per game during his first 38 NFL games, Wilson broke out with Jacoby Brissett under center during the final eight games of 2025, averaging 11.0 targets and 21.2 fantasy PPG. The stretch also coincided with Marvin Harrison Jr. dealing with health issues, and it's worth noting that Wilson's receiving lines in the four games Harrison was active weren't quite as good (3-40-0, 3-61-0, 4-34-0, 3-36-0). A healthy Harrison (along with TE Trey McBride) figures to lead to a return to earth for Wilson, but the 26-year-old did enough late last season to warrant WR4/flex consideration in drafts.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ka'imi Fairbairn remains locked in as a starting fantasy kicker in Week 2, when the Texans host a Bengals team that allowed the third-most points in the NFL last season. Fairbairn led the league in both made and attempted field goals last season. He was limited to one field-goal attempt in Week 1 as the Texans scored four TDs, but the standout kicker showed off his mix of power and accuracy by converting a go-ahead 58-yard field goal in the fourth quarter, though that ultimately wasn't enough to beat the Bills.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ka'imi Fairbairn had a rare miss on a difficult 58-yard field-goal attempt in Houston's Week 2 loss, but he remains one of the NFL's best kickers after leading the league in both made and attempted field goals last season. Fairbairn is locked in as a high-end fantasy starter for a Week 3 road game against a Colts team that has been the NFL's worst defensively. Indianapolis is allowing 37.0 points and 514.5 yards per game, both league highs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ka'imi Fairbairn is just 4-for-5 on field-goal attempts through three games for the 0-3 Texans. It's a less-than-ideal start for the standout kicker, but Fairbairn remains a hold for fantasy purposes considering the Texans bounced back from a 0-3 start last season while supplying Fairbairn with enough opportunities to lead the league in both field goals made (44) and field goals attempted (48) during the 2025 regular season. He has a golden opportunity to break out in Week 4, as the Texans shouldn't have as much trouble moving the ball against the Cowboys, who are allowing 387.0 yards and 27.3 points per game, both of which are among the league's 10 most generous totals.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ka'imi Fairbairn connected on all three of his Week 4 field-goal attempts, improving to 7-for-8 this season. Houston's excellent kicker could be busy in Week 5 against the Titans, whose nine made field goals allowed are tied for fifth-most in the NFL. Fairbairn has established himself as one of the busiest and most accurate kickers in the league, which is an excellent combination for fantasy purposes. He remains a set-and-forget fantasy starter.
outlooksByWeek.6: Ka'imi Fairbairn has connected on all seven of his field-goal attempts over Houston's past two games after going just 4-for-5 through Week 3. He's among the most reliable kickers in the league and can be started with confidence in Week 6 despite a tricky matchup against the Jaguars, who have allowed just seven made field goals and 14.0 points per game through five games. Fairbairn is 55-for-60 on field-goal attempts in 20 regular-season appearances since the start of last season, including a perfect 42-for-42 from inside 50 yards.
outlooksByWeek.7: Ka'imi Fairbairn has missed just one kick all season for the Texans and remains a high-end starting fantasy kicker for Week 7 against the Giants, whose defense is trending in the wrong direction. The Giants allowed just 18.3 points per game through Week 3 but have surrendered 28.3 points per game across their last three, including 34 to the Saints in Week 6. Meanwhile, the Texans have won two consecutive games after starting 0-4, and Fairbairn has made all nine of his field-goal attempts over the past three weeks.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Olave is expected to remain the Saints' top wideout in the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Olave definitely benefitted from Tyler Shough's 56 pass attempts during the Week 1 overtime loss. However, New Orleans averaged 34.8 pass attempts per game in 2025, so Olave will likely continue to see loads of volume. Additionally, he saw a 25 percent target share, which should remain steady until Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) returns later this season. Olave is in for a tough matchup this week, however, with Baltimore's defense allowing just 25.0 PPR fantasy points to WRs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chris Olave is expected to remain one of fantasy's top receivers in the Saints' Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. Olave ranks second in the NFL in both receptions (18) and receiving yards (268) through the first two weeks, cementing himself as New Orleans' top wideout. Currently, he's received a 25.6 percent target share, which should continue proving valuable with the Saints high-volume of pass attempts (90 through two weeks, second-most in the NFL). Olave could struggle against the Raiders, however, whose defense has allowed just 21.9 PPR fantasy points to wideouts per game this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chris Olave is expected to remain one of fantasy's most productive wideouts in the Saints' Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. Olave has surpasses 100 receiving yards in two of three games this season, catching 27 of 36 targets for 373 yards and a touchdown. He's expected to continue benefitting from New Orleans' pass-happy offense that has averaged 44 pass attempts per game through three weeks. Additionally, Olave is in for a very favorable Week 4 matchup against a struggling Falcons secondary that's allowed 38.5 PPR fantasy points per game to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chris Olave is expected to lead New Orleans' receiving corps again in the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. Olave has been spectacular through the Saints' first four games this season, catching 35 of 48 targets for 491 yards (second in the NFL) and a touchdown. He's expected to continue benefitting from head coach Kellen Moore's pass-heavy offense, which has led to ample opportunities for Olave this season. Despite this, Olave could struggle in Week 5 against a tough Vikings secondary that's given up just 30.1 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Chris Olave will look to return to form in the Saints' Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Olave struggled along with the rest of New Orleans' offense in the Week 5 loss to the Vikings, catching four of six targets for 46 yards. On the season, Olave ranks second in the NFL with 537 receiving yards and will likely continue benefitting from head coach Kellen Moore's aggressive style of offense (averaging 41 pass attempts per game). Expect Olave to bounce back against a solid Giants defense that's allowed 30.9 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Chris Olave is expected to remain one of fantasy's top wideouts in the Saints' Week 7 matchup against the Steelers. Olave didn't receive his usual volume in Week 6 but remained productive, catching four of seven targets for 43 yards and a score. He's expected to continue benefitting from Kellen Moore's aggressive offense that's averaged 39.2 pass attempts per game through six weeks. However, Olave is in for a difficult Week 7 matchup, as Pittsburgh's defense has given up just 29.0 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Olave is fresh off a career year in which he reached new highs in targets (156), receptions (100), yardage (1,163) and touchdowns (nine). He finished eighth among receivers in fantasy PPG, which beat out his previous career best of 19th in 2023. Olave finished no lower than seventh among receivers in nearly every counting stat, including end zone targets (12) and air yards (1,816). The big season was a sigh of relief after a 2024 campaign riddled with concussions, and it positions the 26-year-old right back in the fringe-WR1 discussion. Especially with No. 8 overall pick Jordyn Tyson expected to miss a month or two with a hamstring injury, Olave will remain Tyler Shough's top target, and that sets him up for another highly productive campaign.

outlooksByWeek.2: De'Von Achane should again be featured for the Dolphins against the 49ers in Week 2. Achane recorded only 11 carries to open the year, with Miami falling behind early-something that is likely to be a weekly occurrence-but he logged five targets. In Week 1, San Francisco allowed 114 rushing yards and a touchdown plus four receptions to backs, and with Achane rarely leaving the field (88% snap share), the makings are there for a safe outing with scoring upside.
outlooksByWeek.3: De'Von Achane's volume remains elite as the Dolphins get set to host the Chiefs in Week 3. Achane has amassed 31 carries and 11 targets through two weeks, and while his 3.5 yards per carry is modest, there aren't many other options with such a safe workload. Kansas City is allowing 4.0 yards per carry, and they'll surely stack the box against Achane, as everyone else is doing. However, the Chiefs have allowed four catches to an opposing back in consecutive weeks. Achane's volume generates a floor, with scoring providing upside.
outlooksByWeek.4: De'Von Achane will miss the remainder of the season after tearing his ACL. Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright will handle the bulk of the Dolphins' carries.

player.seasonOutlook: Achane has quickly staked his claim as one of the best running backs in the league. The 2023 third-round pick has scored either 11 or 12 touchdowns in each of his three seasons and put up a career-high 1,838 scrimmage yards in 2025. Achane's elite receiving production is nothing new (he has finished in the top five among backs in targets and receiving yards in each of the past two years), but he made another leap forward as a rusher last season, finishing fifth at the position in rushing yards. His 5.62 yards per carry is best among qualified backs since he entered the league. The 24-year-old is eyeing his third straight top-five fantasy campaign, and while that might be tricky in an overhauled Miami offense led by quarterback Malik Willis, Achane has minimal competition for touches and should easily be the offensive centerpiece. He's a solid RB1 option.

Brian Flores' blitz-happy defense has managed exactly 49 sacks, fourth-most in the league, in each of the past two seasons, playing a big part in the team finishing among the position's top seven in fantasy scoring in each of those years. Though Jonathan Allen and Jonathan Greenard are no longer with the team, the Vikings' draft selections of DTs Caleb Banks and Domonique Orange should at least keep them competitive up front. That said, the Vikings face a brutal opening schedule (GB, Week 1; @CHI, Week 2) and have one of the toughest second-half schedules in the league. Be prepared to pivot if this D/ST starts slowly.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jared Goff will look to build off a season-opener win as the Lions travel to Buffalo in Week 2. Goff's performance and Detroit's overall in Week 1 weren't pretty, but he got the job done, finishing with 206 passing yards and two touchdowns. The game also showed that the Lions will continue to have a high-volume air attack, as the veteran ended with 39 pass attempts. Goff will now turn his focus to a Bills defense that ceded 274 passing yards and two touchdowns to C.J. Stroud in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jared Goff will look to keep his high production rolling as the Lions take on the Jets in Week 3. Goff benefited from playing from behind in Week 2 at Buffalo, racking up 327 passing yards and four touchdowns on a 68.4 percent completion rate. The veteran quarterback has now totaled 533 passing yards with a 6:0 TD:INT across his first two games, and Detroit's lacking defense has only helped his output so far. Goff will take on a Jets defense that's allowed a top-10 fantasy points per game (14.2) to quarterbacks in the first two games of the season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jared Goff will continue to benefit from a high-powered offense as the Lions travel to Carolina in Week 4. Goff kept it rolling in Week 3, throwing for 269 yards with two touchdowns and zero interceptions. The veteran quarterback has completed 70.6 percent of his passes for 802 yards and eight touchdowns with no interceptions across three games. He'll face a Carolina defense that's allowed the ninth-most fantasy points per game (23.5) to QBs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jared Goff will remain a high-volume option as the Lions travel to Arizona in Week 5. No matter the outcome of each game so far, Goff has delivered consistent output, and Week 4 against the Panthers was no different. The veteran quarterback recorded season-high totals in completions, pass attempts and passing yards, completing 32 of 52 passes for 412 yards and one touchdown in what was an eventual loss. He's now thrown for 250 or more yards in his last three games, and he's yet to commit a turnover this year. Goff will face a Cardinals defense that's ranked 28th against fantasy quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jared Goff will seek to stay hot as the Lions play the Packers in Week 7. Goff recorded another monster performance heading into Detroit's bye week, and he's yet to throw an interception this season. The veteran quarterback has now completed 67 percent of passes for 1,485 yards with 12 touchdowns and zero interceptions in five games. He'll face a Green Bay defense that allowed 258 passing yards and a 1:2 TD:INT ratio to Dak Prescott in Week 6.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jared Goff will aim to keep it rolling as the Lions play the Vikings in Week 8. Goff's story stayed the same in a Week 7 win over the Packers, completing 22 of 32 passes for 303 yards and two touchdowns. The veteran quarterback has now passed for 300-plus yards in three of six games, and he's also dished out two or more touchdowns in all but one outing. He'll have his biggest test of the season this week, though, as Minnesota has allowed the fewest fantasy points per game to the quarterback position.

player.seasonOutlook: Goff is entering his 10th NFL season, including his sixth with the Lions. The 2016 No. 1 draft pick has been extremely successful through the air over the past three seasons (4,500-plus yards and 30-plus touchdowns in all three), which has helped him to fantasy finishes of seventh, sixth and ninth. Of course, there's some survivorship bias here, as Goff's per-game finishes during the span are 15th, seventh and 12th. The reason for the limited fantasy output is a lack of rushing, as Goff has never cleared 108 rushing yards in a season and was held to 45 yards in 2025. Playing at his absolute ceiling as a passer and still no more than a fringe QB1, the 31-year-old is just a solid backup/occasional streaming option in fantasy.

Zak Kuhr, elevated to the defensive coordinator position early last season, steered this D/ST to the sixth-most fantasy points and a Super Bowl LX berth. Now in the permanent role, he'll have a strengthened unit, with DE Dre'Mont Jones and S Kevin Byard brought on board, though it's fair to point out that the 2025 Patriots generated nearly one quarter of their fantasy points on defensive or special teams touchdowns. This is a team better used as a streaming than weekly defense, and bear in mind it has a tough-as-nails Super Bowl rematch in Seattle to begin the year.

outlooksByWeek.2: Javonte Williams scored twice in the season opener for Dallas. Williams rushed for 41 yards and a touchdown, while catching five passes for 31 yards and a second score, though the Cowboys fell to the Giants by a score of 28-20. Nevertheless, Williams appears to have picked up right where he left off in 2025 during his career year. In Week 2, Williams will face a Washington defense that was gutted on the ground in its season opener. The Commanders yielded 136 yards on the ground, which places them 26th in the NFL in that category currently.
outlooksByWeek.3: Javonte Williams was rather quiet last game for Dallas. Williams managed just 50 yards from scrimmage and did not find the end zone versus Washington, as the passing game took the spotlight in the 37-20 win. Williams may also have a difficult time finding room in Week 3 versus Baltimore. The Ravens are allowing just 83.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is sixth in the NFL. However, Baltimore has allowed three rushing touchdowns already, which is tied for 23rd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Javonte Williams rushed for a season-high 98 yards last game for the Cowboys. Williams also found the end zone for the third time this year. He has received at least 15 touches in every game this season. In Week 4, WIlliams should continue to remain heavily involved against the Houston Texans. The Texans have been extremely stingy against the run, though. Houston is surrendering just 86.7 rushing yards per clash, which is fifth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Javonte Williams scored three times in the second half of the last game for the Cowboys, leading a thrilling comeback victory over the Texans. Williams is averaging just 3.7 yards per tote this season, but has six combined touchdowns through four outings. He has also made his presence felt in the passing game with 15 receptions over that span. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been stellar against the run in 2026. The Bucs are allowing just 78.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is third in the NFL. In addition, Tampa Bay has yielded just one rushing touchdown through four games.
outlooksByWeek.6: Javonte Williams found the end zone yet again last game for Dallas. Williams rushed 12 times for 45 yards and the score, notching his sixth rushing touchdown of the young season. Williams is averaging just 3.7 yards per tote, but has received double-digit carries in every contest in 2026. In Week 6, Williams looks primed for another jaunt to the end zone versus the Packers. Green Bay has given up eight rushing touchdowns already this season, which is 31st in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Javonte Williams found the end zone yet again for Dallas last game. Williams rushed 11 times for 41 yards in the 23-13 loss to the Packers. Williams has scored in four-straight games for the Cowboys, though is averaging just 3.7 yards per tote overall. In fact, he has failed to cross the 50-yard rushing mark in two-straight games. In Week 7, Williams will face a sliding Eagles defense. Philadelphia is allowing 119.3 rushing yards per contest, which is 19th in the league. The Eagles have also yielded eight rushing touchdowns, which is tied for 28th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams re-signed with the Cowboys following a successful first year with the team. After failing to produce a top-25 fantasy campaign during his final three seasons in Denver, Williams finished 12th in 2025, setting career-best marks in carries, rushing yards, touches (287), scrimmage yards (1,338) and yards per carry (4.77). He also scored a career-high 13 touchdowns after totaling 16 during his first four campaigns, and his 16 carries inside the 5-yard line were fifth most among backs. That helped offset his receiving struggles, as his 2.7 yards per target was last among qualified RBs. With minimal competition for touches in a high-scoring Dallas offense, the 26-year-old is a solid RB2 target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ladd McConkey seemed headed for a big performance in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals, catching five of seven targets for 81 yards and a touchdown. However, he was knocked out of the game in the third quarter after a big hit left him with a rib injury. McConkey still led the team in receiving yards and was on the receiving end of Justin Herbert's only TD pass, and the club doesn't seem to believe the injury is serious. His status for Week 2 will remain up in the air until later in the week, if not right up to kickoff. If he is able to suit up, McConkey will be facing a Raiders secondary that was tied for 21st in points per game allowed to WRs last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ladd McConkey was clearly limited by a rib injury in the Chargers' Week 2 loss to the Raiders, catching all three of his targets for 35 yards. That was still good enough to tie for the team lead in receptions, however, as Justin Herbert and the entire offense continue to adjust to the new scheme instituted by OC Mike McDaniel. McConkey is Herbert's clear top downfield option, and as he gets healthier, his production should begin to look more like the 5-82-1 line he delivered in the season opener before getting hurt in the third quarter. McConkey will get a favorable matchup in Week 3 against a Bills secondary that's given up the fourth-most receiving yards to WRs so far this year.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ladd McConkey seemed hampered by his rib injury in the Chargers' Week 3 loss to the Bills, but he still managed to turn five targets into four catches for 66 yards. The clear top option for Justin Herbert, McConkey has 15 targets through three games despite missing most of the second half in Week 2 after getting hurt, turning that volume into a 12-183-1 line. That's the only touchdown Herbert has thrown to a wide receiver so far in 2026. McConkey should be a little healthier in Week 4, but he'll be facing a Seahawks secondary that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ladd McConkey failed to catch either of his targets in the Chargers' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, leaving the game early after aggravating a foot injury he picked up in practice during the week. The third-year wideout was already playing through a rib issue, and an absence of one or more games seems almost assured. The Chargers' passing game has struggled with or without him on the field, but if McConkey does miss time, Quentin Johnston and Tre' Harris would become Justin Herbert's top downfield options in Week 5 against a Broncos secondary that ranks eighth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs but which could be missing its top two cornerbacks, including Patrick Surtain.
outlooksByWeek.6: Ladd McConkey continues to deal with injuries, sitting out the Chargers' Week 5 loss to the Broncos with a foot issue after dealing with a rib injury earlier in the season. He hasn't caught a pass since Week 3, but in those first three games, McConkey managed a 12-183-1 line on 15 targets as Justin Herbert's clear No. 1 option. The rest of the team's wide receiver room is also banged up, which could give the team extra incentive to get McConkey back in the lineup as quickly as possible. Even if he suits up in Week 6, he'll struggle to contribute against a Kansas City secondary that ranks first in the NFL in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Ladd McConkey has only missed one game so far in 2026, but injuries have marred the season for the Chargers' top wide receiver, and he comes out of the team's bye still in the league's concussion protocol. The offense as a whole has struggled, but McConkey's been productive when reasonably healthy, posting a 12-182-1 line on 15 targets over the first three weeks. If he's cleared to return in Week 8, he'll take on a stingy Rams secondary that ranks fifth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: McConkey is looking to rebound after falling short of high expectations in 2025. The 2024 second-round pick was terrific as a rookie (82-1,155-7 receiving line and a 12th-place finish among WRs in fantasy points), but dipped to 66-789-6 line and a 30th-place finish last season. Though he ran considerably more routes, saw similar target numbers and was used a lot more near the goal line (seventh among WRs with 12 end zone targets), McConkey's efficiency plummeted, with his catch rate dipping from 74% to 62% and his yards per target from 10.4 to 7.4. The good news is that there's reason for optimism that he'll bounce back, as he has a new playcaller in Mike McDaniel, the Chargers' offense figures to improve with a much healthier line, and Keenan Allen is out of the picture. McConkey, 24, makes for a fine fantasy WR3.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jakobi Meyers maintains a high floor, though he's a low-ceiling fantasy WR3 or flex play for Jacksonville's Week 2 home game against Denver's elite defense. Meyers has posted at least 39 receiving yards in all 10 of his games with the Jaguars since coming over in a midseason trade last year, including 40 receiving yards and a TD in the Week 1 win over Cleveland. Parker Washington and Brian Thomas have more downfield playmaking capability, but Meyers should see his share of short targets with Trevor Lawrence likely looking to get the ball out quickly to counter a Broncos pass rush that led the league with 68 sacks last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jakobi Meyers has been targeted just three times through Jacksonville's first two games. That lack of volume makes him hard to trust as anything more than a deep-league dart throw in Week 3 against a Patriots defense that held the Seahawks and Steelers to a combined 16 points. Parker Washington (18 targets), Brian Thomas (11 targets), and even TE Brenton Strange (five targets) have all been higher on Trevor Lawrence's priority list than Meyers. To the veteran wide receiver's credit, Meyers's 28-yard effort on one target in the Week 2 loss to Denver marked the first time in 11 games as a member of the Jaguars that he failed to record at least 39 receiving yards. Therefore, he could rebuild a solid fantasy floor if Lawrence starts looking Meyers's way more frequently.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jakobi Meyers led the Jaguars with seven catches for 64 yards and a touchdown on eight targets in Week 3 against the Patriots after catching all three of his targets for 68 yards and a TD across Jacksonville's first two games. The veteran wideout has been playing alongside Parker Washington in two-WR sets and working ahead of Brian Thomas, as Meyers' 79% snap share this season is nearly double Thomas' mark. Washington is the clear No. 1 receiving option for the Jaguars, but Meyers is shaping up as the team's next-most reliable pass catcher, which is enough to be deployed as a WR3 or flex option in Week 4 against the Bengals, who didn't allow a touchdown pass through Week 2 before giving up TDs to three separate Steelers wideouts in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jakobi Meyers has been efficient with his opportunities for the Jaguars, catching 13 of 15 targets for 165 yards and two touchdowns heading into a Week 5 trip to London to face the Eagles. His usage has fluctuated in a Jacksonville passing game with many mouths to feed, but Meyers is a viable flex option for Week 5, especially in deeper leagues. The Eagles are giving up 164 yards and one receiving touchdown per game to WRs, and they could be without top CB Quinyon Mitchell (knee) in Week 5, which would make things easier for some combination of Meyers, Parker Washington, Brian Thomas, and Josh Cameron.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jakobi Meyers is averaging 40 yards per game and has scored twice through five outings heading into Jacksonville's Week 6 matchup with the Texans in London. Houston has struggled to cover wide receivers, having allowed 193 yards per game and six TDs to the position through five games. Meyers is a distant second on the WR depth chart behind Parker Washington, but the plus matchup makes Meyers a viable flex option.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jakobi Meyers has established himself as the No. 2 WR for the Jaguars behind Parker Washington, putting Meyers firmly in the fantasy flex conversation for a Week 8 home game against the Colts. Meyers is averaging 48 receiving yards on 4.7 targets per game, and he set season highs in both of those categories with 83 yards on 10 targets in Jacksonville's Week 6 loss to the Texans prior to a Week 7 bye. The veteran wideout faced the Colts three times last season. Two of those meetings came after Meyers was acquired by the Jaguars in a midseason trade, and he mustered exactly 39 receiving yards in both games while scoring a touchdown in one of those matchups. He has five TDs in 15 regular-season games with Jacksonville.

player.seasonOutlook: One of the league's most underrated players, Meyers is entering his first full season with Jacksonville after being acquired via trade in November. The 2019 UDFA has produced 800-plus receiving yards in five consecutive seasons while operating primarily as a short-to-intermediate target. More of a solid producer than a high-ceiling contributor, Meyers has finished no lower than 32nd in fantasy points over the last five seasons, but has yet to do better than 19th. The 29-year-old isn't much of a touchdown scorer (23 TDs in 78 games since 2021) and has substantial target competition via Parker Washington, Brian Thomas Jr., Brenton Strange and Travis Hunter. Meyers is a good player, but is likely to cap out as a flex option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jason Myers will look to remain perfect this season when the Seahawks visit Arizona in Week 2. Myers made his lone PAT try and both field-goal attempts in a season-opening win over New England, though his FGs were relative chip shots from 30 and 26 yards. Myers made nine field goals from 50-plus yards out each of the previous two seasons, however, so he has plenty of leg to convert from that distance when called upon. The Cardinals aren't expected to be a top NFL defense this year, but they performed well in limiting the Chargers to 14 points in a Week 1 victory.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jason Myers has provided Seattle with a steady boot this season heading into a Week 3 matchup against Washington. The veteran kicker has made all three of his field-goal tries and all five of his PAT attempts through two weeks. However, he hasn't yet been asked to hit from distance, as none of his FG tries have been from 40 yards or greater. The Commanders have yielded a whopping 30.5 points per game through two weeks, so Myers could get plenty of opportunities to kick in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jason Myers enters Seattle's Week 4 clash against the Chargers having not missed a kick so far this season. Myers handled only relatively short kicks over his first two games, but he showed off his leg with a 57-yard field goal against Washington in Week 3. The veteran kicker is now 4-for-4 on FG tries and 9-for-9 on extra-point attempts this season. Opponents have gone 6-for-7 on field-goal attempts against the Chargers so far this year.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jason Myers has had a quiet campaign so far with Seattle on tap to host San Francisco in Week 5. After attempting a career-high 48 field goals in 2025, Myers has had just five FG tries so far this season, making all of them. He's been more active kicking extra points, making 12 of 13 PATs. Perhaps Myers will be relied upon more versus the 49ers, who have allowed just five extra-point tries as opposed to nine FG attempts so far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jason Myers is coming off a huge fantasy performance with Seattle's Week 6 matchup in the Denver altitude on tap. Myers made all five of his field-goal tries and both of his extra-point attempts in a loss to San Francisco this past Sunday, with all five of his FGs coming from 40-plus yards. Fantasy managers who roster Myers were likely waiting for this type of performance, as the veteran kicker had attempted (and made) only five field goals combined over the first four weeks of the campaign. Opponents are 9-for-11 in FG attempts against the Broncos this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jason Meyers and the Seahawks are back home to face off against the 5-0 Chiefs on Sunday Night Football in Week 7. He went 2-for-3 on field-goal attempts and did not attempt a PAT during Seattle's 17-14 overtime loss in Week 6. The missed field goal was his first of the season, giving the 35-year-old a 12-for-13 (92.3%) tally through six games. Meyers and the Seahawks offense could struggle to operate versus a Kansas City defense allowing 16.6 points per game, which is the second-best mark in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jason Myers is in the midst of one of his most accurate NFL seasons going into Seattle's Week 8 matchup against Chicago. Myers has gone 14-for-15 on field-goal tries through seven games and is 16-for-17 on PAT attempts. He's made all three of his field-goal tries from 50-plus yards, with his only miss this season being a 47-yard attempt. However, the Bears haven't yielded many FG tries, allowing just 10 through seven weeks.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ryan Flournoy managed two catches for 22 yards on four targets in the Week 1 loss for Dallas to the Giants. Flournoy finished fourth on the team in targets for the game. The Dallas passing attack struggled as a whole, leaving no receiver with more than 45 yards receiving in the contest. In Week 2, the Cowboys will look to rebound versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ryan Flournoy managed six targets last game for Dallas. Flournoy parlayed those looks into five catches for 23 yards. Flournoy was third in targets behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ryan Flournoy tied for the second on the Cowboys in targets last game. Flournoy saw eight balls thrown his way, though managed just two catches in the 34-31 loss to the Ravens. Flournoy also gained just 22 yards for the game; in fact, he has yet to gain more than 25 yards in any contest in 2026. In Week 4, Dallas faces a Houston defense that has been surprisingly subpar against the pass.  The Texans are allowing 238.7 passing yards per clash, which is 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ryan Flournoy has been targeted at least four times in every game this season for the Cowboys. However, he has yet to cross 40 yards receiving in any contest. Versus the Texans, he had four catches but only for a season-high 37 yards. With a lot of mouths to feed like CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and even tight end Jake Ferguson, Flournoy's output may continue to be depressed. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in terms of yardage. The Bucs are allowing just 204.3 passing yards per tilt, which is ninth in the NFL. However, Tampa Bay has also given up seven throwing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the league. Flournoy is still looking for his first score of the season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Ryan Flournoy set a season high in receiving yardage last game for the Cowboys. Flournoy brought in three passes for 90 yards in the 24-16 loss to the Bucs. CeeDee Lamb was dealing with a quadriceps issue, which also likely contributed to Flournoy's success. However, Lamb's injury does not appear serious, which would knock Flournoy back down the pecking order in Week 6 versus the Packers. Green Bay's defense is also allowing just 181 passing yards per contest, which is fifth in the league. Likewise, the Packers have surrendered only six passing touchdowns on the season, which is tied for 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Ryan Flournoy found the end zone last game for Dallas. Flournoy reeled in seven passes for 40 yards and the score in the 23-13 loss to the Packers. Flournoy has at least four targets in every game this season, though has gone over 40 yards receiving just once. He remains firmly behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens heading into a Week 7 clash with Philly. The Eagles are allowing 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL. However, Philadelphia has given up just eight passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 14th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Ryan Flournoy was second on the Cowboys in receiving yards last game. Flournoy reeled in four passes for 70 yards in the 38-21 win over the Eagles. Flournoy has at least three catches in four-straight contests. In Week 8, the Cowboys will face an Arizona Cardinals defense that has been prone to surrendering the touchdown pass. In fact, Arizona has given up 17 passing scores, which is dead last in the NFL. The Cardinals are also giving up 228 passing yards per tilt, which is 20th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Flournoy is an intriguing deep sleeper as the favorite for No. 3 wide receiver duties behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens in Dallas. Flournoy flashed in 2025, putting up 14.2 fantasy PPG during the only five games in which his route participation was at least 60%. Flournoy did disappear quite a bit behind the heavily targeted Lamb and Pickens (three or fewer targets in seven of his final 10 games), so he's a long shot for standalone fantasy value even if he locks down the No. 3 gig. The 26-year-old should be added to rosters only if Lamb or Pickens are sidelined.

outlooksByWeek.2: Christian McCaffrey heads into a Week 2 matchup against Miami with perhaps a bit less pressure to carry the 49ers' offense. Whereas McCaffrey led the NFL with 413 touches last season, he logged a modest 15 in last Thursday's Week 1 win over the Rams. Rookie Kaelon Black actually got more carries (14) than McCaffrey (10), though McCaffrey was still productive with 68 rushing yards along with 20 receiving yards on five catches. McCaffrey could feast upon a Dolphins defense that allowed Ashton Jeanty to accumulate 147 total yards and two touchdowns in a season-opening loss to Las Vegas.
outlooksByWeek.3: Christian McCaffrey will look to once again show off his dual-threat skill set when the 49ers host the Cardinals in Week 3. McCaffrey is coming off a productive game against the Dolphins,  totaling 66 yards (23 rushing, 43 receiving) and getting into the end zone twice.
