Henderson had one more rush than Rhamondre Stevenson in this shared backfield in Week 4 but converted his 14 carries into only 42 yards. Henderson has not been a factor in the passing game, catching just one ball on the season. Las Vegas is allowing 4.97 yards per carry and has been picked apart by Kenneth Walker and Omarion Hampton, so Henderson appears set up for an ideal opportunity at a few long runs even if the volume won't be high.
outlooksByWeek.6: TreVeyon Henderson is uncertain for Week 6 when the Patriots face the Jets due to an ankle injury. When healthy, he hasn't logged more than a 37% snap share in any of the last three games and has only two catches on the season. The Jets have not faced a prolific rushing offense through five games but have allowed two opposing backs to gain at least 99 yards. If active, a split role with Rhamondre Stevenson caps Henderson's appeal against a defense allowing a stingy 4.3 yards per carry.
outlooksByWeek.7: TreVeyon Henderson figures to handle a modest workload in the Patriots' Week 7 matchup against the Bears. Making a surprise appearance in Week 6 after suffering a high-ankle sprain, Henderson recorded seven carries for 31 yards while also catching his third pass of the season. Rhamondre Stevenson continues to garner a bigger workload but has plodded to a career-low 3.7 yards per carry. Until New England trusts Henderson in pass protection and ball security, however, a change in roles appears unlikely. Facing a Chicago defense on a short turnaround with Week 7's Thursday night kickoff, Henderson will need to solve a run defense that's allowed just three touchdowns to date.
outlooksByWeek.8: TreVeyon Henderson's declining role in the Patriots' rushing approach leads to low expectations in a Week 8 matchup against the Dolphins. He has logged single-digit carries in three straight games and sits with a 3.9 yards per carry average after a 5.1 mark as a rookie. He's also only caught four passes, an area where Miami has been particularly vulnerable against running backs. With New England seemingly happy to distribute the workload across multiple players, an uptick in usage for Henderson appears unlikely.

player.seasonOutlook: Henderson enters Year 2 after a roller-coaster rookie campaign in which he delivered three huge fantasy performances (28-plus points in all three) but otherwise played second fiddle to Rhamondre Stevenson (8.3 points per game in his other 14 games). Though his role was limited, Henderson was effective, averaging 5.1 yards per carry (eighth best) and catching 83% of his targets while scoring 10 touchdowns. The 2025 second-round pick is a candidate for a similar role in 2026, but it's unlikely that Stevenson will completely disappear after he also had a strong 2025. Henderson is safest as a bench option, but there's upside for a lot more if the 23-year-old is promoted to a lead role.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jameson Williams will seek to convert on more of his looks as the Lions travel to Buffalo in Week 2. Williams garnered nine targets against the Saints in Week 1, but he reeled in just four of them for 45 yards. The fifth-year wide receiver will need to keep his catch rate well above 50 percent if he hopes to record a third-straight 1,000-yard campaign, but he'll luckily face a Bills defense that allowed the seventh-most PPR points (40.0) to wide receivers in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jameson Williams will look to do more as the Lions play the Jets in Week 3. Williams' output has been disappointing so far this season, with just six catches for 78 yards across two games. The fifth-year wideout has also reaped no benefits from Detroit's struggling defense, with Amon-Ra St. Brown currently carving out a monopoly in the wide receiver room. Williams will face a New York defense that's allowed 27.2 PPR points per game to its first two opponents, a top-10 mark.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jameson Williams has yet to find the end zone heading into the Lions' Week 4 game at Carolina. Williams totaled a season-high 49 yards against the Jets in Week 3, but he's now recorded four or less catches for 50 or fewer yards in every game this year. The fifth-year wideout will seek to get more out of Detroit's offensive success against a Panthers defense that's allowed a top-five 23.2 fantasy points per game to wide receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jameson Williams will look to build off a big outing as the Lions travel to Arizona in Week 5. Williams had his best game of the year in Week 4 against the Panthers, bringing in six of eight targets for 102 yards. The speedster has still posted just a 16-229-0 receiving line to start the season, but he has seen eight or more targets in two games, which could bode well for his output. He'll also face a Cardinals defense that's ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jameson Williams will seek to stay involved as the Lions play the Packers in Week 7. Williams found the end zone twice in a Week 5 win over the Cardinals before Detroit's bye week, which was done with two catches for 47 yards. The fifth-year wideout has now totaled 18 grabs for 276 yards and two scores on the season. He'll face a Green Bay secondary that's ranked in the middle versus fantasy WRs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jameson Williams will aim to keep it rolling as the Lions play the Vikings in Week 8. Williams produced his best fantasy performance of the year in a Week 7 win over Green Bay, hauling in five of nine targets for 91 yards and two touchdowns. The speedy wideout has now produced four touchdowns in his last two games, along with seven catches for 138 yards in that stretch. He'll face a Minnesota defense that's ranked fourth in fantasy points allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: The slow start to Williams' career is a thing of the past after the speedster delivered 1,000-plus-yard campaigns each of the past two seasons. After breaking out with a 22nd-place fantasy finish (25th PPG) in 2024, Williams set new career highs in targets, catches, yards and touchdowns en route to a 12th-place finish (19th PPG) last season. A lack of goal-line work (eight career end zone targets) and some drop woes (NFL-high eight in 2025) are drawbacks, but Williams' explosive-play ability has led him to finish sixth or better in yards per reception and yards per target each of the past two seasons. The 25-year-old remains one of Jared Goff's top targets in Detroit's high-scoring offense and is a fine fantasy WR3 target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Aaron Jones is primed to lead Minnesota's backfield in Week 2 at Chicago. Jones (29 of 65 offensive snaps) and Jordan Mason (30 snaps) had a near-even split of the backfield reps in Week 1, but Mason led the ground attack with 59 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries. Jones still remained heavily involved, as he logged 12 rushes for 40 yards and one touchdown. This week and beyond, Jones will be set to lead the backfield with Mason on IR for a thumb injury. Jones will look to make the most of his likely increased opportunities against a Bears defense that allowed 33.7 PPR points to Panthers running backs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Aaron Jones should continue to have a high-usage role as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Jones saw a big workload in Week 2 with Jordan Mason (thumb) on IR, rushing the ball 23 times for 105 yards. The veteran running back should continue to have a huge role in the coming weeks, while questions remain with the passing game under returning quarterback Kyler Murray. Jones will face a Buccaneers defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 19.5 PPR points per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Aaron Jones should remain a high-volume option as the Vikings play Miami in Week 3. Jones saw a big workload in Week 3 once again with Jordan Mason (thumb) on IR, rushing the ball 17 times for 58 yards and recording five catches for 34 yards. The veteran running back's high share in the backfield doesn't look to be changing with Mason out another week, even with DeeJay Dallas and Demond Claiborne fighting for touches. Jones will face a Miami defense that's allowed the most fantasy points per game (32.9) to running backs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Aaron Jones will remain a high-usage option as the Vikings travel to New Orleans in Week 5. Jones saw a big workload in Week 4 once again with Jordan Mason (thumb) on IR, rushing the ball 20 times for 94 yards and recording four catches for 34 yards. The veteran running back's high share in the backfield shouldn't change with Mason out another week, even with DeeJay Dallas and Demond Claiborne fighting for touches. Jones will face a Saints defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack versus fantasy RBs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.7: Aaron Jones could be set to share the backfield in Week 7 as the Vikings play the Colts. Jones logged his best game of the season in Week 5 against the Saints before Minnesota's bye, rushing the ball 25 times for 113 yards and a touchdown. The veteran could unfortunately now be in store for a shared role again, as position mate Jordan Mason is primed to return from IR, but the two have proven to be productive together in the past. Indy's defense has ranked 23rd in fantasy points allowed to RBs so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.8: Aaron Jones could be at risk of missing Week 8 as the Vikings travel to Detroit. Jones suffered a knee injury in Minnesota's Week 7 win over the Colts, and he's currently day-to-day. What this means for his status moving forward is unknown until practices start up this week, but it is promising that he avoided a significant injury. The veteran running back logged eight carries for 26 yards before his departure, and it appeared he was still holding a prominent role even with Jordan Mason back on the field. If Jones can get healthy, he'll face a Lions defense that's ranked 11th in fantasy points allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Jones is back for a third season in Minnesota after an injury-plagued 2025 campaign limited him to 747 yards (his fewest since his rookie season in 2017) and three touchdowns in 12 games. Jones remained fairly busy (11.0 carries and 3.4 targets per game) but didn't perform well, ranking dead last among 65 backs with 50-plus carries in forced missed tackle rate and elusive rating, per PFF. Jones failed to record a single top-10 fantasy outing. Now 31 years old, Jones remains a starter and will get some run, but he's well past his prime and unlikely to return to consistent fantasy output. Jones is best valued as a bench player with occasional flex appeal.

outlooksByWeek.2: RJ Harvey's workload was limited in the Broncos' season-opening loss to Kansas City. He gained 18 rushing yards on three carries and caught all four of his targets for 23 yards. That volume was comparable to J.K. Dobbins, who got eight touches-all carries-to Harvey's seven. Turnovers and game flow played a part in limiting their opportunities. Harvey's role as the primary pass-catching back still bodes well for his production in his second NFL season after posting a 47-356-5 line on 58 targets over 17 regular-season games in 2025. He'll get a potentially tough matchup in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that ranked third in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: RJ Harvey wasn't able to suit up in Week 2's win over the Jaguars due to a hamstring strain, putting his availability for a Week 3 matchup against the Rams in question. The second-year back was expected to be the pass-catching complement to J.K. Dobbins for the Broncos, but rookie Jonah Coleman handled that role and didn't look out of place. If Harvey misses too much time, Coleman could take his job, but Dobbins' own checkered injury history could leave Denver patching together a backfield from whoever is healthy.
outlooksByWeek.4: RJ Harvey returned from a one-game absence due to a hamstring strain in Week 2 to contribute to the Broncos' Week 3 win over the Rams, gaining just six rushing yards on two carries but producing a 6-41-0 line on seven targets. The second-year back is secure in his role as Denver's top pass-catcher out of the backfield while J.K. Dobbins is the main option on early downs. Rookie Jonah Coleman could challenge both once he's back from IR. Harvey will look to make a bigger impact in Week 4 against a 49ers defense that's already given up 17 catches to RBs this season, 28th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: RJ Harvey is coming off the best performance of his career as a pass catcher, posting a 10-68-0 line on 10 targets while adding 25 rushing yards on seven carries in the Broncos' Week 4 loss to the 49ers. Denver trailed most of the game, which helped boost the second-year back's usage, but J.K. Dobbins' struggles in the early-down role are also opening the door for Harvey to log more touches in general, as his seven carries were also a season high. The eventual return of rookie Jonah Coleman from a high-ankle sprain could shake up the backfield further, but until then Harvey's arrow appears to be pointed up. He'll look to build on last week's effort in Week 5 against a Chargers defense that ranks 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs..
outlooksByWeek.6: RJ Harvey all but vanished from the Broncos' game plan in Week 5, gaining seven yards on three carries and failing to catch his only target as Sean Payton returned to play-calling duties. His usage as a pass-catcher was especially disappointing after the second-year back was fed 17 targets over the prior two weeks, turning that volume into a 16-109-0 line. J.K. Dobbins is the preferred early-down option in the backfield, and Harvey's value could become very dependent on game flow as a result. He might see more work in Week 6 if Denver falls behind early against a Seattle team that's in the bottom seven in the league in receptions per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: RJ Harvey found the end zone for the first time in 2026 during the Broncos' overtime win over the Seahawks in Week 6. The second-year running back managed just 56 scrimmage yards on nine touches as he continues to work behind J.K. Dobbins in the backfield. Harvey's target volume has declined since Sean Payton took back play-calling duties, notching only five targets the last two weeks while producing a 3-31-0 line through the air. Harvey will try to reclaim a more consistent role in Week 7 against a Cardinals defense that ranks 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: RJ Harvey logged just five touches in the Broncos' Week 7 win over the Cardinals, but he turned one of them into a 52-yard TD reception in the third quarter to salvage his day. The second-year back finished third in the backfield in workload behind rookie Jonah Coleman (11 touches) and veteran J.K. Dobbins (six touches), but Harvey seems to have a steady role as a passing-down option for Bo Nix. Even if Sean Payton continues to roll with a committee approach to his ground game, Harvey's floor should be relatively secure, even if his ceiling is limited to occasional big plays. He's unlikely to make a splash in Week 8 against a Kansas City defense that ranks seventh in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Harvey will go into his sophomore campaign looking to overtake J.K. Dobbins as Denver's lead back. In the 10 games in which both backs were active last season, Harvey handled 50 carries (20% team share) and 29 targets (9%), compared to Dobbins' 153 carries (60%) and 15 targets (4%). With Dobbins sidelined for the team's remaining nine games (including the playoff run), Harvey handled 115 carries (55%) and 41 targets (13%). He averaged 10.0 fantasy points with Dobbins and 14.2 without, though his 3.3 yards per carry during the final nine games was very poor. The entire Denver backfield is set to return in 2026, so similar deployment (which would include receiving specialist Tyler Badie) could be in the cards, though fourth-round rookie Jonah Coleman could factor in eventually as well. Harvey, 25, has a slight bit of breakout potential, but the committee setup suggests he's safest viewed as no more than a flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Matthew Stafford and the Rams will look to bounce back from a rough season-opening loss when they face the Giants in Week 2. Stafford threw for just 155 yards with no TDs and one interception against San Francisco last Thursday. He did still manage to connect with favorite target Puka Nacua five times for 74 yards, but no other Rams pass catcher had more than 26 yards in the defeat. A matchup with the Giants awaits, but New York had good results against Dallas' passing game in Week 1, holding QB Dak Prescott to 175 yards with one interception, albeit with two TDs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Matthew Stafford will look to replicate a huge Week 2 performance when the Rams face Denver in Week 3. On Monday Night Football, Stafford threw for 327 yards and four touchdowns with one interception against the Giants. The reigning NFL MVP didn't have star wideout Puka Nacua (hip) for that contest, so he turned to veteran Davante Adams, who logged eight catches for 195 yards and two of Stafford's TDs. Denver could pose a more potent threat, as the Broncos have a talented secondary and have limited QBs to a 74.5 passer rating, fifth-best in the NFL, through two weeks.
outlooksByWeek.4: Matthew Stafford will look to help guide the Rams to a much-needed win in Week 4 against Philadelphia following a disappointing 1-2 start to the season. Stafford threw for 390 yards and two touchdowns in Week 3 against Denver, but he also tossed two costly interceptions, including a pick-six. The reigning NFL MVP already has four interceptions on his ledger through three contests after logging just eight interceptions across 17 regular-season games last year. The Eagles have yet to pick off a pass this year, and they just got torched by Bears QB Case Keenum for 247 passing yards and two touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.5: Matthew Stafford will look to clean things up in the turnover department when the Rams host Buffalo in Week 5. Stafford was picked off twice and didn't throw any touchdowns in Week 4 against Philadelphia, but he also threw for 317 yards and led Los Angeles to a comeback victory. Still, Stafford has recorded a mediocre 6:6 TD:INT through four games, with the pickoff total nearly reaching the eight interceptions he tossed across 17 regular-season contests during his MVP campaign last year. The Bills have given up 10 passing touchdowns and have picked off just two passes this year, so Week 5 may be a good opportunity for Stafford to get back on track.
outlooksByWeek.6: Matthew Stafford will look to help Los Angeles rebound from a crushing loss on Monday Night Football with a Week 6 matchup against Arizona. Stafford threw for 383 yards and three touchdowns in Week 5 against Buffalo, but the team was defeated in overtime. Still, it was an impressive showing for the reigning NFL MVP, as he posted his fourth consecutive effort of 300-plus passing yards. Stafford could be in for another big performance versus a Cardinals defense that has given up the second-highest passer rating (117.2) this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Matthew Stafford enters the Rams' Week 7 matchup against the Raiders having completed 164 of 249 passes for 1,794 yards, 11 touchdowns and six interceptions through six games. The veteran quarterback is averaging 299 passing yards per contest, but his production has been inconsistent, and Los Angeles has stumbled to a 2-4 record. The absence of Davante Adams, who is expected to miss six to 10 weeks with a hamstring injury, creates another obstacle for Stafford. However, Las Vegas has allowed the sixth-most fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season, making Stafford an appealing bounce-back candidate despite the Rams' recent offensive struggles.
outlooksByWeek.8: Matthew Stafford continues to put up prolific numbers for the Rams heading into a Week 8 matchup versus the Chargers. The reigning NFL MVP threw for 195 yards and three touchdowns against Las Vegas in Week 7, though he also tossed his seventh interception. Stafford has now compiled over 300 passing yards and/or multiple passing touchdowns in all but one game so far this season, and he leads the league with 1,989 total passing yards. The Chargers could at least offer some resistance, as they've allowed a modest 18.6 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks this season, ninth-best in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: The reigning NFL MVP, Stafford returns for his 18th NFL season and his fifth with the Rams. The 38-year-old is fresh off an elite season in which he led the NFL in passing yards and touchdowns, which allowed him nine top-10 fantasy weeks (tied for third most at the position). Stafford's third-place finish in fantasy points per game was his first top-10 finish since 2019, and some regression is likely due to a complete lack of rushing (65 or fewer rushing yards in five straight seasons and one rushing touchdown since 2017). Stafford still has receivers Puka Nacua and Davante Adams and a strong offensive line at his disposal, so another big passing season is possible. That's just enough to keep him in the fringe QB1 mix.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tucker Kraft should continue to have a big role in Green Bay's offense as they face the Jets in Week 2. Kraft reeled in three of six targets for 65 yards against the Vikings in Week 1, but he was definitely a huge focus of their defensive scheme. The star tight end will luckily face a New York defense that should be less menacing this Sunday, as they ceded a lower-half 15.4 PPR points per game to tight ends in the 2025 campaign.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tucker Kraft will look to get more involved as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Kraft was held to just two catches for 15 yards in Week 2, but Green Bay's passing attack was lacking for most of the game. The bruising tight end will seek to re-establish himself as a top outlet for quarterback Jordan Love. Luckily, an Atlanta defense that's allowed 20.7 PPR points per game to tight ends so far this season, 29th in the league, could be a great place to start.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tucker Kraft will seek to bounce back as the Packers play the Buccaneers in Week 4. Kraft brought in four of eight targets for 26 yards against the Falcons in Week 3, with some drops that are usually caught. The fourth-year tight end has now posted a 9-106-0 receiving line on 17 targets across the first three games of the season, which is underwhelming considering his start to last year. He'll face a Tampa Bay defense that's been tough on all but tight ends, allowing a bottom-10 183 receiving yards to the position this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tucker Kraft will seek to build on his best performance of the season as the Packers take on Chicago in Week 5. Kraft recorded a season-high six catches in Week 4 against the Buccaneers, which he converted for 42 yards and a touchdown. The star tight end has started the campaign with a 15-148-1 receiving line, which he could expand on well against Green Bay's biggest rival. Kraft will have a tough task against a Bears defense that's ranked top five against fantasy TEs across four games.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tucker Kraft will look to stay busy as the Packers play the Cowboys in Week 6. Kraft finished with a solid five catches for 64 yards and one rush for two yards against the Bears in Week 5, even with teammates Christian Watson and Matthew Golden combining for 12 receptions for 266 yards and two touchdowns. While the featured tight end has served a different purpose in Green Bay's passing game so far, he still holds a 20-212-1 receiving line on the year. He'll face a Dallas defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy TEs this year.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tucker Kraft will look to do more with his targets as the Packers play the Lions in Week 7. Kraft stayed involved in Week 6 against the Cowboys, catching five of eight targets for 37 yards. The fourth-year tight end has continued to get opportunities with a 25-249-1 receiving line off 37 targets, but he still sits behind the two-man punch of Matthew Golden and Christian Watson at this point in the year. Luckily for Kraft, the Lions have allowed the most fantasy points per game (31.9) to tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tucker Kraft will look to build off a solid showing as the Packers play the Panthers in Week 8. Kraft brought in four of six targets for 48 yards and his second touchdown of the season in Green Bay's Week 7 loss to the Lions. The featured tight end has now put up a 29-287-2 receiving line through the first seven games of the season. He'll face a Carolina defense that's ranked 20th in fantasy points allowed to TEs so far this campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: Kraft's steady career progression had him on the cusp of a full-on breakout last season, but all was derailed by a torn ACL in Week 9. Prior to the injury, Kraft had seen 10 targets in consecutive games, one of which included a career-high 33.3 fantasy points. Through Week 8, only Jake Ferguson had more fantasy points. Granted, Kraft took advantage of a super easy schedule and was way over his head in the TD department (six TDs with an expected total of 1.8 and only two end zone targets), but his boost in usage and terrific RAC skills (he has led the position in the category each of his three seasons) were enough to get him into the weekly TE1 mix. Kraft's recovery will need to be monitored, but even if he's ready for Week 1, a dip in production is possible in his first year back from the major injury. He's a risky middle-round target.

outlooksByWeek.3: Ollie Gordon's workload could increase if Jaylen Wright misses the Dolphins' Week 3 game against the Chiefs. Despite being No. 3 on the depth chart, Gordon has outsnapped Wright behind Miami's workhorse, De'Von Achane. Kansas City allowed stud Jonathan Taylor to rush for two scores in Week 2 but kept Denver's backs under control in Week 1. Barring an injury to Achane, it's difficult to envision a path to meaningful production for Gordon.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaylen Wright will have an elevated role for the Dolphins in Week 4 against the Vikings if he's able to overcome a foot issue that kept him out in Week 3. Miami lost De'Von Achane for the season due to a knee injury, leaving just Wright and Ollie Gordon to handle carries. With the Dolphins often falling behind in most matchups, Wright has the chance to be the preferred pass-catching option. Confidence isn't inspired facing a Vikings defense that's allowing just 3.1 yards per carry and 11 catches to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ollie Gordon could be emerging in the Dolphins' backfield heading into a Week 5 matchup with the Bengals. With De'Von Achane (knee) out, Gordon ran for 100 yards on just nine carries in Week 4, vastly outperforming Jaylen Wright, while also scoring a touchdown for the second straight week. Touches figure to remain low if the Dolphins are forced to play from behind early, but facing a defense that's allowing 4.5 yards per carry could lead to steady yardage without high volume, and Gordon will remain an option near the goal line.
outlooksByWeek.7: Ollie Gordon will likely continue to serve as the lead back for the Dolphins in Week 7 against the Jets. Prior to Miami's Week 6 bye, Gordon had 17 or 18 carries in two of three games. The lone outing with a decrease in carries was also his only 100-yard game, and he scored in each contest. Though he hasn't factored into the passing game, volume remains king for running backs, and Gordon appears to have that in a matchup against a defense that's allowing 4.2 yards per carry, resulting in the 11th-most fantasy points allowed.
outlooksByWeek.8: Ollie Gordon may be hindered by an unfavorable game flow in Week 8 when the Dolphins host the Patriots. He has scored in four straight games, topping 100 yards twice while amassing at least 17 carries three times. Jaylen Wright is uncertain to play in Week 8, which could result in 20-plus carries for Miami's only option in the backfield if they remain competitive and aren't forced to throw the entire second half. New England brings a mid-tier run defense into Week 8, allowing 4.1 yards per carry but just five rushing scores in seven games.

player.seasonOutlook: Gordon is battling Jaylen Wright for backup work behind lead back De'Von Achane in Miami. Gordon was used sparingly as a rookie and didn't exactly move the needle. The 2025 sixth-round pick averaged an ugly 2.84 yards per carry on 70 attempts and 3.6 yards per target on the nine balls thrown his way. Gordon is still very young (22 years old), and his size (6-foot-1, 226 pounds) adds to his long-term intrigue. He'll have some insurance appeal if he beats out Wright for primary backup duties.

outlooksByWeek.2: George Pickens was held to just 28 yards in the season opener for the Cowboys. Pickens did finish second on the team in targets with six, but was rather quiet still by his standards. Despite a porous secondary, the Giants kept the star wideouts for the Cowboys in check, leaving Pickens with an uninspiring output in Week 1. Pickens will look to rebound in Week 2 versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: George Pickens was second on the Cowboys in targets last game.  Pickens managed six catches for just 40 yards, though, as CeeDee Lamb went wild for Dallas. Lamb caught eight passes for 153 yards and two touchdowns in the win over Washington. Pickens has a disappointing nine catches for only 68 yards through two games for Dallas. The task may not get easier in Week 3, as Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: George Pickens is coming off his best game of the season for the Cowboys. Pickens led Dallas in targets with 11 opportunities, parlaying those looks into seven grabs for 82 yards in the 34-31 loss to the Ravens. However, Pickens has yet to find the end zone this season, and his overall numbers remain disappointing following a standout 2025 campaign. In Week 4, the Cowboys will face a Texans defense that has been surprisingly suspect against the pass in 2026.  Houston is allowing 238.7 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the NFL. Moreover, teammate CeeDee Lamb could be guarded by all-pro corner Derek Stingley Jr., which could free up Pickens for more targets.
outlooksByWeek.5: George Pickens has had back-to-back games with at least 75 yards receiving for the Cowboys. On the downside, Pickens was targeted just three times last game as compared to a staggering 21 targets for fellow wideout CeeDee Lamb. The targets are unlikely to be so lopsided in Week 5 versus the Bucs, but Pickens certainly appears to be playing second-fiddle to the aforementioned Lamb in 2026. Tampa Bay's defense has been fairly stingy against the pass in terms of yardage. The Bucs are allowing just 204.3 passing yards per tilt, which is ninth in the NFL. However, Tampa Bay has also given up seven throwing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: George Pickens stepped up last game for the Cowboys. CeeDee Lamb was limited to two catches for just nine yards as he was dealing with a quadriceps issue. As a result, Pickens was the primary target in the passing game and corralled nine of 13 targets for 130 yards and a touchdown.  Lamb is not expected to miss the Week 6 clash versus the Packers, though Pickens would benefit even if Lamb is limited. However, Green Bay's defense is allowing just 181 passing yards per contest, which is fifth in the league. Likewise, the Packers have surrendered only six passing touchdowns on the season, which is tied for 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: George Pickens led the Cowboys in receiving last game. With the Cowboys trailing for the entire contest, the passing game took center stage, though admittedly still struggled. Despite 11 looks, Pickens managed just 73 yards on six catches in the 23-13 loss to the Pack. Pickens has an impressive 24 targets over his last two contests alone. He will look to get back over the 100-yard receiving mark in Week 7 versus Philadelphia. The Eagles are allowing 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL. However, Philadelphia has given up just eight passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 14th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: George Pickens found the end zone last game for Dallas. Pickens snagged four passes for 57 yards and the touchdown. It was his second score in three outings. In Week 8, the Cowboys will face an Arizona Cardinals defense that has been prone to surrendering the touchdown pass. In fact, Arizona has given up 17 passing scores, which is dead last in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Pickens drew the franchise tag from Dallas after a career year in which he ranked near the top of the wide receiver position in most categories, including catches, yards, TDs, end zone targets (second with 18) and air yards (fourth with 1,576). Fantasy's No. 5-scoring receiver in 2025 certainly benefited from CeeDee Lamb missing time (24% target share, or 8.8 per game, and 24.2 fantasy PPG in four games Lamb was injured), but his "with Lamb" splits were also strong. Consider: In 12 full games with Lamb, Pickens handled a 23% target share (8.3 per game) and averaged 16.1 fantasy PPG, which would've ranked eighth at the position over the full season. The 25-year-old will play the same role in Dallas' high-scoring offense in 2026 and has the look of a strong fantasy WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Omar Cooper is uncertain to play for the Jets in Week 2 against the Packers due to an ankle sprain. In his NFL debut, he caught his only target for 30 yards. The Jets ran a heavy ground game to open the year, and while they will likely need to throw more in Week 2 to keep up, Cooper's role, even if healthy, is uncertain. The passing game should continue to flow heavily through Garrett Wilson, leaving Cooper's fantasy value volatile.
outlooksByWeek.7: Omar Cooper brings momentum into the Jets' Week 7 matchup with the Dolphins. Returning from a four-week absence due to an ankle issue, Cooper flashed with 103 yards and a touchdown on seven targets. The Jets remain a low-volume passing attack, and Miami has allowed the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing wide receivers, but Cooper provides a big-play option, averaging 19.0 yards per catch in limited action. He could offer a high-upside bye-week fill-in.
outlooksByWeek.8: Omar Cooper's two-week surge is set to extend into Week 8 when the Jets have an inviting matchup with the Raiders. Cooper has topped 100 yards and scored in consecutive outings since returning from an ankle injury, while snagging 11 of his 12 targets. The volume remains modest in a run-first offense, but Las Vegas is allowing 8.9 yards per target to opposing wide receivers with seven similar players registering at least 53 receiving yards.

player.seasonOutlook: Cooper was selected by the Jets in the first round of April's draft. The Indiana product is fresh off a breakout 2025 season in which he posted a 69-937-13 receiving line after totaling 46 catches during his first three seasons with the Hoosiers. Primarily a perimeter target in limited action from 2022 to 2024, Cooper aligned in the slot on 80% of his routes last season. He is a short-area target (9.0 aDOT last season), but still posted strong efficiency numbers, including a 2.61 YPRR. He'll begin his career behind Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell in New York's Geno Smith-led offense and is unlikely to produce consistent flex value as a rookie.

This already highly regarded defense only got stronger in June with the acquisition of two-time Defensive Player of the Year (2023, 2025) Myles Garrett. He wasn't their only addition, as CBs Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson were brought in from the Chiefs. Expect another productive season from this unit, though it does face one of the tougher early-season schedules, with the 49ers (Week 1), Broncos (3), Eagles (4) and Bills (5) among their first five opponents. The Rams' second-half schedule is one of the easiest, meaning they might be a better in-season trade target than a draft-day pickup.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Bass continues to be busy for the high-scoring Bills' offense as they enter a Week 2 matchup with the Lions. In Week 1, Bass made three extra points and three field goals, though none were 50-plus yards. Detroit's defense, particularly the secondary, was suspect a week ago, and the Bills should score plenty, making Bass appealing.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyler Bass will attempt to bounce back from his first miss of the season when the Bills host the Chargers in Week 3. Bass wasn't afforded a field goal try in Week 2, with Buffalo's offense finding the end zone with ease, but still provided a reasonable floor, hitting five of six extra points. The Bills' offensive efficiency could cap Bass' scoring potential, but historically, the highest-scoring kickers come from the highest-scoring teams.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Bass' opportunities have been limited ahead of a Week 4 matchup between the Bills and Patriots. Through three weeks, Bass has attempted only four field goals, though Buffalo's high-powered offense has generated 12 extra points. New England's defense remains stingy, allowing just 15 total points to opposing kickers, likely keeping Bass out of Week 4 consideration.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Bass remains a stable floor, low ceiling kicking option for the Bills as they enter a Week 5 matchup with the Rams. Bass has collected 14 extra points through four weeks as Buffalo routinely converts drives into touchdowns, but only six field goal attempts, where he's perfect, keeping his scoring capacity limited. The Rams' defense has been stingy to opposing kickers, so don't expect Week 5 to be Bass' breakout party.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tyler Bass is trending up as the Bills get set to face the Raiders in Week 6. Extra points will remain consistent in Buffalo's efficient offense, as Bass has at least three attempts in four of five games, but his field goals increased each of the last three weeks. Las Vegas, however, has been stingy to opposing kicker scoring, surrendering 16 PATs but just six field-goal tries as teams routinely convert drives into touchdowns. Bass' floor Sunday looks stable, but the ceiling may be low.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tyler Bass has increased his workload over the last three weeks as Buffalo gets set to face Baltimore in Week 8. Always a steady source for PATs in Buffalo's high-scoring offense (Bass has made at least two in every game), he went from four field goals across his first three games to nine over his last three. None have come from 50-plus yards, potentially keeping bonus scoring off the table. Baltimore is a mid-tier defense for points allowed to kickers, but they've allowed as many field goal attempts as extra points through seven games, setting Bass up for a strong Week 8.

outlooksByWeek.2: Wan'Dale Robinson had at least a share of the team lead in targets, catches, and receiving yards in his Titans debut, though he had a modest five catches for 38 yards on six targets. Tennessee's passing offense may not improve much, if at all, in Week 2 against an Eagles defense that allowed just six touchdowns to wide receivers last season, which tied for the fewest in the NFL. Robinson relies on target volume to make up for a lack of downfield playmaking capabilities, and the Titans may not throw often or effectively enough for him to make much of a fantasy difference. He's a low-end flex option for Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Wan'Dale Robinson is off to a slow start with the Titans, but he'll try to recapture his magic from last season with the Giants when he faces the Giants in Week 3. The shifty WR was peppered with short targets during his last couple seasons with the Giants, racking up 140 targets apiece in 2024 and 2025. After exceeding 1,000 receiving yards in 2025, Robinson signed a four-year, $78 million contract to join former Giants head coach and current Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll in Tennessee. Robinson is on pace for just 60 targets with his new team, so his involvement is likely to grow moving forward. It will be tough to trust Robinson until Tennessee's passing game shows some signs of life, but there is some deep-league fantasy flex appeal here for Week 3, especially in PPR formats, against a banged-up Giants secondary.
outlooksByWeek.4: Wan'Dale Robinson stepped up against his former team in Week 3 with seven catches for 57 yards and a touchdown on 11 targets against the Giants, but he had just 47 yards on seven targets in his first two games with the Titans. The 5-foot-8 wide receiver gets almost all of his production on short passes, but Robinson is a viable Week 4 flex option on the road against the heavily favored Ravens. The winless Titans may find themselves in another deep hole, which could allow Tennessee's low-octane passing game to make up for a lack of quality with quantity. Baltimore has allowed the second-most catches to wide receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Wan'Dale Robinson takes a two-game touchdown streak into Tennessee's Week 5 home game against the Texans, but he's averaging just 31 receiving yards per game as a Titan after coming over from the Giants in free agency. Houston has been surprisingly poor at defending wide receivers, allowing the second-most catches (60), receiving yards (830), and TDs (six) to the position. Robinson's inconsistent usage in a low-octane passing game makes him hard to trust, but he's a viable flex option for Week 5 given the Texans' struggles against his position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Wan'Dale Robinson is averaging just 35 receiving yards per game for the Titans heading into a Week 6 road affair against the Colts, who are allowing 160 receiving yards per game to wide receivers. Robinson has drawn at least five targets from Cam Ward in all but one game this season, and his steady involvement makes him a viable flex play for Week 6 against the Colts' beatable pass defense. However, Robinson's ceiling is capped due to the poor play of Tennessee's entire offense, which ranks last leaguewide with 11.6 points per game. Two of Ward's three touchdown passes through five games have gone to Robinson.
outlooksByWeek.7: Wan'Dale Robinson drew 30 targets from Titans QB Cam Ward over the past four games. Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll loved peppering Robinson with short targets when they were together on the Giants, and Daboll has maintained that philosophy in their new surroundings. Robinson has caught 19 of those 30 targets for 151 yards and two TDs, and his consistent involvement in Tennessee's offense gives him a respectable floor as a solid Week 7 flex option against the Browns, who are giving up 157 yards per game to WRs and have allowed seven TDs to the position through six games. Robinson and QB Cam Ward are the only Titans with multiple TDs this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Wan'Dale Robinson mustered just seven yards on four catches in the Titans' Week 7 loss to the Browns, and he's likely to continue earning a steady diet of short passes from Cam Ward in Week 8 against the Bengals. Robinson has 23 catches over the past five games but is averaging a career-low 7.1 yards per reception in his fifth NFL season and first with Tennessee. He's a high-floor, low-ceiling flex option for Week 8 against the Bengals, who are allowing 138 yards per game to wide receivers.

player.seasonOutlook: Robinson signed with the Titans after catching 90-plus passes each of the past two seasons. The 2022 second-round pick has progressively improved his production each season in the pros, peaking with a 30% target share (ninth among WRs), 1,014 yards (13th) and 13.6 fantasy PPG (16th) in 2025. An undersized, short-range slot target, Robinson isn't positioned for many big plays and is very rarely used near the goal line (he's yet to clear four TDs in a season and has 13 career end zone targets). In Tennessee, Robinson will battle rookie Carnell Tate and Calvin Ridley for the team lead in targets, but his potential for flex production will depend on whether Cam Ward is able to make a Year 2 leap. Robinson, 25, is a low-ceiling, middle-round target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Bijan Robinson will continue to lead Atlanta's offense in a Week 2 divisional matchup against the Panthers. Robinson received a whopping 29 touches in Week 1, tying Ashton Jeanty for the second-most in the NFL. The Texas product looked explosive despite the Falcons' offensive struggles, which is a good sign for his outlook going forward. Robinson is in for a great matchup as well, with the Panthers defense allowing 291 rushing yards and six rushing touchdowns in a Week 1 loss to the Bears.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bijan Robinson is expected to lead the Falcons' offense in the Week 3 matchup against the Packers, whose defense has given up 22.9 PPR fantasy points per game to running backs this season. Despite Atlanta's offensive struggles through two weeks, Robinson has continued to produce, having recorded 254 total yards and a touchdown on 48 touches. With Michael Penix back at the helm for the Week 3 contest, Robinson should be in for even more production. Additionally, he's in for a favorable matchup, as Green Bay's defense has allowed three rushing touchdowns in its first two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Bijan Robinson is expected to continue being the main playmaker on the Falcons' offense in the Week 4 matchup against the Saints. Robinson has been stellar despite Atlanta's offensive struggles three weeks into the season, accounting for 467 total yards and three touchdowns. He's already recorded 79 touches (26.3 per game) this year, suggesting this massive fantasy output will continue as the season progresses. Additionally, Robinson is in for a favorable Week 4 matchup against a Saints defense that's allowed 27.9 PPR fantasy points per game to the RB position.
outlooksByWeek.5: Bijan Robinson is expected to continue leading Atlanta's offense during the Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. Robinson has excelled through the Falcons' first four games, averaging 153.5 total yards per game and scoring five touchdowns on 99 touches. He ranks second in the NFL in total yards and will likely remain the focal point of a Falcons offense that's averaged 40 points per game over their last two contests. Despite this, Robinson is in for a difficult Wek 5 matchup against a Ravens defense that's allowed just 19.1 fantasy points per game to RBs this year.
outlooksByWeek.6: Bijan Robinson will lead Atlanta's offensive attack in the Week 6 matchup against the Bears. Robinson remained one of fantasy's top running backs in Week 5 despite the overtime loss, totaling 128 yards on 21 touches. He ranks as the No. 3 RB in all of fantasy through five contests, averaging a whopping 26.3 points per game. He could be in for a tough Week 6 matchup, however, as Chicago's defense has given up just 18.8 fantasy points per game this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Bijan Robinson is expected to remain the focal point of the Falcons' offense in the Week 7 matchup against the 49ers. Robinson logged a season-low nine carries in the Week 6 loss to the Bears, as Atlanta was trailing by 24 points in the second half. Despite this, he remained productive when given the opportunities, averaging 6.8 yards per carry. Expect Robinson to bounce back and remain one of fantasy's top running backs in Week 7, as San Francisco's defense has allowed 24.5 fantasy points per game to opposing RBs through five contests.
outlooksByWeek.8: Bijan Robinson is expected to remain the focal point of Atlanta's offense during the Week 8 matchup against the Buccaneers. Robinson has underwhelmed relative to his usual standards over the last two weeks, accounting for 175 total yards and no touchdowns on 36 touches. Despite the lack of scoring, Robinson has still managed to accumulate 4.3 yards per carry during that span. It will likely be tough for Robinson to have a bounce-back performance in Week 8 as well, with Tampa Bay's defense allowing just 18.2 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Robinson enters his fourth season having finished in the top five among running backs in carries, rushing yards, touches, yards and fantasy points in each of the past two seasons. Also a big factor as a receiver, he has ranked no lower than fifth at the position in routes, targets, receptions and receiving yards in his three pro seasons. In 2025, PFF tracked him with 86 forced missed tackles, which was easily the most among backs. The 24-year-old is in his prime and, though he has a new coach in Kevin Stefanski, his path to a massive offensive role remains clear. He's on the short list of players who should be considered with the first pick of your fantasy draft.

outlooksByWeek.2: Josh Allen appears to have the Bills' offense humming as they get set to host the Lions in Week 2. Facing a stout Texans defense last week, Allen accounted for 357 total yards and four touchdowns, against a unit he had previously struggled. No such fears should exist Thursday night, as the Lions' depleted secondary is coming off a game where they allowed 410 yards and three touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Josh Allen has the Bills offense firing on all cylinders heading into a Week 3 matchup with a slumping Chargers squad. Allen has thrown for five touchdowns and run in four in a dominating start to his 2026 season. The Chargers are a desperate team, but they'll also be traveling across the country and have been victimized by far less capable quarterbacks in Jacoby Brissett (277 yards, one TD) and Kirk Cousins (253/3), suggesting the elements are there for Allen to continue his elite production.
outlooksByWeek.4: Josh Allen will look for a bounce-back performance when the Bills face the Patriots in Week 4. Allen failed to throw a touchdown pass in Week 3 for the first time this season, while also tossing his first two interceptions. He rushed for two scores for the third straight week and has at least six carries in three straight games, but he's completed 20 passes or fewer in every outing. He'll oppose a familiar opponent in a Patriots defense that is allowing the third-fewest fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks despite yielding three touchdown passes by Trevor Lawrence in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Josh Allen brings a multi-touchdown streak into the Bills' Week 5 matchup at the Rams. Allen has provided multiple scores in each of Buffalo's first four games, throwing six scores while rushing for seven, though his yardage has topped 253 just once. The Rams, however, have allowed only one rushing touchdown and a mere 4.84 yards per pass attempt in what looks to be a battle of elite versus elite.
outlooksByWeek.6: Josh Allen looks to continue to provide elite returns when the Bills face the Raiders in Week 6. Allen is coming off his best rushing effort of the year in Week 5, finishing with 121 yards while scoring on the ground for the eighth time in five games, adding further upside to his reliable passing efforts. Facing a Raiders defense in Week 6 that's allowing the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks likely won't hinder Allen's appeal, as he's set for top-tier dual-threat production Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.8: Josh Allen hopes to have his full complement of receivers when the Bills come out of their bye to host the Ravens in Week 8. He failed to record a rushing score in Week 6 for the first time all season, but threw multiple touchdowns for the first time since Week 2, maintaining his elite fantasy scoring. This game could bring shootout potential if Baltimore gets Lamar Jackson back under center. Baltimore's defense has been solid against opposing passers, allowing just five touchdown passes in six games before being solved by Joe Burrow for four in Week 7. They've also allowed just one rushing touchdown to the position, but Allen is matchup-proof.

player.seasonOutlook: Allen enters his age-30 campaign having finished each of the past six seasons no worse than second among quarterbacks in fantasy points. Despite seeing less passing volume the past two seasons (14th or lower in pass attempts both years), the 2024 NFL MVP has finished in the top 10 in passing TDs six seasons in a row and remains a major threat with his legs (top five in carries and rushing TDs among quarterbacks all eight seasons of his career). Allen's 21.4 fantasy points per game in 2025 was actually his lowest since 2019, but it was still enough to lead the position. With Joe Brady returning as playcaller and the Bills adding a No. 1 receiver in DJ Moore, Allen remains an elite fantasy quarterback.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brock Bowers sat out the Raiders' season-opening win over the Dolphins after undergoing minor knee surgery just before the start of the campaign. The star tight end isn't expected to be out for long, and in his absence Michael Mayer will top the team's depth chart at the position, although running back Ashton Jeanty may have been the biggest beneficiary in terms of production against Miami. If Bowers is cleared to return in Week 2, he'll be facing a Chargers defense that finished fifth in PPR points allowed to TEs in 2025, although it couldn't contain Trey McBride to begin the current campaign.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brock Bowers is on track to make his season debut in Week 3 against the Saints after missing the Raiders' first two games due to minor knee surgery at the end of training camp. Knee trouble in 2025 prevented Bowers from repeating his dynamic rookie campaign, but if he's able to get fully healthy again, the star tight end should quickly emerge as the team's top option in the passing game, with little competition from a wide receiver room led by Tre Tucker. Bowers will initially be catching passes from Kirk Cousins, but at some point this season Las Vegas will transition to Fernando Mendoza under center, providing one more wrinkle for the offense. If he gets cleared this week as expected. Bowers will be facing a New Orleans defense that has yet to allow a touchdown to a TE in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brock Bowers made up for lost time after missing the Raiders' first two games while recovering from minor knee surgery. In his Week 3 season debut against the Saints, the star tight end turned 13 targets into a 10-116-1 receiving line. Bowers is the clear No. 1 downfield option for Kirk Cousins, especially considering the lack of talent in the wide receiver room, and as long as he can stay healthy, he should continue to see big volume. He's in a good position to put up big numbers again in Week 4 against a Kansas City defense that's been the stingiest in the league against WRs but ranks just 19th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Brock Bowers shook off an illness to once again be the Raiders' top receiving option in a Week 4 loss to Kansas City. He caught six of 11 targets for 86 yards and a touchdown, finding the end zone for a second straight game after missing the first two weeks of the year while completing his recovery from knee surgery. The star tight end is the most dangerous weapon in Kirk Cousins' arsenal, and he's likely to continue getting double-digit targets on a weekly basis while posting elite numbers. Bowers faces his toughest test of the season so far in Week 5 against a Patriots defense that has allowed the fewest fantasy points per game to TEs in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.6: Brock Bowers continues to make up for lost time, producing an 8-110-1 line on 10 targets in the Raiders' Week 5 loss to the Patriots. After missing the first two games of the season while completing his recovery from knee surgery, the superstar tight end has gotten into the end zone in three straight weeks, amassing 24 catches for 312 yards and three scores on 35 targets. Bowers is the clear top option for Kirk Cousins in the passing game, and that isn't likely to change even if Las Vegas eventually switches to rookie Fernando Mendoza under center. Bowers will face a Bills defense in Week 6 that ranks 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Brock Bowers was held somewhat in check by the Bills in Week 6, failing to get double-digit targets for the first time in 2026 and managing a 4-70-0 line on nine looks from Kirk Cousins. Fellow TE Michael Mayer popped for a big game, but Bowers probably won't stay contained for long. Over his four appearances this season, Bowers has a 28-382-3 line on 44 targets as the clear top option in the Raiders' passing game. He'll face a tough test in Week 7 against a Rams defense that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Brock Bowers has been held slightly in check the last two weeks, failing to see double-digit targets in either contest and managing a 10-143-0 line on 17 targets. Those are still strong numbers for a tight end, but a mild disappointment for an elite talent like Bowers. He remains the top option in the Raiders' passing game, even as No. 2 TE Michael Mayer continues to get more work than expected. Bowers will face a tough test in Week 8 against a Jets defense that ranks sixth in fantasy points per game allowed to tight ends, and which has given up just one TD to the position through seven games.

player.seasonOutlook: Bowers entered 2025 with high expectations and appeared well on his way to another productive season with 103 yards in Week 1, but a late-game injury limited him for three weeks and led to five full missed games. Bowers remained productive when healthy, finishing second among tight ends in fantasy PPG. Incredibly, he tied for fifth in the NFL with 13 end zone targets despite all the missed action. Bowers, who posted a 112-1,194-5 receiving line as a rookie in 2024, will be the top target for No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza. The 23-year-old is well positioned for a highly productive season and should be on your radar in the second or third round.

outlooksByWeek.2: David Montgomery scored three total TDs in his Texans debut in Week 1 and profiles as a borderline fantasy RB1 for a Week 2 home game against a Bengals defense that gave up 93 scrimmage yards and a score to Tampa Bay's Bucky Irving. Montgomery had 23 touches to Woody Marks' 10 in Week 1 against the Bills, so the former Lions RB is operating as the clear lead back for his new team. Montgomery's 23 Week 1 touches were more than he had in any game last season with Detroit. Cincinnati beefed up its defensive front in the offseason after allowing the most rushing yards in the NFL last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: David Montgomery produced just 24 scrimmage yards in Houston's Week 2 loss to the Bengals after scoring three TDs in his Texans debut. The veteran RB will cede some backfield work to Woody Marks, particularly if the Texans are forced to play catch-up, but Montgomery is the team's preferred option in valuable red-zone and short-yardage situations. Montgomery is poised for a bounce-back effort in Week 3 and can be trusted as a fantasy RB2 against a Colts defense that's allowing 177 yards per game on the ground.
outlooksByWeek.4: David Montgomery is averaging a paltry 2.8 yards per carry, and Houston's offensive line has struggled to open up holes heading into a Week 4 home game against the Cowboys. The offseason trade acquisition scored three TDs in his Texans' debut but hasn't found the end zone since. Through three games, Montgomery has out-touched Woody Marks 44-29, but Marks scored a one-yard touchdown in the Week 3 loss to the Colts, so Montgomery doesn't have a monopoly on short-yardage opportunities. The Cowboys are allowing 27.3 points per game and have surrendered four total TDs to RBs, so Montgomery is a fantasy RB2 for Week 4, albeit a touchdown-dependent one.
outlooksByWeek.5: David Montgomery has plodded to 2.7 yards per carry and has failed to find the end zone since scoring three TDs in Week 1, his Texans debut. Fellow Houston RB Woody Marks has scored twice during Montgomery's three-game touchdown drought. Montgomery and Marks will likely split carries again in Week 5 against the Titans, who are allowing 100 rushing yards per game to RBs, though Tennessee is giving up only 3.6 yards per carry. If Houston's defense can recapture last season's elite form and stifle the underwhelming Titans offense, Montgomery could get enough volume to wear down Tennessee's defense and make up for a lack of quality with quantity. With Houston's running game stuck in first gear, Montgomery is an unexciting flex candidate for Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.6: David Montgomery is considered week-to-week after departing Houston's Week 5 win over the Titans due to a groin injury. He's likely to sit out in Week 6 against the Jaguars, leaving Woody Marks to lead Houston's backfield against Jacksonville's league-best run defense in London. Montgomery is averaging just 2.7 yards per carry.
outlooksByWeek.7: David Montgomery (groin) sat out Houston's Week 6 win over the Jaguars and is considered week-to-week. If he returns for Week 7 against the Giants, Montgomery would likely split carries with Woody Marks and possibly Jawhar Jordan. Montgomery is averaging just 2.7 yards per carry. The Giants have struggled to defend RBs, allowing 108 rushing yards and one total TD per game to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: Montgomery was traded to Houston after spending his first seven NFL seasons with Chicago and Detroit. The veteran back is coming off a down year in 2025, when he posted career lows in touches (182), yardage (908, his first season under 1,000) and fantasy points per game (9.8). Montgomery was still effective as a rusher (4.53 yards per carry, 2.28 yards after contact) but lost work to Jahmyr Gibbs and wasn't involved much as receiver. The latter doesn't figure to change much in Houston, and while Montgomery is a decent bet to pace the team in carries, second-year back Woody Marks figures to sustain a substantial offensive role. Montgomery enters his age-29 season as a touchdown-dependent flex with limited upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Luther Burden will look to stay highly involved as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. While Week 1 was the highest-scoring game in NFL history, Burden and Chicago's pass-catching corps were overshadowed by a dominant ground game. The second-year wideout's five catches for 63 yards wasn't bad, but he definitely has potential to be more dominant moving forward. He'll take on a Minnesota defense that gave up a 6-147-2 receiving line to Christian Watson and 6-95-0 to Matthew Golden in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Luther Burden will aim to get things going as the Bears play the Eagles in Week 3. Burden has had a slow start to his sophomore campaign, with just eight catches on 12 targets for 95 yards across two games. He could also be in for even worse output, given the unknowns that come with Tyson Bagent starting under center in place of Caleb Williams (hamstring). Burden will take on a Philadelphia defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 29.4 PPR points per game to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Luther Burden will aim to build on an impressive performance as the Bears play the Jets in Week 4. Burden had his first big time of the season against the Eagles in Week 3, turning 11 targets into seven catches for 61 yards and a touchdown. The second-year wideout had a solid connection with veteran Case Keenum, who is likely to fill in under center for at least one more week, if not more. This bodes well for the future of Burden, but he will have to face a New York defense that's allowed the eleventh-least fantasy points per game (28.2) and fourth-least receiving yards (337) to wide receivers across three outings.
outlooksByWeek.5: Luther Burden will aim to stay involved as the Bears travel to Green Bay in Week 5. Burden tied his season high of 63 receiving yards in Week 4 against the Jets, and he's now recorded 60 or more yards in all but one game this season. The second-year wide receiver appears to be a pivotal part of Chicago's offense, and he could be a key piece towards a win in Tundratown. He'll face a Packers defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.6: Luther Burden will continue to be a top option in Chicago's passing game in Week 6 at Atlanta. Burden brought in four of six targets for a team-high 47 receiving yards and rushed the ball four times for two yards in a Week 5 blowout loss to the Packers. The second-year pass catcher has been unable to get things going in multiple games this season, but this can be attributed to the struggles at the quarterback position. No matter who is throwing him the ball, the Falcons ranking 27th in fantasy point allowed to wide receivers this campaign could be favorable for Burden.
outlooksByWeek.7: Luther Burden will seek to stay busy as the Bears play the Patriots in Week 7. Burden secured all eight of his targets for 95 yards in a Week 6 win over the Falcons, leading Chicago in receptions, receiving yards and targets. The second-year wideout has a 31-361-1 line on 43 targets across six games this season, and a dominant connection looks to be growing with quarterback Caleb Williams. Burden will now turn his sights to a New England defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.8: Luther Burden will look to build off a season-best performance as the Bears play the Seahawks in Week 8. Burden was on fire in Week 7 against the Patriots, turning four catches into 130 yards and a touchdown and taking his one carry for seven yards. The second-year pass catcher has now totaled 35 receptions for 491 yards and two touchdowns this season, and he's becoming Caleb Williams' favorite option in the passing game. Burden will now shift focus to a tough Seattle defense that's ranked first in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.

player.seasonOutlook: Burden enters his second NFL season as one of the most popular breakout candidates in fantasy. The 2025 second-round pick played sparingly during most of his rookie season, but flashed elite efficiency when called upon, ranking in the top five among wide receivers in catch rate (77%), yards per target (10.8), RAC (7.3) and YPRR (2.9). Burden is obviously an unproven commodity (he has two career top-20 fantasy outings, after all), but with DJ Moore no longer on the roster, he's a lock for a larger role and very well could lead Chicago in targets. He could cost a pretty penny on draft day, but Burden, 22, is a fine WR3 target with upside for more.

outlooksByWeek.2: Christian Watson will seek to build off a monster outing as the Packers travel to take on the Jets in Week 2. Watson ended a Week 1 loss to the Vikings with a dominant stat line, catching six of his eight targets for 147 yards and two touchdowns. The fifth-year wideout could be a breakout star this season, especially if Green Bay continues to deploy a pass-heavy offense. The Jets secondary, who gave up a middle-of-the-pack 26.4 PPR points to wide receivers in Week 1, looks weaker than Minnesota's as well.
outlooksByWeek.3: Christian Watson remains the top option in Green Bay's offense as they take on the Falcons in Week 3. Watson finished with a quieter four catches for 41 yards and a touchdown against the Jets in Week 2, but he did garner an impressive 11 targets. The fifth-year wideout has now scored three touchdowns on a team-high 19 targets across two games. He'll take on an Atlanta defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 30.3 PPR points per game to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Christian Watson will look to keep his touchdown streak rolling as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 4. Watson finished Week 3 against the Falcons with seven catches for 96 yards and a touchdown, putting him at a 17-284-4 receiving line on the year. The fifth-year wideout remains quarterback Jordan Love's top option at this point in the year, with him and Matthew Golden making for a dangerous duo so far. Watson will face a Tampa Bay defense that's allowed a top-ten 25.4 fantasy points per game to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.5: Christian Watson will remain a top option in Green Bay's passing game against the Bears in Week 5. Watson finished Week 4 at Tampa Bay with a quiet three catches for 47 yards, but Jordan Love threw for just 197 yards. The go-to wideout has now posted a 20-331-4 receiving line on 32 targets so far this campaign, and he's on pace for his first 1,000-yard season if he can stay healthy. Watson could have a tough task versus a Chicago defense that's ranked top five in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Christian Watson will look to continue his dominance as the Packers take on the Cowboys in Week 6. Watson recorded a stellar performance in Week 5 against the Bears, bringing in six of eight targets for 143 yards and two touchdowns. The fifth-year wideout has cemented himself as Jordan Love's top option in the passing game, with a 26-474-6 receiving line through five games. Watson will face a Dallas defense that's ranked 21st in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.7: Christian Watson will look to get back in the end zone as the Packers play the Lions in Week 7. Watson finished Week 6 against the Cowboys tying a season-low of three catches, but he was still able to convert them into 64 yards. The fifth-year wideout has now amassed 29 catches for 538 yards and six touchdowns this season. He'll face a Detroit defense that's ranked 30th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Christian Watson will aim to return to dominance as the Packers play the Panthers in Week 8. Watson brought in five of eight targets for a team-leading 57 yards in a Week 7 loss to the Lions, which was his lowest yardage total since Week 4. The wideout still has a 34-595-6 receiving line through the first seven games of the season, and he's not far off from outpacing his stat totals from the 2024 and 2025 season. Carolina has ranked a stern fifth in fantasy points allowed to WRs this campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: Watson has had quite the boom/bust NFL career and that was on full display in 2025. After missing the first seven games due to injury, Watson returned and scored 18-plus fantasy points four times, but averaged 7.7 in his other six outings. The oft-injured 2022 second-round pick has still yet to play a full regular season, but has weirdly finished with between 611 and 620 receiving yards in three of his four campaigns. Though Watson has yet to deliver a top-40 fantasy season, he's been extremely efficient in his vertical role, ranking exactly second in average depth of target, YPR and YPT each of the last two seasons. Durability is an obvious concern, but the 27-year-old could very well lead Green Bay in targets following Romeo Doubs' departure. Watson should be valued as a volatile flex option with added value in non-PPR leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jacory Croskey-Merritt found the end zone in Week 1 for Washington.  Bill served as the primary ballcarrier, toting the pigskin 16 times for 63 yards and the score. Meanwhile, fellow running back Rachaad White had seven carries for only 22 years. In Week 2, Croskey-Merritt will have a favorable matchup versus the Cowboys. Dallas allowed 165 yards rushing and one score on the ground to the Giants in the season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jacory Croskey-Merritt took 12 carries for 43 yards in Washington's loss to Dallas last game. Meanwhile, fellow running back Rachaad White took seven carries for 43 yards, while also catching six passes for 40 yards as a receiver with Washington playing from behind. Croskey-Merritt looks like the preferred back between the tackles, with White acting as the pass-catching or third-down option. The timeshare will likely continue against a devastating Seattle defense in Week 3. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. In addition, Seattle has yet to allow a rushing touchdown to the opposition, and the Commanders will be without their starting quarterback, Jayden Daniels due to injury.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jacory Croskey-Merritt was perhaps predictably stymied by the Seattle Seahawks last game. However, the touches were a silver lining, as Croskey-Merritt garnered 20 opportunities in the 33-31 win over the defending champions. Bill rushed 19 times for 36 yards, while also catching a seven-yard pass out of the backfield. However, fellow running back Rachaad White  averaged more than double Croskey-Meritt's yards per carry, while also finding the end zone through the air. However, there could be plenty of room to roam in Week 4 versus the Colts. Indianapolis has been dreadful against the run in 2026, allowing 141.3 yards per contest on he ground, which is 29th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jacory Croskey-Merritt was stymied last game in a dismal loss for the Commanders. Bill had nine carries for a season-low 15 yards in the 30-13 defeat to the Colts. Even with Rachaad White sidelined due to injury, Croskey-Merritt could find little room to roam. Bill is struggling overall this season, averaging just 2.8 yards per tote. In Week 5, Washington will face a Giants run defense that has vastly improved from a season ago. New York is allowing 109 rushing yards per tilt, which is tied for 15th in the league. In addition, the G-Men have surrendered only two rushing touchdowns through four contests.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed for a season-high 82 yards last game for the Commanders. Bill also found the end zone for the second time this season. Croskey-Merritt has seen double-digit touches in every contest thus far in 2026. In Week 6, Washington will face the San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing 97.6 rushing yards per tilt, which is 10th in the NFL. San Francisco has also given up just three rushing touchdowns through five outings, which is tied for sixth in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: One of the most hyped-up players entering the 2025 fantasy season, Croskey-Merritt didn't quite live up to lofty expectations, but he was certainly very busy for a seventh-round rookie. "Bill" played 39% of Washington's offensive snaps but, while he finished 23rd among backs in rushing yards, he wasn't much of a factor in the passing game (3% target share). Croskey-Merritt will now compete with newcomer Rachaad White in what appears to be setting up as a committee in Washington. The 25-year-old has shown to be an effective rusher (4.60 yards per carry, 2.19 YAC), but he'll need a big boost in receiving work to find his way into the RB2/flex discussion. He's worth only a late-round flier.

Hill is currently a free agent after being released by Miami. One of the top fantasy players of the past decade, Hill's best days may be behind him as he enters his age-32 campaign. The former fifth-round pick was fantasy's top-scoring receiver from 2017-23, but struggled to an 18th-place finish in 2024 (31st PPG) and then suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 4 of last season. If he's able to play in 2026, Hill may still be able to hit for the occasional explosive play, but considering his age and the major injury, his ceiling is likely that of a boom/bust flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chase Brown and the Bengals are in Houston for a Week 2 showdown versus the Texans. He rushed 16 times for 56 yards and a TD and brought in five of six targets for another 22 yards during Cincinnati's Week 1 victory over Tampa Bay. Brown is the clear-cut lead back on a high-powered offense, and he should continue to see a hefty workload on the ground and in the passing game. However, Houston's defense is tied for third in fantasy points allowed per game (10.5) to RBs, so consider this a less-than-favorable matchup.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chase Brown and the Bengals are in Pittsburgh to battle their division rivals in Week 3. He tallied 20 carries for 80 yards and corralled three of five targets for two yards during Cincinnati's Week 2 win. Brown handled 23 of 26 touches out of the backfield, and he should continue to dominate those looks again in Week 3. The Steelers' defense ranks 26th in fantasy points allowed (27.5) to RBs after giving up 136 rushing yards and 4.9 yards per carry to the Patriots in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chase Brown and the Bengals welcome the 2-1 Jaguars to town for an AFC clash in Week 4. He rushed 13 times for 61 yards and caught both his targets for eight yards during Cincinnati's 30-27 loss in Week 3. It was a quiet afternoon for Brown, with his 15 total touches well below his average of 22 accrued over his first two outings. He'll face another stout defensive unit, as Jacksonville ranks seventh in fantasy points (17.2) and fourth in rushing yards allowed (57.7) per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chase Brown and the Bengals visit the 0-4 Dolphins for a Week 5 showdown. He had nine carries for 10 yards but caught all 11 of his targets for 71 yards during Cincinnati's 22-17 loss in Week 4. Brown set a career high in receptions with Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) leaving in the first half, and with Tee Higgins (adductor) picking up a questionable tag, the running back could again get high volume through the air while still handling the bulk of carries. Miami's defense ranks last in fantasy points (29.7) and receiving TDs (4) allowed to the position, giving Brown a very favorable matchup.
outlooksByWeek.7: Chase Brown and the Bengals are on the road for a divisional clash against the Ravens in Week 7. He registered 13 carries for 39 yards and caught three of four targets for 21 yards during Cincinnati's 31-24 victory in Week 5. Brown took a backseat to Samaje Perine, who had 14 carries for 68 yards and caught both of his targets for 10 yards and a touchdown. Over his last two outings, he's rushed 22 times for 49 yards, a miserable 2.2 yards per carry. Next up is another difficult matchup against a Baltimore defense allowing 18.6 fantasy points per game (7th) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Chase Brown and the Bengals welcome the Titans to town for a Week 8 showdown. He rushed 11 times for 39 yards and caught four of five targets for 19 yards during Cincinnati's 35-13 victory in Week 7. Over his last three outings, Brown has 33 carries for 88 yards (2.7 yards per carry). He'll look to bounce back against a Tennessee defense that gave up 183 rushing yards and three total TDs to the Browns in Week 7.

player.seasonOutlook: Brown is entering his fourth NFL season and third as Cincinnati's lead back. His 2025 season got off to a rocky start (10.1 fantasy points per game and one touchdown during his first seven games), but it turned around drastically down the stretch (21.2 points per game and 10 TDs during his final 10 games). The improvement coincided with Cincinnati's improved QB play, which should continue into 2026 with a healthy Joe Burrow. Brown has yet to finish a season higher than 16th in carries or rushing yards, but he has scored exactly 11 TDs and has finished fifth in receptions in each of the past two years, both of which have resulted in top-10 fantasy campaigns. The 26-year-old once again has minimal competition for touches in a very good Bengals offense. He's best valued as a fringe RB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Keon Coleman doesn't appear to have a meaningful role in the Bills' offense entering Week 2 against the Lions. Despite playing 52% of the team's offensive snaps, Coleman drew only one target, which resulted in a one-yard catch.
