outlooksByWeek.5: Stefon Diggs led the Commanders in targets and receptions last game. With Terry McLaurin sidelined due to a hamstring issue, Diggs managed five catches on nine targets. However, he could only muster 35 yards in the dismal 30-13 loss to the Colts. Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels could return to the fold in Week 5 versus the Giants, which would certainly be a boost for Diggs, regardless of whether McLaurin also suits up. New York has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, though, allowing just 205.3 passing yards per tilt, which is 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Stefon Diggs missed Washington's last game due to a hamstring issue. In his absence, Terry McLaurin led the squad in receiving with 62 yards on four catches in the 27-27 tie with the Giants. Treylon Burks and rookie Antonio Williams would likely benefit if Diggs cannot suit up in Week 6 versus the undefeated San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing just 199.6 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just five passing touchdowns, which is tied for fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.8: Stefon Diggs will serve as the No. 1 wideout for the Commanders for the remainder of the season, as Terry McLaurin will miss the rest of the 2026 campaign due to a knee injury. Diggs has scored four times in five games played for Washington, following a return from a hamstring injury of his own. Following the bye, Washington will face division rival Philadelphia in Week 8. The reeling Eagles have been suspect in defending the pass this season.  Philadelphia is giving up 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Diggs signed with the Commanders in August after he was released by the Patriots earlier this offseason. Successful in his return from an ACL tear suffered midway through 2024, the veteran receiver's lone season in New England resulted in 85 catches (ninth among wide receivers) and his seventh career 1,000-yard campaign. Diggs paced the position with an incredible 83% catch rate (second highest all time for a receiver with 100-plus targets) and ranked fourth in yards per route run (2.8). Not used much near the goal line, however, Diggs was limited to four touchdowns and finished 23rd in fantasy PPG. He obviously still has something left in the tank, but is now 32 years old and his usage is trending downward. He has a path to a substantial offense role in Washington and can be viewed as a low-ceiling flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dak Prescott was held to just 175 passing yards in the season opener for the Cowboys.  Dak did toss two touchdowns, but he also threw a costly interception before the end of the first half, which led to a Giants touchdown. Despite a porous secondary, the Giants kept the star wideouts for the Cowboys in check, leaving Dak with an uninspiring output. Prescott will look to rebound in Week 2 versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dak Prescott tossed four touchdowns last game in a virtuoso performance for the Cowboys. Prescott completed 26-of-31 throws for 279 yards and the four scores in the dominant 37-20 win over the Commanders. Prescott has six touchdowns and just one pick through the first two games of the young season. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Dak Prescott threw for 276 yards and a touchdown in the 34-31 loss to the Ravens last game. Dak has passed for at least 275 yards through the air in each of the last two contests for the Cowboys, while also failing to toss a single interception over that span. In Week 4, the Cowboys will face a Texans defense that has been surprisingly suspect against the pass in 2026.  Houston is allowing 238.7 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Dak Prescott crossed the 300-yard passing mark last game for the Cowboys for the first time in 2026. Prescott actually threw for 335 yards in the thrilling comeback win over the Texans. More than half of the yards came via CeeDee Lamb, as the duo combined for a staggering 17 of Dak's 32 completions. Dak has eight passing scores and just one interception through four games. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in terms of yardage. The Bucs are allowing just 204.3 passing yards per tilt, which is ninth in the NFL. However, Tampa Bay has also given up seven throwing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Dak Prescott went over the 300-yard passing mark for the second-straight game for Dallas. Unfortunately, Dak threw just one touchdown pass for the second-consecutive contest, while also tossing two picks in the dismal 24-16 loss to the Bucs. Nevertheless, Dak is currently fourth in the NFL in passing yards, and tied for eighth in the league in passing touchdowns. However, in Week 6, Dallas will face a Green Bay defense allowing just 181 passing yards per contest, which is fifth in the league. Likewise, the Packers have surrendered just six passing touchdowns on the season, which is tied for 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Dak Prescott has thrown four interceptions in his last two games for the Cowboys. While Dak has also thrown for over 250 yards in five-straight outings, he has passed for one touchdown apiece in four consecutive contests. Dallas has lost three of those four games. He will look to right the ship in Week 7 versus division foe Philadelphia. The Eagles are allowing 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL. However, Philadelphia has given up just eight passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 14th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Dak Prescott tossed multiple touchdowns last game for Dallas for the first time since the middle of September. Prescott threw for 212 yards and three touchdowns in the 38-21 win over the Eagles. Prescott now has 13 touchdowns in seven starts in 2026. In Week 8, the Cowboys will face an Arizona Cardinals defense that has been prone to surrendering the touchdown pass. In fact, Arizona has given up 17 passing scores, which is dead last in the NFL. The Cardinals have also given up the most points per game in the NFL overall to date.

player.seasonOutlook: Prescott is entering his 11th NFL season following a successful 2025 campaign in which he led the NFL in completions and ranked no lower than fourth in dropbacks, pass attempts, passing yards and passing TDs. Prescott appeared in all 17 games and has now finished no worse than 11th in fantasy points during all seven seasons in which he has played at least 16 games. Last season, his nine top-10 fantasy weeks were tied for third most at the position. Prescott is no longer much of a threat with his legs, but he should continue to put up big passing numbers with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens at his disposal. The 33-year-old is a fringe QB1.

outlooksByWeek.6: Dameon Pierce was the last running back standing for the Eagles last game. Will Shipley started the game and found the end zone early for the Eagles, but did not return to the contest due to a foot injury. His status for Week 6 versus Carolina is up in the air. Pierce could start against the Panthers, as Saquon Barkley is nursing a hamstring ailment and Tank Bigsby is on Injured Reserve. Whoever lines up in the backfield could have a tasty matchup versus a suspect Panthers run defense. Carolina is allowing 156.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is second-to-last in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Dameon Pierce rushed for 35 yards and a touchdown in Saquon Barkley's place last game for the Eagles.  Pierce also caught four balls out of the backfield. If Barkley cannot suit up in Week 7 due to his balky hamstring, Pierce would be facing a Dallas defense that has allowed the most rushing yards in the NFL to date. Per game, the Cowboys are allowing a brutal 149.8 yards on the ground.
outlooksByWeek.8: Dameon Pierce still managed to maintain a solid role despite the return of Saquon Barkley from injury for the Eagles.  Barkley rushed seven times for 62 yards and a touchdown but tweaked his hamstring while also suffering a compensatory back injury. This allowed Pierce to take 14 carries for 47 yards and a touchdown of his own.  However, Pierce could be seen leaving the field late in the fourth quarter with a potential injury as well. If neither Barkley nor Pierce can play in Week 8 versus Washington, Elijah Mitchell would be the only healthy option at running back. The Commanders are allowing 100.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is 14th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Anthony Campanile's defense was one of the most surprisingly productive of 2025, finishing fifth in fantasy points, and the team was fortunate to get him back for this year. That said, the team had modest sack and fumble recovery numbers, and it did lose LB Devin Lloyd and CB Greg Newsome over the offseason. Fantasy managers can still freely select this defense, knowing it has one of the best opening-week matchups by hosting the Browns, but they'll likely need to swap them out for Weeks 2 through 6 (@DEN, NE, @CIN, PHI, HOU).

outlooksByWeek.2: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals take on the Texans, who ranked 26th in fantasy points allowed per game (41.5) to WRs in Week 2. After a two-catch, 12-yard dud in the season opener, he'll be aiming for a big bounce-back performance against a vulnerable secondary. Chase logged just four targets in Week 1 despite 35 pass attempts from Joe Burrow. The QB-WR duo should be primed for a rebound against a Houston defense that gave up 409 total yards at home last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals travel to square off against the Steelers' second-ranked pass defense in Week 3. Pittsburgh is allowing just 15.5 fantasy points per game to WRs and is one of six teams that have yet to give up a receiving TD to the position. Chase will surely put that to the test, as he's coming off a 7-75-2 receiving line on nine targets in Cincinnati's Week 2 win over Houston. Across two outings versus the division-rival Steelers in 2025, Chase registered a 19-191-1 line on 33 targets, so Joe Burrow will continue to feed his star wideout regardless of the matchup.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals host the Jaguars for a battle between 2-1 teams in Week 4. He caught nine of 12 targets for 98 yards and his third receiving touchdown of the season during Cincinnati's Week 3 defeat. Chase led the team in receptions, yardage, and targets, and it's clear that his two-catch, 12-yard outing in the season opener was a fluke. He should continue garnering a massive target share from star QB Joe Burrow against Jacksonville's 17th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (31.5) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals travel to face the winless Dolphins in Week 5. He caught all three of his targets for 27 yards in Week 4 before leaving Cincinnati's 22-17 loss with a concussion in the second quarter. Chase was evaluated for the injury after his facemask was pulled following a catch, and he'll have to clear the NFL's five-step concussion protocol before he can return to practice and play in the upcoming contest versus Miami. If he is indeed active, Chase will be going up against the Dolphins, who rank third in fewest fantasy points allowed (22.2) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals are on the road for an AFC North showdown against the Ravens in Week 7. He corralled six of 10 targets for 77 yards and a touchdown during Cincinnati's 31-24 win in Week 5. Chase cleared concussion protocol in time to pace his team in all receiving categories, as no other Bengal had more than 25 yards or four targets. He'll once again be the primary offensive threat for Joe Burrow versus the Ravens' 22nd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (34.1) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals are set to host the 1-6 Titans in Week 8. He caught five of seven targets for 62 yards and a touchdown in Cincinnati's 35-13 Week 7 victory. Tee Higgins garnered the same number of looks from Joe Burrow, but Chase turned his into six receptions for 148 yards and a score. The good news is that the concussion appears to be behind Chase, and he'll be ready to exploit a Tennessee defense tied for 24th in fantasy points allowed per game (35.8) to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Chase is fresh off yet another elite fantasy season and he's now finished four of his five NFL campaigns no lower than fifth in fantasy PPG (the exception was 11th in 2023). Chase actually saw a big dip in yardage (1,740 to 1,426), TDs (17 to 8) and fantasy PPG (23.7 to 19.6) from 2024 to 2025 (which was no surprise with Joe Burrow missing nine games), but still put up big numbers thanks to pacing the league in pass routes and targets for the second season in a row. In fact, Chase's 125 receptions make him the third receiver in NFL history with 125-plus catches in multiple seasons. The 26-year-old remains the top target in a high-scoring Bengals offense, and is one of the top players in all of fantasy.

outlooksByWeek.2: Saquon Barkley averaged 5.5 yards per tote in Week 1 for the Eagles. Barkley rushed 15 times for 83 yards, though was held out of the end zone in the 24-22 win over Washington. Barkley should have even greater success in Week 2 versus a dismal Titans squad. Tennessee allowed 367 yards from scrimmage to the Jets in their season opener. Tennessee was torched on the ground in particular, allowing 152 rushing yards and two touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Saquon Barkley missed portions of Philadelphia's last game due to a stinger, leaving his status in question for Week 3 versus the Bears. Barkley is slated to undergo an MRI to determine if he will miss any time. Saquon had five carries for just 20 yards in the 24-20 win over the Titans. Meanwhile, Tank Bigsby had 15 touches and a touchdown, while Will Shipley saw nine touches and managed 29 yards overall. Bigsby and Shipley would likely split touches if Barkley cannot go, with Bigsby getting the slight edge. The Eagles will face a Bears run defense in Week 3 allowing 122 yards per clash on the ground, which is 22nd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Saquon Barkley rushed for 82 yards last game for the Eagles. Philadelphia fell behind in the second half, though, which forced the Eagles to all but abandon the run. Barkley has yet to rush for 100 yards in a game this season. In Week 4, Barkley will face a stout defensive line with Aaron Donald when the Eagles clash with the Rams. Los Angeles is allowing 101.3 rushing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the NFL. In addition, the Rams have yielded just one rushing score through the first three games of the season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Saquon Barkley left Philadelphia's last game due to a hamstring ailment. While the injury is not considered serious, it remains to be seen whether Barkley will be able to suit up in London in Week 5 versus the Jags. If Barkley can play, he will face a stiff test, as Jacksonville is allowing just 74.3 rushing yards per tilt, which is second in the NFL. In addition, the Jags have given up just two rushing touchdowns through the first four games of the season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Saquon Barkley missed Philadelphia's last game due to a hamstring injury. His status for Week 6 versus Carolina remains up in the air. The Eagles could be on their fourth-string running back in the form of Dameon Pierce, as Tank Bigsby is on Injured Reserve and Will Shipley started last game but suffered a foot injury of his own and did not return. Whoever lines up in the backfield could have a tasty matchup versus a suspect Panthers run defense, though. Carolina is allowing 156.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is second-to-last in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Saquon Barkley has missed the last two games for the Eagles due to a hamstring ailment, leaving his status for Week 7 versus the Cowboys in jeopardy. Dameon Pierce rushed for 35 yards and a touchdown in Barkley's place, while also catching four balls out of the backfield. If Barkley can somehow suit up, he will be facing a Dallas defense that has allowed the most rushing yards in the NFL to date. Per game, the Cowboys are allowing a brutal 149.8 yards on the ground.
outlooksByWeek.8: Saquon Barkley returned from injury for the Eagles, only to tweak his hamstring while also suffering a compensatory back injury. Barkley rushed seven times for 62 yards and a touchdown, though played sparingly in the second half of the game, and ultimately could be sidelined again in Week 8 versus the Commanders. If Barkley is able to suit up, he will face a Washington defense that has been fairly stingy against the run in 2026.  The Commanders are allowing 100.5 rushing yards per clash, which is 14th in the league. In addition, Washington has allowed just five rushing touchdowns, which is tied for 11th in the league. If neither Barkley nor backup Dameon Pierce can play, Elijah Mitchell would be the only healthy option at running back.

player.seasonOutlook: Barkley is looking to rebound in his ninth NFL season (third with the Eagles) following a big step back in 2025. After producing 2,283 yards and 15 touchdowns on 378 touches in his first season with Philly, Barkley dipped to 1,413 yards and nine scores on 317 touches in 2025. Barkley fell from first among backs in fantasy points per game (22.5) to 15th (14.5). Now 29 years old, it's possible Barkley's best days are behind him, but he's still positioned as a clear feature back in a good offense that will have a healthier line and a new playcaller in Sean Mannion. Barkley is riskier than ever, but he's still worthy of mid- to back-end RB1 consideration.

outlooksByWeek.2: Drake London looks poised to bounce back from a tough Week 1 in the Falcons' Week 2 matchup against the Panthers. Carolina's defense just allowed a whopping 59 points to the Bears in Week 1, giving up 42.2 PPR fantasy points to wide receivers. London's rebound could depend on the quarterback play, as Michael Penix (knee) and Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) are both questionable for Sunday's contest. However, with Carolina's defensive struggles during Week 1, London should be in for a fantastic matchup.
outlooksByWeek.3: Drake London will look to bounce back from a slow start in the Falcons' Week 3 matchup against the Packers. London has caught just six of nine targets for 80 yards in Atlanta's first two games, as Cooper Rush and Jack Strand struggled to get the offense going. However, Michael Penix is set to return as the Falcons' QB1 during the Week 3 contest, giving London a far more optimistic projection. He's in for a favorable matchup as well, with Green Bay's defense allowing three receiving touchdowns and 34.5 PPR fantasy points per game to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Drake London will look to stay hot in the Falcons' Week 4 matchup against the Saints. With Michael Penix returning from injury in the Week 3 win over the Packers, London had one of the best performances of his career, catching nine of 10 targets for 194 yards. With Penix on the field, London has averaged 6.7 receptions, 98.7 receiving yards and 0.6 touchdowns per game, suggesting he'll remain one of fantasy's top wideouts as long as Penix remains healthy. Despite this, London is in for a tough Week 4 matchup against a Saints secondary that's given up 29.0 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Drake London is expected to remain the Falcons' top wideout in the Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. London has excelled since the return of Michael Penix in Week 3, catching 14 of 16 targets for 290 yards across his last two contests. With Penix at the helm, London has averaged a whopping 6.6 receptions and 98.5 yards per game, suggesting that he'll remain one of fantasy's top wideouts as the season progresses. Additionally, London is in for a terrific matchup against a Ravens secondary that's allowed 37.9 fantasy points per game to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Drake London will likely remain the Falcons' top pass catcher in the Week 6 matchup against the Bears. London impressed in the Week 5 loss despite not finding the end zone, totaling 118 yards on seven receptions. He's been one of fantasy's top wideouts since Michael Penix (ribs) returned in Week 3, averaging seven receptions and 136 yards per game across three contests. As long as Penix is healthy for the Week 6 contest, London should have another fantastic opportunity to put up big numbers against a Bears defense that's given up 32.0 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts.
outlooksByWeek.7: Drake London is expected to remain the Falcons' top wideout in the Week 7 matchup against the 49ers. Despite logging double-digit targets for the third time in his last four games, London recorded just four receptions and 62 yards in the Week 6 loss to the Bears. Since Michael Penix returned from injury in the Week 3 win over the Packers, London has averaged 9.3 targets, 6.3 receptions and 117.5 yards per game, making him one of fantasy's most productive receivers. Even so, London could struggle against a tough 49ers defense in Week 7 that's given up just 28.1 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts through five games this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Drake London is expected to remain one of fantasy's top wideouts in the Falcons' Week 8 matchup against the Buccaneers. London paced Atlanta's pass catchers in the Week 7 win over the 49ers, catching seven of nine targets for 66 yards and a score. Since quarterback Michael Penix returned from injury in the Week 3 win over the Packers, London has averaged a whopping 6.4 receptions and 107.2 yards per game, making him one of the league's most productive WRs. He's in for a tough matchup in Week 8, however, as Tampa Bay's secondary has allowed just 29.6 fantasy points per game to the position this season.

player.seasonOutlook: London enters his fifth NFL season with eyes on finishing in the top 15 in fantasy points per game for the third season in a row. The 2022 first-round pick broke out with a 100-1,271-9 receiving line and a fifth-place finish in fantasy points (14th PPG) in 2024. Last season, he missed five games and fell to 19th in fantasy points, but he was actually better on a per-game basis (seventh) and was the top scorer among receivers three times between Weeks 6 and 10. London remains heavily targeted (career 28% share) and sees plenty of work near the goal line (25 end zone targets over the past two seasons). As long as one of Tua Tagovailoa or Michael Penix Jr. can play somewhat competent ball, the 25-year-old London shouldn't have trouble providing fringe-WR1 fantasy production.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kyren Williams may again be part of a pretty evenly split backfield when the Rams face the Giants in Week 2. Though Williams scored Los Angeles' only touchdown in a season-opening loss to the 49ers, he had 13 fewer rushing yards on one more carry than backfield mate Blake Corum. Williams did produce more total yards thanks to logging 24 receiving yards on three catches, but Corum seems to have forced his way into a substantial backfield role after averaging over five yards per carry last year. Both backs will look to break through a Giants defense that gave up just 69 yards and 3.8 YPC against Dallas in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kyren Williams will look to get into the end zone for the Rams again in Week 3 versus Denver. Williams posted a 12-85-0 rushing line against the Giants on Monday Night Football and added a 2-12-1 line through the air. The veteran running back has scored each of the first two weeks of the campaign after racking up double-digit scores each of the past three seasons. The Broncos have struggled against the run so far in 2026, allowing the third-most rushing yards (286) to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kyren Williams is fresh off his most productive performance of the campaign heading into the Rams' Week 4 clash against Philadelphia. Williams posted season-best tallies with 15 carries for 88 yards in Week 3 against Denver, and he complemented his output on the ground with a season-high six catches for 70 yards through the air. Whereas fellow running back Blake Corum has frequently eaten into Williams' volume since last season, Corum recorded just six totes and 15 total yards against the Broncos. Corum isn't likely to exit the picture anytime soon, but Williams remains a consistent week-to-week producer. However, he could have his work cut out for him in Week 4 versus an Eagles defense that ranks 12th in the league in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kyren Williams enters the Rams' Week 5 matchup against the Bills with plenty of momentum. Williams totaled 147 yards and two touchdowns in a comeback win over Philadelphia in Week 4, pushing him up to four total TDs on the season. The star running back has logged at least 80 rushing yards in three straight games, and he's averaged 68.5 receiving yards across his past two contests. Buffalo has yielded 22.2 fantasy points per game to running backs so far, sixth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kyren Williams will take aim at the end zone again in the Rams' Week 6 matchup versus the Cardinals. Though Williams was held to 49 yards on 16 carries against Buffalo in Week 6, he added 27 yards as a receiver and scored his fifth touchdown of the season. He also continued to put plenty of space between him and No. 2 RB Blake Corum, logging 11 more totes than his backup. Williams could find ample running room against an Arizona defense that ranks 19th in the league by allowing 4.17 yards per carry to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kyren Williams remains the Rams' leading running back entering Week 7 against the Raiders, having rushed 80 times for 393 yards and four touchdowns while adding 30 receptions for 217 yards and another score. He's averaging an efficient 4.9 yards per carry, and his Week 6 showing against the Cardinals was right in line with that, as he notched 50 rushing yards in just 10 carries. Williams' receiving involvement provides a dependable fantasy foundation, particularly with Davante Adams sidelined for an extended period, and this looks like a favorable matchup on paper for the star tailback since Las Vegas has allowed the ninth-most fantasy points per game to opposing running backs in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.8: Kyren Williams will look to continue his consistent campaign when the Rams face the Chargers in Week 8. Williams posted 121 total yards Sunday against Las Vegas, marking the third time this season's he's logged over 100 total yards in a game. While his backfield mate Blake Corum has at times impacted Williams' workload, the latter has made the most of his carries, averaging a career-best 5.1 yards per rush, and he's also having his best season as a pass catcher. Williams could feast on a Chargers defense that's giving up 20.1 fantasy points per game to running backs to rank 25th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams continues to produce at a high level as the Rams' lead back. The 2022 fifth-round pick has produced 1,350-plus scrimmage yards in three straight seasons (including a career-high 1,533 in 2025), and he's one of 11 backs in NFL history who have scored 13-plus touchdowns in three of his first four seasons. Williams' carry share actually dropped quite a bit last season, but it was mostly offset by a boost in both rushing and receiving efficiency, and he still averaged a healthy 15.5 fantasy points. Williams doesn't do much as a receiver (he has never cleared 36 catches in a season), but his overall usage and scoring potential in the Rams' elite offense is enough to make the 26-year-old a solid RB2 option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Davante Adams will look to get going when the Rams face the Giants in Week 2. Adams was held to a 3-26-0 receiving line versus San Francisco in Week 1, though the Rams' offense as a whole was held in check. Adams did draw the second-most targets (six) among Los Angeles pass catchers, as he continued to draw QB Matthew Stafford's attention more than any other player besides star Puka Nacua (nine targets). The Giants largely held Dallas' passing game in check during a Week 1 win, with no Cowboys pass catcher logging more than five receptions or 44 yards.
outlooksByWeek.3: Davante Adams is coming off an explosive Monday Night Football performance heading into the Rams' Week 3 matchup versus Denver. With Puka Nacua sidelined by a hip injury, Adams starred Monday against the Giants, posting a massive 10-195-2 line. Nacua's status for Week 3 is up in the air, and Adams would logically stand to be Matthew Stafford's top target again if Nacua can't suit up. However, Denver is a tough matchup, as the Broncos have yielded just 6.55 yards per target to wideouts this season (fifth-best in the NFL).
outlooksByWeek.4: Davante Adams has looked resurgent of late ahead of the Rams' Week 4 tilt against the Eagles. With Puka Nacua (hip) sidelined the past two weeks, Adams has gone off for 15 catches, 332 yards and two touchdowns. However, Nacua has a chance to return to action against Philadelphia, which would potentially result in Adams seeing less attention from QB Matthew Stafford. With that said, both wideouts could feast against an Eagles defense that ranks in the bottom half of the league by giving up an average of 157.7 receiving yards per game to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Davante Adams is coming off a quiet performance as the Rams prepare to host the Bills in Week 5. Against Philadelphia in Week 4, Adams was held to four catches for 32 yards. That was a substantial downturn after Adams averaged 7.5 catches and 166 yards over the previous two contests, though he still got a healthy nine targets against the Eagles. It has to be mentioned that star wideout Puka Nacua returned to action in Week 4 and posted a 9-125-0 line, while Adams' big performances the previous two weeks took place in games Nacua missed due to injury. Both WRs could find success against the Bills, who have allowed the fourth-most receiving yards to wideouts this year.
outlooksByWeek.6: Davante Adams is coming off his second two-TD game of the campaign heading into the Rams' Week 6 battle versus Arizona. Against Buffalo on Monday Night Football in Week 5, Adams recorded a 5-51-2 line on seven targets. While he lagged far behind Puka Nacua's 24 targets and massive 17-138-1 line, Adams continued to work as a top option for QB Matthew Stafford in the red zone. That could come in handy again versus the Cardinals, who have surrendered a league-high 10 receiving touchdowns to wide receivers so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Davante Adams was placed on Injured Reserve due to a ruptured left hamstring in the Week 6 loss to the Cardinals and is expected to be sidelined until after the Rams' Week 11 bye in a best-case scenario. With Adams out, names such as Jordan Whittington, Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell should be in line for more targets, while established threats in the passing game like Puka Nacua, Tyler Higbee and Kyren Williams will also be in line for an uptick in numbers. Adams has 30 catches for 480 yards and four touchdonwns this season, and he will be sidelined for the time being, so he'll miss out on the chance of being productive in a favorable Week 7 matchup against a below-average Raiders defense.

player.seasonOutlook: Adams' first season in Los Angeles was a success, as the veteran led the wide receiver position in touchdowns for the third time in the past six seasons. His 27 end zone targets were nine more than any other player and he now sits second in that category (148) and in TDs from scrimmage (117) since entering the league in 2014. Adams' ninth-place finish in fantasy PPG marked his ninth top-10 in his past 10 seasons. Now 33 years old, he isn't targeted as much as in years past (24% target share in 2025 was his lowest since 2016), but he's the clear No. 2 behind Puka Nacua in the Rams' elite, Matthew Stafford-led offense. Adams' heavy usage near the goal line helps cement him as a fine fantasy WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Warren salvaged his fantasy day in the Colts' season-opening loss with a nine-yard touchdown catch in the fourth quarter, but he had only four receiving yards across the rest of the game. The 2025 first-round pick has just 213 receiving yards in his last eight games after recording 617 yards in his first 10 outings. Warren did enough in Week 1 to warrant another fantasy start in most formats for a Week 2 road game against the Chiefs, but his lack of yards since the halfway point of his rookie season is becoming a worrying trend.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tyler Warren has started his second NFL season on a two-game TD streak but has a meager 34 receiving yards on 12 targets. The Colts' 2025 first-round pick is poised to keep logging plenty of targets in Week 3 against the Texans, as Indianapolis is running out of NFL-caliber pass catchers in the absence of Alec Pierce (heel). Warren had six catches in the Week 2 loss to Kansas City, a game Pierce exited early. Given Warren's mix of talent and usage, he remains a top-10 fantasy TE in Week 3 against Houston's talented defense.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Warren has increased his catch total by three with each subsequent game this season, and he has scored in two of the Colts' three games heading into a Week 4 international game against the Commanders in London. Coming off a nine-catch game, Warren is a set-and-forget starting fantasy TE against a Washington defense that has allowed five TDs to the position through three games. The 2025 first-round pick is a key part of a Colts passing game that's missing top WR Alec Pierce (heel), who is on injured reserve.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Warren has emerged with a consistent role as a short outlet for Colts QB Daniel Jones. Warren has caught 23 of 27 targets for 130 yards and two TDs, averaging almost six catches per game but just 5.7 yards per catch. His floor is high enough to be trusted as a weekly fantasy starter at TE, as Warren leads the Colts in catches and is one target shy of Josh Downs' team-leading total. Week 5 at Pittsburgh is no exception, even though the Steelers are tied for the fourth-fewest catches allowed to TEs with 13. Two of those 13 receptions have resulted in touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tyler Warren had a season-high 83 receiving yards and a short rushing TD in the Colts' Week 5 loss to Pittsburgh. The versatile TE has been the team's second-best offensive player behind star RB Jonathan Taylor. Warren has accounted for three of the team's five non-Taylor touchdowns and leads the Colts with 30 catches through five games. Warren remains a set-and-forget fantasy starter in Week 6 due to his prominent involvement in the game plan every week, even against a Titans defense that has allowed the third-fewest receiving yards to TEs at 29 per game.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tyler Warren sat out the Colts' Week 6 loss to the Titans after being a late addition to the injury report due to a groin injury. If the 2025 first-round pick is cleared to return in Week 7 against the Vikings, he would reclaim his role as a key cog on offense for the Colts and a borderline top-five fantasy TE. Jonathan Taylor has seven of the Colts' 13 offensive TDs this season, and Warren has scored three of the other six while averaging six receptions per game. Minnesota hasn't allowed a TE to score this season while giving up 44 receiving yards per game to the position.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tyler Warren hasn't suited up since Week 5 due to a groin injury. He leads the Colts with 30 catches despite missing the past two games, so Warren would immediately return to the fantasy starting range if he gains clearance to return in Week 8 against a Jaguars defense that has been much more vulnerable through the air than on the ground. Jacksonville is holding TEs to 35 yards per game but has allowed the position to score four times in six outings, and Warren has accounted for three of the six TDs scored by Colts other than Jonathan Taylor.

player.seasonOutlook: Warren put together a solid rookie season, but it could've been even better. In 12 games with a healthy Daniel Jones, Warren scored five touchdowns and averaged 13.1 fantasy PPG. In five games without Jones, Warren fell to 6.3 PPG and failed to find the end zone. In fact, the 2025 first-round pick was unlucky in the scoring department, ranking fifth among tight ends in end zone targets (seven) and expected TDs (7.5). Warren finished the season third among tight ends in targets and also had three goal-line carries. The 24-year-old was already a featured target and might see even more work with Michael Pittman Jr. shipped to Pittsburgh. Warren is a quality TE1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Drake Maye will hope to clean up mistakes when the Patriots host the Steelers in Week 2. Maye threw three interceptions in the season opener while under constant pressure, and Pittsburgh's defense, led by T.J. Watt, recorded four sacks last week. While the chemistry was still developing, Maye is now also without No. 1 WR A.J. Brown (ankle) for the immediate future, leading to questionable receiving options. While Maye remains a dangerous runner that will keep his floor reasonable, this likely low-scoring game may not be ideal for a true bounce-back performance.
outlooksByWeek.3: Drake Maye will look to get on track when the Patriots face the Jaguars in Week 3. He is averaging just 183 passing yards through two weeks, with only one touchdown pass and four interceptions. Maye was picked off just eight times all last season. Opponents seem to be pressuring Maye, though Jacksonville is middling at getting after the passer. However, they've allowed only two touchdown passes while limiting quarterbacks to 44 rushing yards. With A.J. Brown still sidelined, Maye will be challenged to exhibit his 2025 form.
outlooksByWeek.4: Drake Maye's confidence appears shaken in the face of pressure ahead of the Patriots' Week 4 matchup with the Bills. Maye has a 1:6 TD:INT ratio through three games, completing just 14 passes in each of his last two games while posting a season-high of 208 yards in Week 2. While he remains dangerous with his legs, he's been held to 18 yards or fewer in Weeks 2 and 3. Buffalo's defense is allowing the seventh-most fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks, giving up seven touchdowns with just one interception. The game could be high-scoring or at least force the Patriots to try and match points, but Maye didn't throw a touchdown pass against this unit a year ago.
outlooksByWeek.5: Drake Maye will look to carry momentum in Week 5 when the Patriots face the Raiders. After a dismal 1:6 TD:INT ratio through three games, Maye provided a season-high 269 yards and three touchdowns while adding 54 yards on eight rushes in Week 4 against Buffalo. Las Vegas is surrendering a 7:4 TD:INT ratio through four games, with six of those touchdowns coming in the last two weeks, suggesting Maye can provide the 2025 version expected by his fantasy managers in Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.6: Drake Maye will look to extend his hot streak to three games in Week 6 when the Patriots face the Jets. After a terrible start to his season (one touchdown, six interceptions), Maye has produced eight touchdowns and one interception over the last two weeks. The Jets are statistically stout against the pass, allowing the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks (195.4 yards per game), but it's come against the likes of Cam Ward, Deshaun Watson, and the Bears' backups. Maye averaged 268.5 yards and threw six touchdown passes in two games against the Jets last season, suggesting his surge can continue in Week 6.
outlooksByWeek.7: Drake Maye hopes to extend his hot streak to four games when the Patriots face the Bears in Week 7. After throwing just one touchdown in his first three games, Maye has burst out with 10 touchdown passes and a scoring rush over his last three games. He now has his full complement of receivers with A.J. Brown returning from an ankle injury. Chicago has allowed two 300-yard passers and multiple touchdown passes three times to date, giving Maye an opportunity to continue his current form Thursday night.
outlooksByWeek.8: Drake Maye's recent surge should continue when the Patriots face the Dolphins in Week 8. In Week 7, he topped 300 passing yards for the second time in three weeks and also added a rushing touchdown for the second time in three games, bringing his total to 14 touchdowns over his last four games. Miami's secondary has been decimated by opposing signal-callers, allowing seven touchdown passes in the last two weeks, multiple touchdown passes in five of six games, and the third-worst yards per attempt at 8.1. This firmly entrenches Maye in Week 8 lineups.

player.seasonOutlook: Maye is entering his third NFL season and second full season as New England's starter. The 2024 No. 3 draft pick is fresh off a breakout 2025 campaign in which he finished in the top five among quarterbacks in pass completions, yards and TDs, as well as rush attempts and yards. Maye, who led the league in completion percentage (72%) and yards per attempt (8.9), trailed only Josh Allen in fantasy points (351.9), fantasy points per game (20.7) and top-10 fantasy weeks (10). The NFL MVP runner-up will need to overcome a tougher schedule, but he has a better supporting cast (including A.J. Brown) and the 24-year-old's combination of passing talent and rushing ability have him well positioned for another top-five fantasy campaign.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tony Pollard got just eight touches in the season opener as the Titans fell behind against the Jets and abandoned the run. Negative game scripts could be a recurring problem for Pollard, and the Titans will be substantial Week 2 underdogs at home against the Eagles. On the bright side, Pollard recorded at least 1,288 scrimmage yards in each of the previous two seasons, even as the Titans posted a 3-14 record both years. Pollard's status as the team's starting running back keeps him in the Week 2 flex/RB3 conversation.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tony Pollard could be worth plugging into Week 3 fantasy lineups as a high-end RB3/flex option for the Titans' road matchup with a Giants defense that has struggled to contain RBs in the early going. Javonte Williams scored two TDs against the Giants in Week 1, then Kyren Williams and Blake Corum each exceeded 90 scrimmage yards against the Giants in Week 2, with Williams tacking on a TD. Pollard has reprised his role as the 1A option in Tennessee's backfield over Tjyae Spears. The former Cowboys RB has averaged 77 scrimmage yards per game since joining the Titans prior to the 2024 campaign, but Pollard has been limited to 99 yards through two games to begin this season. Negative game scripts are often a problem for the Titans, but Tennessee is likely to stay within striking distance and keep Pollard involved on the ground against a Giants team that's missing starting QB Jaxson Dart (knee).
outlooksByWeek.4: Tony Pollard has increased his yardage total in each of Tennessee's first three games heading into a Week 4 road game against the Ravens, who are allowing 99 scrimmage yards per game to RBs. Pollard had just 34 scrimmage yards on eight touches in a lopsided Week 1 loss to the Jets, but he recorded 65 yards on 15 touches in Week 2 and 96 scrimmage yards on 21 touches in Week 3 as the Titans managed to stay within striking distance before falling to the Eagles and Giants, respectively. With second-year QB Cam Ward struggling to move the ball through the air, the Titans will likely try to continue featuring their Pollard-led ground game, though there is a substantial risk of Lamar Jackson and the Ravens pulling away and forcing Tennessee into a more pass-heavy game plan. Given Pollard's status as the lead back in a low-octane offense, he has a decent floor as a flex play but isn't the most exciting Week 4 RB option.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tony Pollard is averaging 61 scrimmage yards per game and scored his first touchdown of the season in Week 4 against the Ravens, though that wasn't enough to keep the Titans from dropping to 0-4. In Week 5, Tennessee hosts the AFC South rival Texans, who are also 0-4. The Titans should manage to stay within striking distance and give Pollard his full workload on the ground, though Houston has held RBs to just 91 scrimmage yards per game. Pollard is a high-floor, low-ceiling flex play as usual for Week 5 given his role as the lead back in a struggling Titans offense that's averaging the fewest yards and second-fewest points per game.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tony Pollard remains a viable flex option in Week 6 against the Colts thanks to his high touch floor as the starting RB in a putrid Titans offense. Pollard has at least 14 touches and 50 scrimmage yards in all but one game this season but has been limited to one TD on a Titans offense that has found the end zone just six times through five games. Indianapolis is giving up 100 rushing yards per game to RBs as well as a league-high 53 receiving yards per game to the position, so Pollard has a higher ceiling than usual in this Week 6 matchup to go with his steady floor.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tony Pollard has at least 14 touches and 50 scrimmage yards in each of the Titans' last five games. He's locked into a high touch floor in any game the 1-5 Titans can keep within striking distance, and Tennessee is unlikely to fall too far behind in Week 7 at home against the Browns, who are scoring just 17.7 points per game, tied for fourth-fewest in the NFL. Cleveland has started 4-2 thanks to a stout defense that's allowing 20.3 points per game and has allowed just one TD to a running back all season, but Pollard's hefty usage keeps him locked in as a viable flex play for Week 7, even though he looks unlikely to add to his season total of one TD in a Titans offense that's tied for the worst in the league at 14.0 points per game.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tony Pollard is coming off his best game of the season, as he racked up 129 rushing yards and three TDs against the Browns in Tennessee's Week 7 loss. The veteran RB is the most consistent offensive player on the Titans, having racked up at least 14 touches and 50 scrimmage yards in six consecutive games. His solid touch floor makes Pollard a passable fantasy RB2 for Week 8, but don't expect a repeat of his Week 7 outburst against a Bengals defense that has limited RBs to three total TDs in six games.

player.seasonOutlook: Pollard has handled a hefty 67.2% of the Titans' designed rushing attempts since his arrival two seasons ago (15.2 per game) and, even with solid efficiency, he has finished 22nd and 30th in fantasy points per game. The culprits? Tennessee's struggling offense (Pollard has exactly five TDs in both seasons) and a limited receiving role when Tyjae Spears has been healthy (Pollard's targets fell from 3.5 per game in 2024 to 2.5 per game in 2025). Barring a major leap from quarterback Cam Ward, Pollard is unlikely to deliver only the second top-20 fantasy campaign (in points per game) of his career. The 29-year-old, entering his eighth NFL season (third with Tennessee), is a low-ceiling flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chuba Hubbard is expected to continue leading the Panthers' backfield in the Week 2 matchup against the Falcons. Hubbard out-touched Jonathon Brooks 13 to five in the Week 1 loss, which is a good sign for his fantasy outlook going forward. Hubbard also found the end zone twice and looked very efficient, averaging 6.7 yards per touch. He's in for a tougher Week 2 matchup, however, as Atlanta allowed just 16.4 PPR fantasy points to the running back position last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain the Panthers' top running back in the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Hubbard appears to have returned to his 2024 form over Carolina's first two games this season, rushing for 102 yards (4.6 yards per carry) and a touchdown while catching all five of his targets for 49 yards and a score. Additionally, with Jonathon Brooks (groin) exiting the Week 2 win in the fourth quarter, Hubbard's role could continue growing. He faces a difficult matchup, however, as the Browns' defense has given up just 16.9 PPR fantasy points per game through two weeks.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain the Panthers' lead back in the Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Without Jonathon Brooks (groin) in the Week 3 loss, Hubbard accounted for 82.1 percent of the Panthers' running back touches (23 to AJ Dillon's five). Despite Carolina throwing the ball over 40 times per game this season, Hubbard has remained one of fantasy's most productive backs, averaging 16.7 opportunities and 17.7 PPR points per game. He's likely to remain the bell-cow in Carolina's Week 4 matchup against a Lions defense that's allowed 19.7 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain productive in the Panthers' Week 6 matchup against the Eagles. Hubbard is coming off one of the best games of his career in the Week 4 win over the Lions, totaling 129 yards and two touchdowns on 21 touches. He's been a true work-horse running back for the Panthers since Jonathon Brooks' (groin) injury, playing 84% of Carolina's snaps in Weeks 3 and 4. Expect Hubbard to continue producing in the Week 6 matchup against an Eagles defense that's given up 20.8 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain the Panthers' lead back in the Week 7 matchup against the Buccaneers. Hubbard has been extremely productive for Carolina over its last three games, averaging 120 yards and a touchdown per game on 73 total touches. While Jonathon Brooks (groin) remains on the injured reserve list, Hubbard is expected to continue taking the vast majority of work in the Panthers' backfield. Despite this, he's in for a tough Week 7 matchup against a Buccaneers defense that's allowed just 17.4 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain the Panthers' lead back in the Week 8 matchup against the Packers. Hubbard had his worst performance of the season in the Week 7 loss to the Buccaneers, accumulating just 60 yards on 11 touches. Across six contests this season, Hubbard has amassed 459 rushing yards, 112 receiving yards and six total touchdown, the 19th-most total yards in the NFL. He'll have a good opportunity to rebound in Week 8 against a Packers defense that's allowed 25.8 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Hubbard is coming off a disappointing 2025 campaign in which he battled injury and lost lead-back duties to Rico Dowdle. The veteran was limited to 734 yards on 164 touches (he cleared 275 touches and 1,100 yards in 2023 and 2024), and he ranked 64th among 65 qualified backs in forced missed tackle rate and elusive rating, per PFF. Still in his prime at age 27, a bounce-back season is possible, especially with Dowdle gone and unproven Jonathon Brooks as his competition for touches. Hubbard should be considered a flex/bench option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Godwin is expected to remain one of the Buccaneers' top receiving options in the Week 2 matchup against the Browns. The 30-year-old was Tampa Bay's second-most productive wideout in the Week 1 loss, hauling in all four of his targets for 40 yards. Godwin likely won't have many big plays after sustaining multiple serious lower-body injuries throughout his career, but he should remain a reliable PPR option and an important part of the Buccaneers' offense moving forward. Additionally, he's in for a great Week 2 matchup, as the Browns defense allowed 13.6 yards per target to WRs in Week 1, the second-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chris Godwin will look to bounce back from a slow start in the Buccaneers' Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. Godwin leads Tampa Bay's receiving corps in offensive snaps played (101) and has caught all seven of his targets through two weeks. However, this hasn't translated to much production, as he's accumulated just 86 receiving yards. Expect Godwin to remain one of the Buccaneers' most reliable targets in a difficult matchup against a Vikings defense that's given up just 27 receptions to wideouts through two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chris Godwin is expected to remain one of the Buccaneers' most reliable targets in the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. Godwin had a quiet Week 3 performance (3-25-0), though he had an 85-yard touchdown reception called back for holding. The veteran wideout has struggled along with the rest of Tampa Bay's offense, and those struggles could be amplified with Baker Mayfield (thumb) sidelined for the Week 4 contest. However, Godwin is in for a favorable matchup against a Packers defense that's allowed 6.7 yards per pass attempt this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chris Godwin is expected to remain one of the Buccaneers' top weapons in the Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. Godwin was targeted a season-high seven times in the Week 4 loss to the Packers, catching six of them for just 31 yards. The veteran wideout may actually benefit from Jalon Daniels acting as Tampa Bay's starting quarterback while Baker Mayfield (thumb) is sidelined, as Godwin could act as the rookie's safety blanket. Additionally, Godwin is in for a good Week 5 matchup against a Dallas defense that's allowed five receiving touchdowns to WRs through four contests this year.
outlooksByWeek.6: Chris Godwin is expected to remain Tampa Bay's top safety blanket in the Week 6 matchup against the Steelers. Godwin has caught 19 of 22 targets this season, totaling 179 yards. Despite ranking second on the Buccaneers in receptions and third in targets, he's gotten just one red-zone target all season and could struggle finding fantasy relevance without a touchdown. Regardless, Godwin is in for a tough Week 6 matchup against a Steelers defense that's given up 220.8 passing yards per game this year.
outlooksByWeek.7: Chris Godwin is expected to remain one of the Buccaneers' top receiving options in the Week 7 matchup against the Panthers. Godwin was targeted a season-high eight times during the Week 6 loss to the Steelers, recording four receptions for 37 yards. The veteran wideout ranks second on Tampa Bay in targets (30), receptions (23) and yards (216) through the first six games and could benefit from the potential return of Baker Mayfield (thumb) in Week 7. However, Godwin is in for a tough matchup against a Panthers secondary that's allowed just 5.9 yards per pass attempt this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Chris Godwin is expected to remain one of Tampa Bay's top wideouts in the Week 8 matchup against the Falcons. Godwin was the Buccaneers' second-leading receiver in the Week 7 win over the Panthers, catching four of five targets for 27 yards. After Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) was sidelined last week, Godwin now leads Tampa Bay in receiving yards (243) through seven games. Godwin could remain successful in Week 8 against a Falcons defense that's allowed 8.0 yards per target to opposing wideouts this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Godwin is on the comeback trail after injuries have limited him to 16 games during the past two seasons. In 2025, he appeared in nine games and reached 11 fantasy points only twice. It seems like a long time ago, Godwin was second among receivers in fantasy points in 2024 when he suffered a severe ankle injury. He wasn't nearly as effective when he was on the field last season, but he's now more than a full year recovered from the injury and has less target competition with Mike Evans no longer on the roster. Entering his age-30 season, Godwin's days as a fantasy WR1 may be over, but with Emeka Egbuka as his only competition to lead the team in targets, he certainly has a path to flex numbers.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rachaad White found himself on the losing end of the timeshare out of the backfield in Week 1 for Washington.  White had seven carries for 22 yards, while fellow rusher Jacory Croskey-Merritt managed 16 carries for 63 yards and a touchdown. White only had one more reception than Croskey-Merritt as well. In Week 2, Washington has a favorable matchup with the Cowboys, as Dallas allowed 165 rushing yards on the ground to the Giants in their season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rachaad White recorded 13 touches for 83 yards out of the backfield last game for the Commanders. White took seven carries for 43 yards, while also catching six passes for 40 yards as a receiver with Washington playing from behind. White remains in a timeshare for touches with Jacory Croskey-Merritt, though, and will face a devastating Seattle defense in Week 3.  The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points and 214 yards per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league in both categories.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rachaad White found the end zone last game for Washington. White caught a six-yard touchdown pass from backup quarterback Marcus Mariota during the stunning 33-31 win over the Seahawks. White also doubled up starting running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt in terms of yards per carry. However, Bill out-touched White by a margin of 20-9 for the game. Nevertheless, both backs should remain involved in Week 4 versus a suspect Colts defense. Indianapolis is allowing the most yards per game in the NFL through three contests.
outlooksByWeek.5: Rachaad White missed Washington's last game due to a shoulder issue, leaving his status in question for Week 5 versus the Giants. An argument can be made that White has been more productive than fellow rusher Jacory Croskey-Merritt in 2026, though that point may be moot as long as White is sidelined. Austin Ekeler will be the backup to Bill if White remains shelved. In Week 5, Washington will face a Giants run defense that has vastly improved from a season ago. New York is allowing 109 rushing yards per tilt, which is tied for 15th in the league. In addition, the G-Men have surrendered only two rushing touchdowns through four contests.
outlooksByWeek.6: Rachaad White returned to the lineup for Washington following a one-game absence due to a shoulder issue. However, White failed to have much of an impact. He rushed seven times for just 18 yards, while also catching a two-yard pass out of the backfield. Meanwhile, starting running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed for 82 yards and a touchdown. In Week 6, the Commanders face a 49ers defense that has been rather stingy against the run. The Niners are allowing 97.6 rushing yards per clash, which is 10th in the league. In addition, San Fran has surrendered just three rushing scores to date, which is tied for sixth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.8: Rachaad White will serve as the No. 1 running back for the Commanders in Week 8, as starter Jacory Croskey-Merritt was placed on Injured Reserve with a groin injury. White has found the end zone in two of the last three games as a receiver out of the backfield, but is averaging just 4.0 yards per carry as a rusher. Still, the expanded role should give him double-digit touches against a floundering Eagles defense. Philadelphia is allowing 119.3 rushing yards per clash, which is 21st in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: White signed with the Commanders after spending his first four seasons with the Buccaneers. The 2022 third-round pick operated as a feature back in 2023 (he finished in the top five among backs in touches, yards and fantasy points), but he played a situational role during his other three seasons. White is fine as a rusher, but he's a standout as a receiver. He's the only back in the NFL with 40-plus catches in each of the past four seasons, and his 89.1% career catch rate is easily best in NFL history among players with 100-plus targets. The 27-year-old is the favorite to lead the Washington backfield, but Jacory Croskey-Merritt and perhaps others will be involved. White will find himself on the weekly flex radar as long as he remains atop the depth chart.

The No. 1 D/ST selected on average last season, the Steelers finished a disappointing 14th in fantasy points and scored fewer than five points in 8-of-17 games. They've since overhauled their coaching staff, with Mike McCarthy replacing Mike Tomlin, and Patrick Graham as defensive coordinator, the same role he held with the Raiders from 2022-25. The offseason additions of S Jaquan Brisker and CB Jamel Dean should bolster this unit, and it benefits greatly from one of the softest September and October schedules in the league. Get this D/ST early, but be prepared to seek a replacement after that point.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kyler Murray's status is up in the air as the Vikings travel to Chicago in Week 2. Murray went down early in Week 1 against the Packers after taking a hard hit to the head. Before his exit, Murray completed three of five passes for 18 yards and one interception, tacking on two rushes for nine yards on the ground. The veteran is now under evaluation for a concussion, which could very likely keep him sidelined for an extended period. Backup quarterback Carson Wentz delivered the win for Minnesota, and he's set to assume QB duties once again. The Bears gave up 361 passing yards, three touchdowns and one interception to Bryce Young in Week 1, so big output could definitely be in the cards for whoever lines up under center for the Vikings.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kyler Murray will return to the field as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Murray has cleared concussion protocol after suffering a nasty hit early in Week 1. The veteran quarterback will finally get the chance to prove himself, especially given that he completed just three of five passes for 18 yards and one interception before his opening-game departure. He'll face a Bucs defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 20.4 fantasy points per game to QBs across its first two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kyler Murray will aim to build on a serviceable performance as the Vikings play the Dolphins in Week 4. Murray returned to the field in Week 3 versus the Buccaneers, completing 15 of 29 passes for 168 yards with a 1:1 TD:INT ratio, along with rushing the ball twice for 17 yards. The veteran quarterback also lost star wideout Justin Jefferson in the first half, so his final output and delivery of a win were more impressive. Miami has been much more favorable against quarterbacks than Tampa so far this season, allowing the seventh-most fantasy points per game (23.7) to the position.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kyler Murray will look to do more as the Vikings travel to New Orleans in Week 5. In his second full start of the year, Murray completed 27 of 37 passes for 247 yards, but he was unable to find the end zone. The veteran quarterback also now holds a 1:2 TD:INT through his three appearances this season, so he'll need to do more for Minnesota to lock him down as a long-term option. The Saints have ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kyler Murray will look to keep the Vikings rolling in Week 7 against the Colts. Murray recorded his best game of the season against the Saints heading into Minnesota's bye, completing 80 percent of passes for 229 yards and a touchdown, with 10 rushes for 51 yards. The veteran quarterback could be a dangerous threat moving forward, especially if he can get it going on the ground once again. He'll face an Indy defense that's ranked 21st in fantasy points allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Kyler Murray will look to do more as the Vikings play the Lions in Week 8. Murray completed 14 of 24 passes for 150 yards and a touchdown, with five carries for 39 yards in a Week 7 win over the Colts. The veteran has yet to lose a game this year, but his output has been quite low compared to that of usual winning quarterbacks. He'll luckily face a Detroit defense that's allowed the most fantasy points per game to QBs so far this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Murray signed with the Vikings after spending his first seven seasons with the Cardinals. The change comes after a disappointing and injury-shortened 2025 season in which he failed to clear 18.3 fantasy points in any of his five appearances. Murray has settled in as an accurate but conservative passer and continues to add value with his legs (78-572-5 in 17 games in 2024). Prior to the 2025 dud, Murray had finished each of his first six NFL seasons as a top-12 fantasy QB (points per game). Now that he beat out J.J. McCarthy for Minnesota's starting job, he'll have the luxury of working with Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison and T.J. Hockenson. Add that to his rushing ability, and the 29-year-old certainly could find his way into the weekly QB1 mix. Consider Murray in the middle to late rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: Matt Gay was perfect in his Raiders debut, converting field goals from 30 and 47 yards and all three extra points in a season-opening win over the Dolphins. A rebuilding opponent certainly provided Gay with extra opportunities, but the Las Vegas offense could also be better than expected. New head coach Klint Kubiak and an improved quarterback situation, with Kirk Cousins steadying the ship until rookie Fernando Mendoza is ready, should help. The pending return of Brock Bowers will also help generate more scoring drives. Gay may not be able to squander any chances in Week 2 against a Chargers team that ranked ninth in points per game allowed in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Matt Gay has been busy to begin his Raiders' career, converting all three of his field-goal attempts and all six of his extra points through the first two games of the season. The outlook for the offense should improve once Brock Bowers is cleared for his 2026 debut, and while there's additional uncertainly on the horizon once first overall pick Fernando Mendoza is deemed ready to replace Kirk Cousins under center, Gay could actually benefit if the young QB struggles to get the ball into the end zone while he figures out NFL defenses. Gay will face a Saints team in Week 3 that's allowed an exact mirror to his production so far, with opposition kickers getting three FGs and six PATs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Matt Gay has been both busy and perfect for the surprising 3-0 Raiders, connecting on all six of his field goal attempts and all eight of his PATs. The veteran kicker was also successful on his only attempt from 50-plus yards, as he looks to boot at least three long-range FGs for a sixth straight season. Gay has also benefited from a favorable early schedule, as all three of Las Vegas' games so far have been played indoors. The team will get a fourth straight game under a roof in a Week 4 home tilt against Kansas City, but Gay likely won't be able to afford to squander any opportunities versus an opponent that has given up just 16.7 points per game, tied for third in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Matt Gay continues to benefit from the Raiders' surprisingly strong start to the season on offense with Kirk Cousins under center. In a Week 4 loss to Kansas City, Gay was a perfect 4-for-4 on FG tries while also converting his only PAT. The veteran has yet to miss an attempt in 2026, going 10-for-10 on FGs and 9-for-9 on extra points, putting him third in the NFL in kicker scoring behind the Vikings' Will Reichard and the Colts' Spencer Shrader. Gay likely won't be able to afford to start squandering opportunities in Week 5 against a Patriots team that's allowed 19.3 points per game so far, tied for sixth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Matt Gay missed his first kick of the season in the Raiders' Week 5 loss to the Patriots, pinging the upright on a field goal attempt from 48 yards out. He's still having a strong season, converting all 11 of his PATs and going 11-for-12 on FG attempts, including his only attempt from 50-plus yards. Gay has benefited from a surprisingly potent offense under Kirk Cousins, but the veteran QB may be reverting to his usual level, perhaps opening the door for first overall pick Fernando Mendoza to take the reins, so it's not necessarily bad news for Gay's long-term outlook. Gay will take on a Bills team in Week 6 that's allowing 28.2 points per game, 28th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Matt Gay stayed busy in the Raiders' Week 6 loss to the Bills, going a perfect 3-for-3 on both field goal attempts and extra points. The veteran kicker has benefited from the team's offensive resurgence under new head coach Klint Kubiak, and Gay sits third in scoring in the NFL behind the Colts' Spencer Shrader and the Bills' Tyler Bass. Gay will face a Rams team in Week 7 that's allowed 23.0 points per game, tied for 17th in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: T.J. Hockenson will look to build off a solid Week 1 performance as the Vikings travel to Chicago in Week 2. Hockenson was second in targets against the Packers behind Justin Jefferson, reeling in four of five targets for 36 yards and a touchdown. The veteran tight end was a go-to outlet for veteran Carson Wentz, and he could continue to be one no matter who lines up under center moving forward. He'll take on a Bears defense that allowed a middle-of-the-pack 11.5 PPR points to Carolina tight ends in a high-scoring season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: T.J. Hockenson will look to stay involved as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Hockenson saw his volume go down a bit in Week 2 against the Bears, reeling in just three catches for 29 yards. The starting tight end looks like he'll be a touchdown-dependent fantasy option. With that being said, Kyler Murray is slated to start Sunday, and he's been known to rely on his tight ends in the past. The Bucs have allowed 22.1 PPR points per game to TEs so far this season, 31st in the lerague.
outlooksByWeek.4: T.J. Hockenson remains a secondary option in Minnesota's passing game heading into Week 4 against the Dolphins. Other than a 4-36-1 receiving line in Week 1, Hockenson has looked otherwise like a disappointment this season. The veteran tight end has stayed consistent with four targets in back-to-back games, but he's converted them into a combined five catches for 40 yards in the stretch. Miami has allowed the fourth-most fantasy points per game to tight ends (16), but even then, Hock will likely need to find the end zone to have relevance beyond a depth option.
outlooksByWeek.5: T.J. Hockenson will look to build on a huge performance as the Vikings play New Orleans in Week 5. Hockenson finished Week 4 with a bang after starting the season quietly, catching all 13 of his targets for a whopping 119 yards. The veteran tight end could continue to be an outlet for quarterback Kyler Murray, especially with some struggles from the quarterback so far. The Saints have ranked bottom five against fantasy TEs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: T.J. Hockenson holds a questionable tag heading into Minnesota's Week 7 matchup against the Colts. Hockenson sustained a concussion in the Vikings' Week 5 win over the Saints heading into the bye, so his status is up in the air just two weeks later. The veteran tight end will need to clear protocol if he hopes to get back on the field, and that'll be evident through his practice availability. Indianapolis has ranked in the middle against fantasy TEs so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.8: T.J. Hockenson remains a top option in Minnesota's passing game heading into Week 8 against the Lions. Hockenson found the end zone for the second time of the season in a Week 7 win over the Colts, and he complemented his score with four catches for 35 yards. The veteran tight end has now brought in 27 catches for 237 yards and two touchdowns this season. He enters a favorable matchup versus a Detroit defense that's ranked 32nd in fantasy points allowed to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: It's been a rough go for Hockenson since he peaked with a 95-960-5 receiving line in 2023. He tore an ACL in Week 16 that season and was limited to a 41-455-0 receiving line upon his return in 10 games in 2024. A bounce-back was expected in 2025, but Hockenson handled a weak 16% target share (his lowest since he was a rookie in 2019) and couldn't overcome the team's QB woes en route to a 51-438-3 showing. Hockenson has now followed four straight top-seven fantasy PPG seasons with finishes of 17th and 26th. The 29-year-old could very well get back on track in 2026, but he'll need solid play from Kyler Murray. Hockenson is a fringe TE1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Keenan Allen can still get open on short passes, but the 34-year-old WR's lack of big-play potential limits his fantasy relevance to deeper formats heading into the Colts' Week 2 road game against the Chiefs. Allen caught all six of his targets in his Colts debut, leading the team in receptions, but he totaled just 32 receiving yards. Expect him to post plenty of similar stat lines this season after averaging a career-low 9.6 yards per catch with the Chargers last year.
outlooksByWeek.3: Keenan Allen should get plenty of playing time in Week 3 against the Texans with the Colts' banged-up WR room, but the 34-year-old wideout may not have enough gas in the tank to make much of the opportunity. Allen has exceeded 44 yards just once and failed to score a TD in his last 12 games. Despite that lack of recent production, he's a viable deep-league dart throw, as Indianapolis will be without Alec Pierce (heel) and possibly Ashton Dulin (ankle), leaving Allen as the top option for snaps at WR alongside Josh Downs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Keenan Allen turned back the clock in the Colts' Week 3 win over the Texans, catching six of nine targets for 63 yards and his first TD since Week 7 of the previous season. The 34-year-old WR is poised to maintain an expanded role in Week 4 against Washington's weak secondary as the Colts continue to play without starting WR Alec Pierce (heel), who is on IR. A repeat effort may be too much to ask from Allen, who averaged just 32 yards per game during his 12-game touchdown drought, but he's a viable flex option considering the Commanders have allowed league-high totals in catches and touchdowns to WRs, with 46 and six, respectively.
outlooksByWeek.5: Keenan Allen missed the Colts' Week 4 win over the Commanders due to a groin injury. If the 34-year-old WR is cleared to return in Week 5, he could play a prominent role opposite Josh Downs in a Colts WR room that remains without Alec Pierce (heel), who is on IR. Concerns about Allen's injury and performance limit his viability to deeper formats, even against a Steelers secondary that's giving up 149 receiving yards per game to wide receivers. Allen snapped a 12-game touchdown drought in the Colts' Week 3 win over Houston.
outlooksByWeek.6: Keenan Allen has caught 11 of 18 targets for 108 yards and a TD in his last two outings for the Colts, sandwiched around a Week 4 absence due to a groin injury. The 34-year-old wideout has stepped up in the absence of WR Alec Pierce (heel), who remains on injured reserve ahead of a Week 6 home game against the Titans. Allen lacks Pierce's ability to stretch the field, but a steady diet of short targets should put Allen back into the flex mix in Week 6 against a Titans defense that ranks among the 10 most generous units in terms of catches and yards allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Keenan Allen has turned back the clock over his past three appearances for the Colts, securing 19 of 29 targets for 190 yards and a TD over that span while drawing at least nine targets in every game. The 34-year-old wideout should continue to fill a high-volume role in a Colts WR room that lacks appealing alternatives in the continued absence of Alec Pierce (heel). Allen is a high-floor fantasy WR3 in Week 7 against the Vikings, who are allowing 10 catches for 133 yards per game to WRs. Minnesota's aggressive blitz packages will likely force the Colts into plenty of the quick and short throws on which Allen thrives.
outlooksByWeek.8: Keenan Allen is averaging over seven targets per game and has operated as the Colts' co-No. 1 WR alongside Josh Downs since Alec Pierce went down with a heel injury. Pierce remains on injured reserve ahead of a Week 8 trip to Jacksonville. Allen will be a high-floor flex candidate against a Jaguars defense that's giving up a league-high 210 yards per game to wide receivers. He's averaging 55 receiving yards per game over the past four and has scored one TD this season.
